Month 1-2: Complete NCERT History (Class 6-12) with supplementary reading on Satavahana, Eastern Chalukya, and Vijayanagara for AP-specific content. Read Laxmikanth for polity and start daily current affairs from Eenadu, Deccan Chronicle, or The Hindu with AP-specific focus.

Month 3-4: Deep-dive into Indian and AP Geography (physical and economic, especially Godavari-Krishna river basin, Vizag industrial belt, Rayalaseema geography) and Economy (Indian and AP, including Polavaram, agriculture, and industry). Start Telugu Paper IV preparation in parallel; aim for 1 hour per day on Telugu essay and grammar. Write 3 answers per week on GS topics.

Month 5-6: Solve APPSC Group 2 previous year papers from 2016 to 2023 (10 sets minimum). Take at least 5 full-length Prelims mock tests. Focus revision on AP-specific chapters and weak GS areas. Start Mental Ability daily practice (30 questions per day).

Month 7-8: Prelims focused mode. Daily current affairs revision, mock tests every 3 days, and detailed AP GK sweep (chief ministers of AP, YSR-era schemes, Jagan Mohan Reddy schemes, budget highlights, new districts formation, capital dispute status). Prelims on June 21, 2026 sits at the end of this window.

Month 9-12 (post-Prelims): Full Mains preparation mode. Answer writing practice for GS Papers II and III. Telugu Paper IV daily practice with essay writing on AP-current-affairs topics. Interview preparation from Month 11 onwards for candidates confident of Mains qualification.

Candidates with prior UPSC preparation can compress the plan to 6 months by focusing on AP-specific content and Telugu Paper IV, since UPSC prep covers the core GS syllabus adequately. Candidates with prior APPSC Group 1 preparation can compress it to 4 to 5 months since the Group 1 and Group 2 syllabi overlap by around 70 percent.

## Common mistakes candidates make

Seven mistakes account for most APPSC Group 2 rejections across cycles.

Under-preparing AP-specific General Knowledge. Standard UPSC preparation material has minimal AP coverage. APPSC Group 2 Prelims and Mains have 15 to 20 questions each on AP directly (chief ministers, YSR and Jagan schemes, budget, new districts, three-capitals policy, Polavaram, tribal welfare). Missing this is the single biggest score gap.

Ignoring Telugu Paper IV until the last minute. Paper IV carries 150 merit marks and cannot be substituted. Candidates who begin Telugu preparation only 2 months before Mains score 40 to 50 percent on this paper, which drops final rank by 200 to 300 positions.

Wrong post preference order. The commission allocates posts based on merit rank and the preference order given in the application form. Putting Junior Assistant as first preference when the real target is Assistant Section Officer is a common mistake that gets locked at application and cannot be changed later.

Missing the nativity certificate at document verification. Candidates who claim BC, SC, ST reservation or claim AP nativity for post preference must present the Tahsildar-issued nativity certificate at document verification. Missing this document triggers a downgrade to General category or full disqualification.

Skipping the Mental Ability section during Prelims prep. Mental Ability carries around 25 percent of Prelims marks. Candidates focused only on GS often score badly on Mental Ability and fail the Prelims cutoff by a small margin.

Under-answering in Mains. Descriptive papers reward structured answers with introduction, body with sub-points, and conclusion. Wall-of-text or bullet-only answers lose marks compared to structured essays. Practise answer writing weekly from Month 4 onwards.

Ignoring AP current affairs. National current affairs are covered by every candidate. AP-specific current affairs (state budget, new schemes, chief minister announcements, court judgments on the three-capitals issue) differentiate serious candidates. Read Eenadu or Deccan Chronicle daily.

## APPSC Group 2 vs APPSC Group 1 vs UPSC Civil Services

APPSC Group 2 and APPSC Group 1 target different cadre levels within the AP state administration, while UPSC Civil Services recruits into central services and All India Services. This comparison helps candidates decide the right primary target.

| Feature | APPSC Group 2 2026 | APPSC Group 1 (latest cycle) | UPSC Civil Services 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vacancies | 783 | Around 100 to 150 | 1,056 |
| Selection ratio | 1 in 700 | 1 in 3,500 | 1 in 800 |
| Age (General) | 18 to 42 | 18 to 42 | 21 to 32 |
| Attempts limit | No cap, only age ceiling | No cap, only age ceiling | 6 for General, 9 for OBC, unlimited for SC/ST |
| Prelims marks | 150 (qualifying only) | 240 (2 papers, qualifying + eligibility) | 400 |
| Mains marks | 600 merit (4 papers) | 750 merit (5 papers plus optional) | 1,750 merit |
| Interview marks | 75 (Group 2 posts only) | 100 | 275 |
| Total merit ceiling | 675 (Group 2), 600 (Group 2A) | 850 | 2,025 |
| Salary entry | Level 13 to 15 (Rs. 37,100 to 40,270) | Level 20 (Rs. 56,100 basic) | Level 10 (Rs. 56,100 basic) |
| Career ceiling | Principal Secretary rare | Chief Secretary AP possible | Cabinet Secretary direct |
| Home state posting | Guaranteed | Guaranteed | Depends on cadre allocation |
| Prep time typical | 6 to 12 months | 12 to 24 months | 12 to 24 months |
| Syllabus overlap with UPSC | 55 percent | 70 percent | Baseline |

APPSC Group 2 is the right primary target for candidates with AP nativity ties who want a solid state government career with lower competition than Group 1 and shorter preparation timelines than UPSC. APPSC Group 1 is the right target for candidates aiming at the elite Andhra Pradesh administrative service with Deputy Collector-level entry. UPSC is the right target for candidates aiming at national-level cadres with higher career ceilings. Many candidates prepare for all three in parallel because the syllabus overlap allows shared study effort.

## Frequently asked questions

**Who is eligible for APPSC Group 2 2026?**
Indian citizens aged 18 to 42 (General category) with a Bachelor's degree from a UGC-recognised university and AP nativity certification. BC candidates get 5 years extra (up to 47), SC and ST candidates get 10 years extra (up to 52), and PwBD get 10 years over the applicable limit.

**How many vacancies are in APPSC Group 2 2026?**
783 vacancies across 12 post categories including Assistant Section Officer at the Secretariat, Revenue Divisional Officer, Mandal Revenue Officer and Inspector, Municipal Commissioner Grade III, Assistant Registrar (Cooperative), and Assistant Commercial Tax Officer.

**What is the last date to apply for APPSC Group 2 2026?**
March 15, 2026. The online application window opens February 15, 2026 on psc.ap.gov.in. The Preliminary screening test was scheduled for June 21, 2026.

**Is AP nativity mandatory for APPSC Group 2?**
Yes for post allocation and reservation benefits. Non-AP candidates can apply but cannot claim BC, SC, ST reservation and cannot get posts reserved for AP nativity holders. A Tahsildar-issued nativity certificate is verified at the document verification stage.

**How much is the application fee?**
Rs. 250 for General and OBC candidates. Rs. 120 for SC, ST, and PwBD candidates. Payment is online only through Net Banking, UPI, or credit and debit card. There is no offline payment option.

**What is the exam pattern for APPSC Group 2 2026?**
Three stages. Prelims is one 150-mark General Studies and Mental Ability paper (qualifying only). Mains is four papers of 150 marks each (Essay and English, GS I, GS II, Telugu), totalling 600 merit marks. Interview is 75 marks for Group 2 posts only.

**What is the salary of an APPSC Group 2 Assistant Section Officer?**
Pay Level 15 in AP Revised Pay Scales 2022, basic pay Rs. 40,270. Gross monthly Rs. 62,000 to Rs. 72,000 including DA, HRA, and other allowances. In-hand around Rs. 52,000 to Rs. 60,000 after standard deductions.

**Is Telugu Paper IV compulsory?**
Yes for all Group 2 and Group 2A applicants. Telugu Paper IV carries 150 merit marks in Mains and cannot be substituted with any other language. Candidates without Telugu-medium schooling need at least 6 months of structured Telugu preparation.

**How many attempts can I make for APPSC Group 2?**
No cap on total attempts. Only the upper age limit (42 for General, 47 for BC, 52 for SC and ST) applies. You can appear as many times as the age ceiling allows.

**Should I prepare for APPSC Group 2 alongside APPSC Group 1?**
Yes if you have AP nativity and 12 to 24 months of preparation runway. The Group 2 and Group 1 syllabi overlap by around 70 percent. Group 2 becomes a strong fallback if you clear Prelims for both, and the shared preparation time is far more efficient than serial attempts.

## UPSSSC Lower PCS 2026: main exam on 23 August

The Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission is recruiting for its Combined Lower Subordinate Services Examination at graduate level under Advertisement 07-Exam/2026, and the main examination was scheduled for 23 August 2026 from 10:00 am to 12:00 noon.

That is eleven days away at the time of writing.

Applications ran from 29 May 2026 and closed on 25 June 2026 after an extension from the original date of 18 June. Vacancy figures have been reported at various points as around 2,285, then 2,516 following an increase, and 2,587, so the position is best described as roughly 2,500 posts with the exact figure confirmed in the commission's own notices rather than in secondary reporting.

Around 1,00,492 candidates were shortlisted for the main examination on the basis of their normalised PET 2025 scores. Against roughly 2,587 vacancies, that is about 39 candidates per post at the mains stage, which is the honest competition position.

## The PET gateway, and why it matters more than this exam

This is the structural feature that defines UPSSSC recruitment and it is where candidates most often misunderstand the process.

UPSSSC does not run each recruitment as a standalone examination open to all graduates. It runs a common Preliminary Eligibility Test, the PET, and a valid PET score is the precondition for applying to any UPSSSC recruitment. Without one you cannot apply, however well qualified you are.

For this recruitment, the PET 2025 score is what was required. Candidates holding a valid PET 2025 scorecard could apply; those without one could not, and no amount of preparation for the main examination changes that.

Three consequences follow, and they matter for planning a UPSSSC career rather than just this attempt.

The PET is the real bottleneck. Around a lakh candidates were shortlisted here from a PET field that is far larger, so the PET determines who reaches the door and this examination determines who gets through it.

Your PET score has a validity period, and within that window it opens every UPSSSC recruitment advertised. A good PET score is therefore an asset across multiple recruitments rather than a single one, which is why it deserves serious preparation in its own right.

If you do not currently hold a valid PET score, the practical step is to prepare for and sit the next PET rather than tracking individual recruitment notifications you cannot apply to. That is the sequencing candidates get wrong most often.

## Important dates

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Advertisement | 07-Exam/2026 |
| Applications opened | 29 May 2026 |
| Applications closed | 25 June 2026, extended from 18 June |
| Main examination | 23 August 2026, 10:00 am to 12:00 noon |
| Shortlisted for mains | About 1,00,492 candidates on normalised PET 2025 scores |

The two-hour window for the main paper is worth noting. This is a compact examination rather than a long one, which places a premium on pace.

## What the posts are

Combined Lower Subordinate Services covers a range of Group C posts across Uttar Pradesh government departments, filled through a single examination rather than separately.

The posts recruited under this heading typically include supply inspector, excise constable-level and inspector posts, marketing inspector, revenue-side positions, cane supervisor, and a variety of assistant and inspector roles across departments such as food and civil supplies, excise, revenue, cane development, panchayati raj and others.

Because the advertisement covers multiple posts across departments, candidates express post preferences and allocation follows merit, preference and vacancy position. The exact post list, department-wise vacancy distribution and any post-specific eligibility conditions are set out in the advertisement, and that is the document to read rather than a general description.

One practical point: some posts within such combined recruitments carry additional requirements or tests, such as a physical standard for field-facing roles or a specific subject qualification. Check whether any post you have preferenced carries such a condition, since it applies in addition to the general eligibility.

## Main examination pattern

The main examination is a written paper of two hours, held on 23 August 2026 from 10:00 am to 12:00 noon.

The subject coverage for UPSSSC graduate-level main examinations generally spans Hindi language and grammar, general knowledge with substantial weight on Uttar Pradesh, general intelligence and reasoning, current affairs, and elementary arithmetic, with the exact section-wise composition and marks distribution fixed in the advertisement for the cycle.

Because the commission sets the paper structure per recruitment and it has varied between advertisements, the authoritative source for your paper is the advertisement and any subsequent notice on upsssc.gov.in rather than a general description of UPSSSC papers.

What is consistent across UPSSSC examinations is the emphasis on Uttar Pradesh material. State geography, districts and divisions, rivers, agriculture, industries, historical sites, culture, administration, and current state schemes and appointments recur reliably. This is the highest-yield portion of the syllabus and the part where candidates from the state hold an advantage that out-of-state candidates rarely close.

## Preparing in the remaining days

With eleven days to the paper, the work is revision and practice rather than new study.

Concentrate on Uttar Pradesh general knowledge. It is the largest predictable block in the paper and the material is finite: districts, rivers, parks, tribes, festivals, historical sites, state schemes and recent state-level developments can be revised to near-completeness in the time available, which is not true of any other section.

Revise current affairs of roughly the past year, with attention to Uttar Pradesh specifically alongside national developments.

Practise reasoning and arithmetic under timed conditions rather than reading theory. Both are trainable and both reward pace on a two-hour paper.

Work Hindi language and grammar deliberately if your schooling was in another medium. Sandhi, samas, tatsam and tadbhav, idioms, and error correction are rule-based and respond to focused revision quickly.

Take at least two full papers under the two-hour clock in the final week, and use the analysis to fix time allocation rather than only to count marks.

## What happens after the main examination

Following the main examination, the process continues through document verification and, for posts that require it, additional stages such as a skill test or physical standards, before the final merit list and appointment.

Final merit for most UPSSSC recruitments rests on the main examination score, with the PET serving as a screening stage whose marks do not carry into the final ranking. Confirm that for this recruitment in the advertisement, since the commission specifies the merit basis there.

Document verification is where candidatures are lost on paperwork rather than performance. Assemble your documents now rather than after the result: educational certificates, proof of date of birth, category certificate in the Uttar Pradesh format with a current non-creamy layer certificate for OBC candidates, domicile documents, and identity documents matching your application. A discrepancy between a name or date across documents is a common and avoidable problem.

Group C posts recruited through this examination sit in the Uttar Pradesh state pay structure, with the specific pay level varying by post.

Entry pay for graduate-level Group C posts in the state services generally falls in the range associated with pay levels in the lower-middle band of the state matrix, with dearness allowance, house rent allowance depending on the classification of the posting city, and other admissible allowances on top of basic pay. The advertisement states the pay scale for each post, and that is the figure to rely on rather than a general estimate, since the posts covered here differ.

Beyond pay, these are permanent state government posts carrying the leave, medical and pension entitlements applicable to Uttar Pradesh government employees, along with promotion prospects within the departmental hierarchy.

## Career progression

Group C posts in the state services progress through departmental promotion, and the pace depends on the department and the vacancy position in the higher grades.

Alongside promotion, a serving employee who holds a graduate degree and remains within the age band can appear for higher recruitments, including the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission examinations for gazetted posts and other UPSSSC recruitments at higher levels. Many candidates use a Group C post as a stable base from which to prepare for those, since the working hours in most such roles allow it and the position provides income security during preparation.

Our [UPPSC PCS](/sarkari-naukri/uppsc-pcs-2026) page covers the state's gazetted-level route for candidates considering that progression.

It is worth being clear about the distinction between the two, since the names invite confusion. This recruitment is Lower Subordinate Services, conducted by UPSSSC for Group C posts, gated by the PET. UPPSC PCS is the Provincial Civil Services examination conducted by the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission for gazetted posts including Deputy Collector and Deputy Superintendent of Police, with its own preliminary, mains and interview structure and no PET requirement. They are different examinations, different commissions and different levels of the state service, despite both containing the letters PCS.

A candidate whose target is the gazetted service should be preparing for UPPSC rather than UPSSSC, and the general studies base overlaps enough that a serving Group C employee can work towards it while employed.

## Parallel options worth applying to

Because UPSSSC recruitments are advertised irregularly and gated by PET validity, a graduate targeting government employment should keep other applications running rather than waiting on one commission.

Central graduate-level recruitment runs on its own calendar and needs no state-specific gateway: [SSC CGL](/sarkari-naukri/ssc-cgl-2026) for central government posts, [RRB NTPC](/sarkari-naukri/rrb-ntpc-2026) for graduate railway posts, and the banking examinations including [IBPS PO](/sarkari-naukri/ibps-po-2026) and [IBPS Clerk](/sarkari-naukri/ibps-clerk-2026).

The preparation base overlaps substantially. Reasoning, arithmetic, English or Hindi language and general awareness serve all of them, and only the state-specific general knowledge is particular to UPSSSC. A candidate who has prepared Uttar Pradesh general knowledge thoroughly for UPSSSC has done work that does not transfer, but everything else does.

The practical approach is to treat the UP-specific material as the addition rather than the foundation, and to apply to every central and state recruitment your qualification permits in a given year rather than concentrating on one.

## How to apply in the next cycle

Applications for this recruitment are closed. For a future UPSSSC recruitment, the sequence is what matters.

1. Sit the Preliminary Eligibility Test and obtain a valid PET score. Without this you cannot apply to any UPSSSC recruitment, so it is the first step rather than a parallel one.
2. Register on upsssc.gov.in and complete the one-time registration, which the commission reuses across its recruitments.
3. Watch for advertisements you are eligible for and apply within the window, quoting your valid PET score.
4. Fill personal, educational and category details exactly as on your certificates, since these feed both eligibility and reservation.
5. Enter post preferences carefully, as allocation follows merit and preference together.
6. Upload photograph and signature in the specified format and pay the fee.
7. Submit, save the application, and download the admit card when released.

## Understanding the PET properly

Since the PET governs access to every UPSSSC recruitment, it deserves more than a passing mention for anyone planning a UP state government career.

The Preliminary Eligibility Test is a screening examination conducted for graduate-level and intermediate-level candidates separately, producing a score that remains valid for a defined period. During that validity, the score is quoted on applications to UPSSSC recruitments as they are advertised.

The design intent is administrative. UPSSSC advertises many recruitments across many departments, and running a separate preliminary stage for each would be enormously expensive and slow. A single common screening test, with a score reused across advertisements, replaces that.

For a candidate the implication is a change of strategy. Rather than preparing intensively for whichever recruitment happens to be advertised, the sensible approach is to prepare seriously for the PET once, secure a strong normalised score, and then apply to every advertisement your qualification permits during the validity window. A candidate with a strong PET score and a modest number of applications is worse placed than one with the same score and many.

The PET syllabus covers ground that overlaps heavily with the mains: Indian history and the national movement, geography, economy, polity and administration, general science, elementary arithmetic, general Hindi, reasoning, current affairs and, importantly, Uttar Pradesh-specific general knowledge. That overlap means PET preparation is not separate from mains preparation; it is the foundation of it.

Normalisation applies to PET scores, since the test runs across shifts, so your usable score is the normalised one rather than your raw marks.

## Common mistakes in UPSSSC applications

Not holding a valid PET score and preparing for the mains anyway. This is the most consequential error, since the application is simply not possible, and it is entirely avoidable by checking the requirement before starting.

Treating the PET as a formality. It determines who reaches the mains across every recruitment, so a mediocre PET score constrains an entire validity period rather than one attempt.

Filling post preferences casually. Allocation follows merit and preference together, so an order that does not reflect what you actually want can produce a posting in a department you would not have chosen.

Ignoring post-specific conditions. Some posts in a combined recruitment carry physical standards or subject requirements, and a candidate who preferences one without meeting them loses the allocation at verification.

Neglecting the Uttar Pradesh portion of general knowledge. It is the most reliably recurring and highest-yield section in UPSSSC papers, and candidates who prepare only national-level material give away marks that are freely available.

Practise reasoning and arithmetic under timed conditions rather than reading theory. Both are trainable and both reward pace on a two-hour paper.

Work Hindi language and grammar deliberately if your schooling was in another medium. Sandhi, samas, tatsam and tadbhav, idioms, and error correction are rule-based and respond to focused revision quickly.

Group C posts recruited through this examination sit in the Uttar Pradesh state pay structure, with the specific pay level varying by post.

Entry pay for graduate-level Group C posts in the state services generally falls in the range associated with pay levels in the lower-middle band of the state matrix, with dearness allowance, house rent allowance depending on the classification of the posting city, and other admissible allowances on top of basic pay. The design intent is administrative. UPSSSC advertises many recruitments across many departments, and running a separate preliminary stage for each would be enormously expensive and slow. A single common screening test, with a score reused across advertisements, replaces that.

For a candidate the implication is a change of strategy. Rather than preparing intensively for whichever recruitment happens to be advertised, the sensible approach is to prepare seriously for the PET once, secure a strong normalised score, and then apply to every advertisement your qualification permits during the validity window. A candidate with a strong PET score and a modest number of applications is worse placed than one with the same score and many.

The PET syllabus covers ground that overlaps heavily with the mains: Indian history and the national movement, geography, economy, polity and administration, general science, elementary arithmetic, general Hindi, reasoning, current affairs and, importantly, Uttar Pradesh-specific general knowledge. That overlap means PET preparation is not separate from mains preparation; it is the foundation of it.

Normalisation applies to PET scores, since the test runs across shifts, so your usable score is the normalised one rather than your raw marks.

Not holding a valid PET score and preparing for the mains anyway. This is the most consequential error, since the application is simply not possible, and it is entirely avoidable by checking the requirement before starting.

Treating the PET as a formality. It determines who reaches the mains across every recruitment, so a mediocre PET score constrains an entire validity period rather than one attempt.

Filling post preferences casually. Allocation follows merit and preference together, so an order that does not reflect what you actually want can produce a posting in a department you would not have chosen.

Ignoring post-specific conditions. Some posts in a combined recruitment carry physical standards or subject requirements, and a candidate who preferences one without meeting them loses the allocation at verification.

Neglecting the Uttar Pradesh portion of general knowledge. It is the most reliably recurring and highest-yield section in UPSSSC papers, and candidates who prepare only national-level material give away marks that are freely available.

Assembling documents after the result. Document verification is where candidatures are lost on paperwork, and category or domicile certificates in the wrong format take weeks to correct.

## NEET PG 2026: the edit window closes today

NEET PG 2026, conducted by the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences, was scheduled for 30 August 2026. That is twenty days away at the time of writing.

Two things need attention immediately.

The selective edit window was open until 10 August 2026, which is today. If anything in your application needs correcting, that closes now and does not reopen. Registration itself closed on 21 July 2026.

And the exam pattern has changed for 2026. NBEMS reduced the paper from 200 questions to 180, and the total from 800 marks to 720. Candidates preparing from older material, or working through mock papers built on the previous structure, are practising a paper that no longer exists.

## Important dates

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Registration closed | 21 July 2026 |
| Selective edit window | Until 10 August 2026 |
| Examination | 30 August 2026 |
| Result | Expected within a fortnight of the exam, around 15 September 2026 |
| Counselling | Conducted by MCC in multiple rounds after the result |

The fortnight turnaround between exam and result is characteristic of NEET PG and worth planning around. Unlike examinations where results take months, you will know your position by mid-September, and counselling registration follows quickly. Candidates who treat the period after 30 August as a break often find themselves unprepared for counselling choices that need research.

## The revised 2026 exam pattern

| Element | 2026 | Previously |
|---|---|---|
| Questions | 180 | 200 |
| Total marks | 720 | 800 |
| Duration | 3 hours 30 minutes | 3 hours 30 minutes |
| Mode | Computer based | Computer based |
| Marking | +4 correct, −1 wrong | +4 correct, −1 wrong |

Twenty fewer questions in the same time changes the arithmetic of the paper more than it appears. You now have about 70 seconds per question rather than 63, which is a meaningful increase in thinking time on a paper where the questions are clinically dense.

The practical consequence is that the 2026 paper rewards accuracy slightly more and raw speed slightly less. With fewer questions carrying the same weight each, every individual question matters more to the final score: one question is now worth about 0.56 per cent of the total rather than 0.5 per cent.

Candidates should also check that their mock test material has been updated. A 200-question mock taken in 210 minutes trains a pace that is now unnecessarily fast, and one built to the old marks total gives a misleading sense of where you stand.

## Marking, and the negative marking calculation

Four marks for a correct answer, one deducted for a wrong one, nothing for an unattempted question.

That is a 4 to 1 ratio, which is more forgiving than it first sounds. Guessing blindly among four options yields on average one correct at plus 4 against three wrong at minus 3, a net gain of 1 mark. So blind guessing carries positive expected value.

Eliminating even one option improves that substantially. With two plausible options remaining, the expected value of attempting is strongly positive.

The implication for a 180-question paper is that you should leave very few blanks. A candidate finishing with twenty unattempted questions has forgone roughly 20 marks of expected value, which on a percentile-ranked examination with a dense field is a material loss.

That said, NEET PG is scored against a percentile rather than an absolute standard, so the goal is relative performance. Reckless attempting that produces many wrong answers still costs marks against candidates who are more selective, so the balance is to attempt everything you can reason about at all and leave only the questions where you genuinely cannot narrow the field.

## What the paper covers

NEET PG tests the MBBS syllabus across pre-clinical, para-clinical and clinical subjects, weighted towards the clinical subjects that dominate postgraduate practice.

The pre-clinical subjects are Anatomy, Physiology and Biochemistry. The para-clinical subjects are Pathology, Pharmacology, Microbiology and Forensic Medicine, along with Community Medicine or Preventive and Social Medicine. The clinical subjects are Medicine, Surgery, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Paediatrics, Orthopaedics, Ophthalmology, Ear Nose and Throat, Dermatology, Psychiatry, Anaesthesia and Radiology.

Medicine, Surgery, Obstetrics and Gynaecology and Paediatrics carry the heaviest weight between them, and Community Medicine has grown in prominence in recent cycles. Questions are increasingly clinical in framing rather than recall-based, presenting a case and asking for diagnosis, next investigation or management.

Because the paper draws on the entire MBBS curriculum, the realistic preparation strategy in the final twenty days is revision and question practice rather than fresh study of any subject.

## Percentile, and what qualifying means

NEET PG results are reported as a score and a percentile, and the qualifying standard is set as a percentile rather than a fixed mark.

The usual qualifying percentiles are the 50th percentile for General and EWS candidates, the 40th percentile for SC, ST and OBC candidates, and the 45th percentile for General category candidates with a benchmark disability. NBEMS and the Medical Counselling Committee confirm the applicable cutoffs after each result, and they have on occasion been revised downward in a given cycle when seats remained unfilled, so the announced figures for your cycle govern.

Qualifying is not the same as getting a seat. Clearing the percentile makes you eligible to participate in counselling; what determines whether you get a seat, and in which speciality and college, is your rank against the field and the choices you make in counselling.

That distinction matters because the gap between the qualifying percentile and the score needed for a competitive speciality in a good college is very large. A candidate at the 50th percentile has qualified and will realistically be choosing among the less contested options.

## Counselling: how seats are actually allotted

After the result, the Medical Counselling Committee conducts counselling online across multiple rounds.

Seats are divided broadly into the All India Quota, administered centrally by MCC, and the State Quota, administered by individual state authorities through their own counselling processes. Deemed and central universities, and certain institutional seats, are handled within the MCC process.

The practical implication is that most candidates participate in two parallel processes: the MCC counselling for All India Quota and central institutions, and their state's counselling for state quota seats. Registering for both, where eligible, widens the options considerably, and candidates who engage only with one reduce their chances without realising it.

Counselling proceeds in rounds. In each round you register, pay the fee, fill and lock a preference list of college and speciality combinations, and receive an allotment based on rank and preferences. You may then accept and report, or in some rounds choose to participate again for a better allotment, subject to the rules on resignation, forfeiture and security deposits, which differ by round.

Those rules are where candidates lose seats through procedural error rather than rank. Reading the MCC information bulletin for the current cycle before the first round opens is genuinely important, because decisions about whether to freeze an allotment or float for a better one carry consequences that cannot be undone.

## Choice-filling: the decision that shapes a career

The preference list is the most consequential thing a candidate does after the examination, and it gets far less attention than the exam itself.

You are choosing combinations of speciality and college, and the two trade off against each other. A more competitive speciality at a less prestigious institution, or a less contested speciality at a better one, are genuinely different career paths rather than better and worse versions of the same thing.

Some practical considerations. Clinical specialities with strong practice prospects are contested hardest, which means the same rank buys a much better college in a less contested branch. Non-clinical and para-clinical specialities are available at ranks where clinical branches are not, and they lead to academic, laboratory and public health careers that suit some doctors better than clinical practice does. Bond conditions, stipends and service obligations vary enormously between states and institutions and should be checked before preferencing, since a bond can bind several years of your life.

Research previous years' closing ranks for the combinations you are considering. They are published and they tell you far more about your realistic options than any general advice can.

## What happens on exam day

Practical details, since a computer-based clinical paper has its own logistics.

Your admit card specifies the reporting time, which is well ahead of the examination start, and NBEMS does not admit candidates who arrive after the stated closing time. Biometric verification and document checks take time, which is why the window opens early.

Carry the printed admit card and the photo identity document specified on it, and ensure the name matches your application exactly. NBEMS is strict on identity verification.

Electronic items are prohibited: mobile phones, smart watches, calculators, Bluetooth devices and storage media. So are bags and written material. Centres do not reliably provide storage.

The examination runs for 210 continuous minutes with no scheduled break, which is a genuine endurance requirement. Candidates who have not sat a full 210-minute mock discover this on the day, which is a poor time to learn it.

Because the paper is computer based, spend the first minute familiarising yourself with the navigation, the review and marking tools, and where the question palette shows attempted and unattempted items. Knowing how to jump quickly to flagged questions matters when you return to fill blanks at the end.

## Where NEET PG sits among the medical PG routes

NEET PG is the main route to postgraduate medical seats, but it is not the only examination a medical graduate encounters.

| Route | For | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| NEET PG | MD, MS and PG Diploma seats across India | The principal route, conducted by NBEMS |
| INI CET | Postgraduate seats at Institutes of National Importance such as AIIMS, PGIMER, JIPMER and NIMHANS | A separate examination with its own cycle and counselling |
| [NEET SS](/entrance-exams/neet-ss-2026) | Super-speciality courses, DM and MCh, after completing a postgraduate degree | Taken later, after PG |
| State-level processes | State quota seats | Administered through state counselling using NEET PG scores |

The distinction worth noting is that INI CET is a genuinely separate examination for the institutes of national importance, so a candidate targeting AIIMS or PGIMER needs to sit that as well as NEET PG rather than instead of it. The two have separate registrations, separate dates and separate counselling.

NEET SS comes later in a career, after a postgraduate degree, for super-speciality training.

## Eligibility

Candidates must hold an MBBS degree recognised by the National Medical Commission, or be due to complete the internship by the cutoff date specified in the information bulletin for the cycle.

Registration with the National Medical Commission or a State Medical Council is required, whether provisional or permanent.

Completion of the compulsory rotating internship by the prescribed date is the condition that most commonly affects eligibility, and the date is set in the bulletin each year.

There is no age limit and no cap on the number of attempts.

## The final twenty days

With the examination on 30 August, the useful work is narrow.

Revise rather than study new material. Twenty days before a paper drawing on the whole MBBS curriculum, the return on opening a new subject is close to zero while the cost in revision time is real.

Work questions, not chapters. Clinical vignette questions train the reasoning the paper actually tests, and they surface gaps far faster than reading does, because a gap you cannot answer around is immediately visible in a way that a chapter you have read passively is not.

Take full-length mocks built to the 180-question, 720-mark pattern, under the 210-minute clock, and analyse each one properly. If your mock material is still on the 200-question structure, the timing it trains is now wrong.

Prioritise the high-weight clinical subjects and Community Medicine in revision, since that is where the marks concentrate, and resist the temptation to spend the final fortnight shoring up a pre-clinical subject that carries few questions.

Rehearse the attempt strategy: with a 4 to 1 marking ratio, decide in advance that you will attempt anything you can narrow at all, and reserve the final minutes to fill remaining blanks.

And begin reading about counselling now, in the gaps. The result arrives around mid-September and the choices come quickly after, so the research you do in August is research you will not have time for later. Pull the closing ranks for the speciality and college combinations you would realistically consider, note the bond conditions attached to each, and keep the list somewhere you can return to once you have a rank.

One more thing worth doing today rather than later: check your application in the edit window before it closes. A misspelled name, a wrong category entry or an incorrect photograph can create problems at the centre or at counselling verification, and the correction window is the only opportunity to fix any of it.

NEET PG 2026 was scheduled for 30 August 2026, conducted by NBEMS in computer-based mode. Registration closed on 21 July 2026. The selective edit window remains open until 10 August 2026, after which no corrections to the application are possible.

NBEMS releases the result within a fortnight of the examination, so with the exam on 30 August 2026 the result is expected around 15 September 2026. Counselling by the Medical Counselling Committee follows shortly afterwards, which is why counselling research is best done in August rather than after the result.

**What are the NEET PG qualifying percentiles?**
Usually the 50th percentile for General and EWS candidates, the 40th percentile for SC, ST and OBC candidates, and the 45th percentile for General category candidates with a benchmark disability. NBEMS and MCC confirm the applicable cutoffs after each result, and they have occasionally been revised downward in a cycle when seats remained unfilled, so the announced figures for your cycle govern.

**Does qualifying NEET PG mean I get a seat?**
No. Clearing the qualifying percentile makes you eligible to participate in counselling. Whether you receive a seat, and in which speciality and college, depends on your rank against the field and the choices you make during counselling. The gap between the qualifying percentile and the score needed for a competitive speciality at a good college is very large.

Seats divide broadly into the All India Quota administered by MCC and the State Quota administered by individual states, with deemed and central university seats handled within the MCC process. Most candidates should register for both MCC counselling and their state's counselling where eligible, since engaging with only one narrows the options.

**What should I consider when filling NEET PG choices?**
That speciality and college trade off against each other. Competitive clinical branches are contested hardest, so the same rank buys a better college in a less contested branch. Non-clinical and para-clinical specialities are available at ranks where clinical branches are not and lead to academic, laboratory and public health careers. Check bond conditions, stipends and service obligations before preferencing, since these vary enormously and a bond can commit several years. Research published closing ranks for the combinations you are considering.

The internship completion date is the condition that most commonly affects eligibility. There is no age limit and no cap on attempts.

The para-clinical subjects are Pathology, Pharmacology, Microbiology and Forensic Medicine, along with Community Medicine or Preventive and Social Medicine. The clinical subjects are Medicine, Surgery, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Paediatrics, Orthopaedics, Ophthalmology, Ear Nose and Throat, Dermatology, Psychiatry, Anaesthesia and Radiology.

Medicine, Surgery, Obstetrics and Gynaecology and Paediatrics carry the heaviest weight between them, and Community Medicine has grown in prominence in recent cycles. Questions are increasingly clinical in framing rather than recall-based, presenting a case and asking for diagnosis, next investigation or management.

Because the paper draws on the entire MBBS curriculum, the realistic preparation strategy in the final twenty days is revision and question practice rather than fresh study of any subject.

## Percentile, and what qualifying means

NEET PG results are reported as a score and a percentile, and the qualifying standard is set as a percentile rather than a fixed mark.

The usual qualifying percentiles are the 50th percentile for General and EWS candidates, the 40th percentile for SC, ST and OBC candidates, and the 45th percentile for General category candidates with a benchmark disability. Qualifying is not the same as getting a seat. Clearing the percentile makes you eligible to participate in counselling; what determines whether you get a seat, and in which speciality and college, is your rank against the field and the choices you make in counselling.

That distinction matters because the gap between the qualifying percentile and the score needed for a competitive speciality in a good college is very large. A candidate at the 50th percentile has qualified and will realistically be choosing among the less contested options.

After the result, the Medical Counselling Committee conducts counselling online across multiple rounds.

Reading the MCC information bulletin for the current cycle before the first round opens is genuinely important, because decisions about whether to freeze an allotment or float for a better one carry consequences that cannot be undone.

The preference list is the most consequential thing a candidate does after the examination, and it gets far less attention than the exam itself.

You are choosing combinations of speciality and college, and the two trade off against each other. A more competitive speciality at a less prestigious institution, or a less contested speciality at a better one, are genuinely different career paths rather than better and worse versions of the same thing.

Some practical considerations. Clinical specialities with strong practice prospects are contested hardest, which means the same rank buys a much better college in a less contested branch. Non-clinical and para-clinical specialities are available at ranks where clinical branches are not, and they lead to academic, laboratory and public health careers that suit some doctors better than clinical practice does. Bond conditions, stipends and service obligations vary enormously between states and institutions and should be checked before preferencing, since a bond can bind several years of your life.

Research previous years' closing ranks for the combinations you are considering. They are published and they tell you far more about your realistic options than any general advice can.

## What happens on exam day

Practical details, since a computer-based clinical paper has its own logistics.

Your admit card specifies the reporting time, which is well ahead of the examination start, and NBEMS does not admit candidates who arrive after the stated closing time. Biometric verification and document checks take time, which is why the window opens early.

Carry the printed admit card and the photo identity document specified on it, and ensure the name matches your application exactly. NBEMS is strict on identity verification.

Electronic items are prohibited: mobile phones, smart watches, calculators, Bluetooth devices and storage media. So are bags and written material. Centres do not reliably provide storage.

The examination runs for 210 continuous minutes with no scheduled break, which is a genuine endurance requirement. Candidates who have not sat a full 210-minute mock discover this on the day, which is a poor time to learn it.

Because the paper is computer based, spend the first minute familiarising yourself with the navigation, the review and marking tools, and where the question palette shows attempted and unattempted items. Knowing how to jump quickly to flagged questions matters when you return to fill blanks at the end.

## Where NEET PG sits among the medical PG routes

NEET PG is the main route to postgraduate medical seats, but it is not the only examination a medical graduate encounters.

| Route | For | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| NEET PG | MD, MS and PG Diploma seats across India | The principal route, conducted by NBEMS |
| INI CET | Postgraduate seats at Institutes of National Importance such as AIIMS, PGIMER, JIPMER and NIMHANS | A separate examination with its own cycle and counselling |
| [NEET SS](/entrance-exams/neet-ss-2026) | Super-speciality courses, DM and MCh, after completing a postgraduate degree | Taken later, after PG |
| State-level processes | State quota seats | Administered through state counselling using NEET PG scores |

The distinction worth noting is that INI CET is a genuinely separate examination for the institutes of national importance, so a candidate targeting AIIMS or PGIMER needs to sit that as well as NEET PG rather than instead of it. The two have separate registrations, separate dates and separate counselling.

NEET SS comes later in a career, after a postgraduate degree, for super-speciality training.

## Eligibility

Candidates must hold an MBBS degree recognised by the National Medical Commission, or be due to complete the internship by the cutoff date specified in the information bulletin for the cycle.

Registration with the National Medical Commission or a State Medical Council is required, whether provisional or permanent.

Completion of the compulsory rotating internship by the prescribed date is the condition that most commonly affects eligibility, and the date is set in the bulletin each year.

There is no age limit and no cap on the number of attempts.

With the examination on 30 August, the useful work is narrow.

Revise rather than study new material. Twenty days before a paper drawing on the whole MBBS curriculum, the return on opening a new subject is close to zero while the cost in revision time is real.

Work questions, not chapters. Clinical vignette questions train the reasoning the paper actually tests, and they surface gaps far faster than reading does, because a gap you cannot answer around is immediately visible in a way that a chapter you have read passively is not.

Take full-length mocks built to the 180-question, 720-mark pattern, under the 210-minute clock, and analyse each one properly. If your mock material is still on the 200-question structure, the timing it trains is now wrong.

Prioritise the high-weight clinical subjects and Community Medicine in revision, since that is where the marks concentrate, and resist the temptation to spend the final fortnight shoring up a pre-clinical subject that carries few questions.

Rehearse the attempt strategy: with a 4 to 1 marking ratio, decide in advance that you will attempt anything you can narrow at all, and reserve the final minutes to fill remaining blanks.

And begin reading about counselling now, in the gaps. The result arrives around mid-September and the choices come quickly after, so the research you do in August is research you will not have time for later. Pull the closing ranks for the speciality and college combinations you would realistically consider, note the bond conditions attached to each, and keep the list somewhere you can return to once you have a rank.

One more thing worth doing today rather than later: check your application in the edit window before it closes. A misspelled name, a wrong category entry or an incorrect photograph can create problems at the centre or at counselling verification, and the correction window is the only opportunity to fix any of it.

NEET PG 2026 is on 30 August 2026, conducted by NBEMS in computer-based mode. Registration closed on 21 July 2026. The selective edit window remains open until 10 August 2026, after which no corrections to the application are possible.

720 marks, from 180 questions at 4 marks each. This is down from the previous 800 marks across 200 questions. Each question is now worth about 0.56 per cent of the total rather than 0.5 per cent, so individual questions carry slightly more weight.

## MH SET Exam 2026 registration, exam date, and how to apply

The Maharashtra State Eligibility Test 2026 (MH SET Exam 2026) closed for applications on June 16, 2026, with the exam scheduled for July 26, 2026. Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU) conducts the test on behalf of the Government of Maharashtra. Anyone planning to become an Assistant Professor in a college affiliated to a Maharashtra or Goa university needs this certificate before recruitment.

## Important dates for MH SET Exam 2026

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Registration opens | June 2, 2026 |
| Last date to apply | **June 16, 2026** |
| Last date to pay fee | June 17, 2026 |
| Correction window | June 18 to June 20, 2026 |
| Admit card release | Second week of July 2026 |
| Exam date | **July 26, 2026** |
| Provisional answer key | First week of August 2026 |
| Result | August to September 2026 |

## How to apply for MH SET Exam 2026 step by step

Applications go through setexam.unipune.ac.in only. The board does not accept offline forms.

1. Visit setexam.unipune.ac.in and click "MH SET 2026 Registration".
2. Enter your name, date of birth, category, and a valid email plus mobile number. You will receive a registration ID.
3. Log in with the registration ID and fill in academic details, subject choice, and preferred exam city.
4. Upload a passport photo (max 100 KB, JPG) and signature (max 40 KB, JPG).
5. Pay the fee online via net banking, debit card, or UPI.
6. Download the confirmation page and print two copies. Keep one for the exam day.

The correction window on June 18 to 20 lets you fix any error in name, subject, or category. After that, no change is allowed.

## Eligibility for MH SET Exam 2026

You are eligible if you have a Master's degree in the subject you want to appear in, with at least 55% marks (50% for OBC, SC, ST, PwD, and third-gender candidates). Final-year Master's students can apply provisionally but must submit their mark sheet within two years of clearing the exam.

There is no upper age limit.

### Three quick worked examples

- Priya, MA English, 58%, general category: eligible. She can appear in the English subject paper.
- Rahul, MSc Physics, 53%, OBC: eligible. His 53% clears the 50% OBC threshold.
- Anjali, MCom, 49%, SC: not eligible for the 2026 attempt. She needs 50% minimum. She could upgrade her marks through a bridge program or re-attempt select papers if her university allows.

PhD holders who completed their doctorate under UGC 2009 or later regulations are exempt from SET/NET for direct Assistant Professor recruitment, though the SET certificate still helps in interviews.

## MH SET Exam 2026 pattern and marking

MH SET has two papers on the same day, held in a single sitting with no break.

**Paper I: Teaching and research aptitude**
Compulsory for every candidate. 50 questions, 100 marks, 60 minutes. Sections cover teaching aptitude, research aptitude, reading comprehension, communication, reasoning (including mathematical reasoning), data interpretation, ICT, people and environment, and higher education system.

**Paper II: Subject-specific**
100 questions, 200 marks, 120 minutes. You appear in the subject of your post-graduation.

No negative marking in either paper. Every correct answer gets 2 marks.

## Paper I topic-by-topic breakdown

Paper I is where most candidates lose or gain their edge because it is the same for every subject and rewards consistent scoring. Here is what each of the 9 topic areas tests:

- **Teaching aptitude:** teaching methods, learner characteristics, factors affecting teaching, teaching support systems. About 5 to 7 questions.
- **Research aptitude:** research methods, thesis writing, research ethics, IPR basics. 4 to 6 questions.
- **Reading comprehension:** two passages of about 500 words each, 5 questions per passage. Practice with previous year passages.
- **Communication:** types of communication, barriers, mass media, and effective communication. 4 to 5 questions.
- **Reasoning including mathematical:** number series, letter series, coding-decoding, and basic mathematical reasoning. 6 to 8 questions.
- **Logical reasoning:** venn diagrams, syllogisms, analogies. 4 to 5 questions.
- **Data interpretation:** table-based, bar chart, pie chart interpretation. 4 to 5 questions.
- **ICT:** internet basics, e-learning, MS Office fundamentals, computer terminology. 3 to 5 questions.
- **People, development, and environment:** current environmental issues, sustainable development, environmental policies. 3 to 4 questions.
- **Higher education system:** governance of higher education in India, UGC, AICTE, professional councils, institutions of higher learning. 3 to 5 questions.

Scoring 65 marks out of 100 on Paper I is a realistic and often decisive target.

## Subjects offered in MH SET Exam 2026

Over 60 subjects are available. The most popular are:

- Humanities: History, Political Science, Sociology, Public Administration, Marathi, Hindi, English, Sanskrit
- Commerce and Management: Commerce, Business Administration, Home Science
- Sciences: Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics, Botany, Zoology, Environmental Science, Geography, Earth Science
- Professional: Computer Science, Electronic Science, Library and Information Science, Physical Education, Law, Journalism and Mass Communication

You must appear in the subject that matches your post-graduation. A candidate with MA Political Science cannot appear in the Economics paper.

## Application fee for MH SET Exam 2026

| Category | Fee |
|---|---|
| General / Open | Rs. 800 |
| OBC / EWS / SBC | Rs. 650 |
| SC / ST / PwD / Third-gender | Rs. 550 |

Fees are non-refundable. Pay before June 17, 2026 to avoid rejection.

## MH SET 2026 exam centres

The exam is held at 30+ centres across Maharashtra and 2 in Goa. Popular cities include Mumbai, Pune, Nagpur, Nashik, Aurangabad, Kolhapur, Solapur, Amravati, Thane, and Panaji (Goa).

At registration, you select up to three preferred cities in order of priority. The final centre allotment is confirmed on your admit card and is generally the first or second preference. Once allotted, the centre cannot be changed. Plan travel and accommodation accordingly, especially if you are allotted a centre 2 to 3 hours from your home city.

Reporting is at the exam centre, not the university campus, so read your admit card carefully for the exact address.

## Exam day guide for MH SET 2026

The exam runs in a single sitting from 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM (Paper I from 10:00 to 11:00, Paper II from 11:00 to 1:00, no break).

- **Reach by 8:30 AM.** Gates typically close at 9:30 AM. Late entry is not allowed.
- **Carry these to the centre:** printed admit card (2 copies), a valid original photo ID (Aadhaar, PAN, Driving Licence, Passport, or Voter ID), and 2 recent passport photos matching the one uploaded.
- **What to bring for writing:** blue or black ballpoint pen only. Pencils, correction fluid, and gel pens are not allowed for OMR marking.
- **What is banned inside the hall:** mobile phones, smartwatches, Bluetooth devices, calculators, wallets, bags, printed material, and any electronic gadget. Storage outside the hall is at your own risk, so travel light.
- **Dress code:** no formal dress code, but comfortable full-sleeve clothing is recommended because centres often keep AC low. Avoid heavy metallic jewellery to speed up frisking.
- **After the exam:** you keep your admit card, not the OMR. Store your admit card safely because you will need it for the answer key objection window and any downstream correspondence.

## Reservation and category-wise cutoff mechanics

MH SET's qualifying formula has two stages, both of which must clear:

1. **Aggregate cutoff across both papers combined**: 40 percent for General, EWS, and Open category candidates; 35 percent for OBC, SC, ST, PwD, and Third-gender candidates.
2. **Top 6 percent per subject, per category**: from the pool of candidates who cleared step 1, the top 6 percent in each subject and each category are declared SET-passed.

The second stage is the actual bottleneck. A candidate scoring 45 percent may still not qualify if their subject and category pool is heavily contested, while a candidate scoring 41 percent could qualify in a less-competitive subject or category. Cutoffs are not fixed in absolute marks and are calculated post-result.

## Preparation strategy for MH SET Exam 2026

You have roughly 45 days between the last application date and the exam. That is enough time if you already know your subject well.

- Weeks 1 and 2: solve 5 years of previous year papers for Paper I. This alone tells you which topics MH SET repeats.
- Weeks 3 and 4: cover your Paper II syllabus from your PG textbooks. Do not buy a new "MH SET guide". The standard university textbooks are enough.
- Weeks 5 and 6: full-length mocks, one every alternate day. Aim for 65 percent in Paper I and 55 percent in Paper II.

Candidates who cleared past cycles most often recommend KVS Madaan (Pearson) and Rukmini Bhaya Nair for Paper I, along with the free NTA UGC-NET Paper I resource on the official portal.

## MH SET vs UGC-NET: which one should you take

| Feature | MH SET | UGC-NET |
|---|---|---|
| Conducting body | SPPU | NTA |
| Frequency | Once a year | Twice a year (June and December) |
| Valid in | Maharashtra and Goa | All Indian states |
| Certificate validity | Lifetime | Lifetime |
| Application fee | Rs. 550 to Rs. 800 | Rs. 600 to Rs. 1,150 |
| Difficulty | Moderate | Slightly higher |

Most serious aspirants attempt both. Clearing either one qualifies you for teaching in Maharashtra colleges. Clearing UGC-NET gives you national mobility.

## What happens after you clear MH SET

The MH SET certificate has lifetime validity. Once you clear, you can:

1. Apply to any Maharashtra or Goa college recruiting Assistant Professors (watch openings on collegerecruitment.mahaonline.gov.in and individual college websites).
2. Appear for university NET-cleared teaching positions.
3. Register on the government's SET-passed candidate portal for direct interview calls.

The certificate does not guarantee a job. It is a minimum eligibility filter. Actual recruitment depends on individual college interviews, which weigh subject knowledge, teaching demo, and (increasingly) research output.

## The reality of Assistant Professor recruitment after MH SET

Passing the exam is step one. Actual recruitment in Maharashtra runs on three tracks:

- **Government (aided) colleges:** highest job security and best pay (7th CPC, Rs. 57,700 to Rs. 1,82,400 entry level). Recruitment happens through college-wise notifications, but appointment is usually approved by the state Department of Higher Education. Interview panels are strict; PhD, publications, and NET/SET together are often expected.
- **Unaided private colleges:** salaries range Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 50,000 per month at entry level, sometimes lower. Fewer perks but faster hiring. Many candidates use these as a first step before moving to aided colleges.
- **Autonomous and deemed universities:** apply directly via their own recruitment portals. Selection processes vary widely and often skip the state approval step.

Publication record and PhD status matter more than raw MH SET scores in interviews. Start planning your first UGC-CARE listed paper as soon as you clear.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- Applying in the wrong subject. The subject you appear in must match your PG degree exactly. A candidate with MA Sociology cannot appear in the Political Science paper even if the syllabi overlap.
- Uploading oversized documents. The portal silently rejects photos above 100 KB. Compress before uploading.
- Missing the correction window. After June 20, no change is allowed. Verify every field before June 17 payment.
- Waiting for the "final" answer key to challenge questions. Objections must be raised during the provisional answer key window, not after.
- Skipping the mock test phase because "I know the syllabus". Time management on OMR is a distinct skill; without practice, most candidates finish Paper II 10 to 15 minutes late.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is MH SET Exam 2026 online or offline?**
MH SET Exam 2026 is a pen-and-paper (OMR) exam held at physical centres across Maharashtra and Goa on July 26, 2026. It is not a computer-based test.

**How many attempts are allowed for MH SET?**
There is no cap on the number of attempts. You can appear every year until you clear.

**What is the passing percentage for MH SET Exam 2026?**
Candidates need at least 40 percent aggregate across both papers for General category and 35 percent for reserved categories. From this qualifying pool, the top 6 percent per subject per category are declared SET-passed.

**Can final-year PG students apply for MH SET Exam 2026?**
Yes. Final-year Master's candidates can apply provisionally but must submit their mark sheet within two years of the result date.

**Is MH SET valid outside Maharashtra?**
No. MH SET is valid only in Maharashtra and Goa. For other states, either clear that state's SET (Karnataka SET, Kerala SET, and similar) or clear UGC-NET which is valid nationally.

**How do I download the MH SET 2026 admit card?**
Admit cards release in the second week of July on setexam.unipune.ac.in. Log in with your registration ID and password. Download and print two copies.

**Is there negative marking in MH SET Exam 2026?**
No. There is no negative marking in either Paper I or Paper II. Every correct answer gets 2 marks, and wrong or unanswered questions get zero. Attempt every question even if you are unsure.

**Can I change my exam centre after applying?**
No. Once your admit card is issued, the centre is fixed. Plan travel to your allotted centre in advance. This is why choosing three realistic preferred cities during registration matters.

**How is the MH SET result calculated?**
The result is based on your combined score across both papers, computed as a percentage of total marks (300). You must clear the category aggregate threshold and then rank in the top 6 percent per subject per category.

**When will the MH SET 2026 certificate be issued?**
The digital certificate is available for download on setexam.unipune.ac.in within 4 to 8 weeks of the result declaration. It carries lifetime validity for Assistant Professor recruitment in Maharashtra and Goa.

## Official website

setexam.unipune.ac.in. Always cross-check any date or notification you see elsewhere against this official portal.

- Professional: Computer Science, Electronic Science, Library and Information Science, Physical Education, Law, Journalism and Mass Communication

You must appear in the subject that matches your post-graduation. A candidate with MA Political Science cannot appear in the Economics paper.

## Application fee for MH SET Exam 2026

| Category | Fee |
|---|---|
| General / Open | Rs. 800 |
| OBC / EWS / SBC | Rs. 650 |
| SC / ST / PwD / Third-gender | Rs. 550 |

Fees are non-refundable. Pay before June 17, 2026 to avoid rejection.

## MH SET 2026 exam centres

The exam is held at 30+ centres across Maharashtra and 2 in Goa. Popular cities include Mumbai, Pune, Nagpur, Nashik, Aurangabad, Kolhapur, Solapur, Amravati, Thane, and Panaji (Goa).

At registration, you select up to three preferred cities in order of priority. The final centre allotment is confirmed on your admit card and is generally the first or second preference. Once allotted, the centre cannot be changed. Plan travel and accommodation accordingly, especially if you are allotted a centre 2 to 3 hours from your home city.

Reporting is at the exam centre, not the university campus, so read your admit card carefully for the exact address.

## Exam day guide for MH SET 2026

The exam runs in a single sitting from 10:00 AM to 1:00 PM (Paper I from 10:00 to 11:00, Paper II from 11:00 to 1:00, no break).

- **Reach by 8:30 AM.** Gates typically close at 9:30 AM. Late entry is not allowed.
- **Carry these to the centre:** printed admit card (2 copies), a valid original photo ID (Aadhaar, PAN, Driving Licence, Passport, or Voter ID), and 2 recent passport photos matching the one uploaded.
- **What to bring for writing:** blue or black ballpoint pen only. Pencils, correction fluid, and gel pens are not allowed for OMR marking.
- **What is banned inside the hall:** mobile phones, smartwatches, Bluetooth devices, calculators, wallets, bags, printed material, and any electronic gadget. Storage outside the hall is at your own risk, so travel light.
- **Dress code:** no formal dress code, but comfortable full-sleeve clothing is recommended because centres often keep AC low. Avoid heavy metallic jewellery to speed up frisking.
- **After the exam:** you keep your admit card, not the OMR. Store your admit card safely because you will need it for the answer key objection window and any downstream correspondence.

## Reservation and category-wise cutoff mechanics

MH SET's qualifying formula has two stages, both of which must clear:

1. **Aggregate cutoff across both papers combined**: 40 percent for General, EWS, and Open category candidates; 35 percent for OBC, SC, ST, PwD, and Third-gender candidates.
2. **Top 6 percent per subject, per category**: from the pool of candidates who cleared step 1, the top 6 percent in each subject and each category are declared SET-passed.

The second stage is the actual bottleneck. A candidate scoring 45 percent may still not qualify if their subject and category pool is heavily contested, while a candidate scoring 41 percent could qualify in a less-competitive subject or category. Cutoffs are not fixed in absolute marks and are calculated post-result.

## Preparation strategy for MH SET Exam 2026

You have roughly 45 days between the last application date and the exam. That is enough time if you already know your subject well.

- Weeks 1 and 2: solve 5 years of previous year papers for Paper I. This alone tells you which topics MH SET repeats.
- Weeks 3 and 4: cover your Paper II syllabus from your PG textbooks. Do not buy a new "MH SET guide". The standard university textbooks are enough.
- Weeks 5 and 6: full-length mocks, one every alternate day. Aim for 65 percent in Paper I and 55 percent in Paper II.

Candidates who cleared past cycles most often recommend KVS Madaan (Pearson) and Rukmini Bhaya Nair for Paper I, along with the free NTA UGC-NET Paper I resource on the official portal.

## MH SET vs UGC-NET: which one should you take

| Feature | MH SET | UGC-NET |
|---|---|---|
| Conducting body | SPPU | NTA |
| Frequency | Once a year | Twice a year (June and December) |
| Valid in | Maharashtra and Goa | All Indian states |
| Certificate validity | Lifetime | Lifetime |
| Application fee | Rs. 550 to Rs. 800 | Rs. 600 to Rs. 1,150 |
| Difficulty | Moderate | Slightly higher |

Most serious aspirants attempt both. Clearing either one qualifies you for teaching in Maharashtra colleges. Clearing UGC-NET gives you national mobility.

## What happens after you clear MH SET

The MH SET certificate has lifetime validity. Once you clear, you can:

1. Apply to any Maharashtra or Goa college recruiting Assistant Professors (watch openings on collegerecruitment.mahaonline.gov.in and individual college websites).
2. Appear for university NET-cleared teaching positions.
3. Register on the government's SET-passed candidate portal for direct interview calls.

The certificate does not guarantee a job. It is a minimum eligibility filter. Actual recruitment depends on individual college interviews, which weigh subject knowledge, teaching demo, and (increasingly) research output.

## The reality of Assistant Professor recruitment after MH SET

Passing the exam is step one. Actual recruitment in Maharashtra runs on three tracks:

- **Government (aided) colleges:** highest job security and best pay (7th CPC, Rs. 57,700 to Rs. 1,82,400 entry level). Recruitment happens through college-wise notifications, but appointment is usually approved by the state Department of Higher Education. Interview panels are strict; PhD, publications, and NET/SET together are often expected.
- **Unaided private colleges:** salaries range Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 50,000 per month at entry level, sometimes lower. Fewer perks but faster hiring. Many candidates use these as a first step before moving to aided colleges.
- **Autonomous and deemed universities:** apply directly via their own recruitment portals. Selection processes vary widely and often skip the state approval step.

Publication record and PhD status matter more than raw MH SET scores in interviews. Start planning your first UGC-CARE listed paper as soon as you clear.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- Applying in the wrong subject. The subject you appear in must match your PG degree exactly. A candidate with MA Sociology cannot appear in the Political Science paper even if the syllabi overlap.
- Uploading oversized documents. The portal silently rejects photos above 100 KB. Compress before uploading.
- Missing the correction window. After June 20, no change is allowed. Verify every field before June 17 payment.
- Waiting for the "final" answer key to challenge questions. Objections must be raised during the provisional answer key window, not after.
- Skipping the mock test phase because "I know the syllabus". Time management on OMR is a distinct skill; without practice, most candidates finish Paper II 10 to 15 minutes late.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is MH SET Exam 2026 online or offline?**
MH SET Exam 2026 is a pen-and-paper (OMR) exam held at physical centres across Maharashtra and Goa on July 26, 2026. It is not a computer-based test.

**How many attempts are allowed for MH SET?**
There is no cap on the number of attempts. You can appear every year until you clear.

**What is the passing percentage for MH SET Exam 2026?**
Candidates need at least 40 percent aggregate across both papers for General category and 35 percent for reserved categories. From this qualifying pool, the top 6 percent per subject per category are declared SET-passed.

**Can final-year PG students apply for MH SET Exam 2026?**
Yes. Final-year Master's candidates can apply provisionally but must submit their mark sheet within two years of the result date.

**Is MH SET valid outside Maharashtra?**
No. MH SET is valid only in Maharashtra and Goa. For other states, either clear that state's SET (Karnataka SET, Kerala SET, and similar) or clear UGC-NET which is valid nationally.

**How do I download the MH SET 2026 admit card?**
Admit cards release in the second week of July on setexam.unipune.ac.in. Log in with your registration ID and password. Download and print two copies.

**Is there negative marking in MH SET Exam 2026?**
No. There is no negative marking in either Paper I or Paper II. Every correct answer gets 2 marks, and wrong or unanswered questions get zero. Attempt every question even if you are unsure.

**Can I change my exam centre after applying?**
No. Once your admit card is issued, the centre is fixed. Plan travel to your allotted centre in advance. This is why choosing three realistic preferred cities during registration matters.

**How is the MH SET result calculated?**
The result is based on your combined score across both papers, computed as a percentage of total marks (300). You must clear the category aggregate threshold and then rank in the top 6 percent per subject per category.

**When will the MH SET 2026 certificate be issued?**
The digital certificate is available for download on setexam.unipune.ac.in within 4 to 8 weeks of the result declaration. It carries lifetime validity for Assistant Professor recruitment in Maharashtra and Goa.

## Official website

setexam.unipune.ac.in. Always cross-check any date or notification you see elsewhere against this official portal.
