The Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission is recruiting 500 posts through the Combined State and Upper Subordinate Services Examination 2026, and the preliminary examination is on 6 December 2026. Applications ran until 3 August 2026 and the correction window closed on 10 August.

This is the exam that produces Uttar Pradesh's Sub Divisional Magistrates, Deputy Superintendents of Police and Block Development Officers. If you applied, prelims is on 6 December 2026.

## Where this recruitment stands

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Notification | 25 June 2026 |
| Vacancies | 500 |
| Application last date | 3 August 2026, closed |
| Correction window | Closed 10 August 2026 |
| Prelims | 6 December 2026 |
| Mains | Not announced |
| Stages | Prelims, Mains, Interview |
| Portal | uppsc.up.nic.in |

If you saw a figure of 200 posts or a January deadline on this page previously, both were wrong and have been corrected.

## The posts, and what the job actually is

Deputy Collector is the post most candidates are chasing. It places you in the provincial civil service on the track toward Sub Divisional Magistrate and, with promotion, eventually into the Indian Administrative Service through the state quota. The work is district administration: revenue, land, magistracy, elections, disaster response, and whatever else lands on a district officer's desk.

Deputy Superintendent of Police is the provincial police service equivalent, with promotion prospects into the Indian Police Service through the same state quota route.

Block Development Officer sits at the block level running rural development schemes, and it is the post where the largest share of candidates actually land. The work is closer to implementation than to magistracy, and it carries real authority over scheme delivery across a block.

Beyond those, the list covers Assistant Labour Commissioner, Naib Tehsildar, Sub Registrar, District Commandant Home Guard, Assistant Controller of Legal Measurement and a range of other Group A and Group B gazetted posts across departments.

The preference order you submitted matters more than most candidates treat it as mattering. Allocation follows merit rank applied strictly down your list, so ranking a post you do not want above one you do can hand you the former with no recourse.

## Prelims on 6 December

The preliminary examination has two papers, both objective, both two hours.

|---|---|

| Essay | 150 |
| General Studies I | 200 |
| General Studies II | 200 |
| General Studies III | 200 |
| General Studies IV | 200 |
| General Studies V | 200 |
| General Studies VI | 200 |
| Written total | 1500 |
| Interview | 100 |
| Grand total | 1600 |

|---|---|---|

The thing that confuses almost everyone searching for this recruitment is that the dates appear to contradict each other. One page says the exam was on 12 July 2026, another says 30 August 2026, a third gives an application deadline that has already passed. All of them can be right at once.

MPPSC is not running this as one exam. It is running it as a series of subject groups, each with its own application window, its own admit card release, and its own exam date. Your dates depend entirely on which subject you applied for. Checking a date meant for a different subject group is the single most common mistake candidates make here.

## Exam schedule by subject group

These are the batches confirmed so far. Check the one that matches your subject, and confirm on mppsc.mp.gov.in, since MPPSC has issued corrigenda revising dates more than once in this recruitment.

| Subject group | Admit card | Exam date |
|---|---|---|
| Sanskrit, Geography, Psychology, Law, Geology, Yogic Science | 2 July 2026 | 12 July 2026, at Indore |
| History, Physics, Chemistry, Botany, Mathematics and the subjects grouped with them | 29 July 2026 | 30 August 2026 |

A corrigendum dated 25 June 2026 revised the schedule for History, Physics, Chemistry, Botany and Mathematics, which is why older pages carry different dates for those subjects. If your subject is not listed above, MPPSC publishes the schedule group by group, so watch the commission's notice board rather than relying on aggregator pages.

## Application window, and the late fee structure

Applications are closed. The revised last date to apply online was 9 June 2026, and MPPSC then ran an unusual two-tier late window: applications with a late fee of Rs 3,000 were accepted from 10 to 16 June 2026, and applications with an ultra-late fee of Rs 25,000 were accepted on 17 June 2026.

That Rs 25,000 figure is not a misprint, and it is worth knowing about for the next cycle. MPPSC uses steep late fees rather than simply closing the window, which means a candidate who misses the ordinary deadline still has a route in, at a price that for most people is several months of the salary they are applying for. Apply inside the ordinary window.

The ordinary application fee was Rs 540 for General candidates and candidates from outside Madhya Pradesh, and Rs 290 for SC, ST, OBC and EWS candidates who are residents of Madhya Pradesh.

## Vacancy breakdown

The 949 posts span Arts, Commerce, Social Sciences and Science subjects. The largest allocations reported are as follows.

| Subject | Posts |
|---|---|
| Chemistry | 160 |
| Physics | 145 |
| Commerce | 94 |
| Economics | 84 |
| Geography | 74 |

The remaining posts are distributed across the other subjects, including History, Mathematics, Botany, Zoology, Sanskrit, Psychology, Law, Geology and Yogic Science. Category reservation applies within each subject as per Madhya Pradesh government rules, covering General, SC, ST, OBC and EWS.

On education, you need a Master's degree in the relevant subject with at least 55 per cent marks, or an equivalent grade, from a recognised university. Candidates in reserved categories get the usual relaxation to 50 per cent as per UGC norms.

On the eligibility test, you need to have qualified the National Eligibility Test conducted by UGC, or CSIR NET, or the State Level Eligibility Test or State Eligibility Test, including the Madhya Pradesh SLET. Candidates holding a PhD awarded in accordance with the UGC regulations are exempt from the NET requirement.

That exemption is worth reading carefully, because it is conditional rather than automatic. The PhD must have been awarded in compliance with the UGC Regulations on minimum standards and procedure for the award of the degree, which set requirements on coursework, evaluation and viva. A PhD that does not meet those conditions does not carry the exemption, and this is checked at document verification rather than at the application stage.

On age, the band is 21 to 40 years, with relaxation for reserved categories and other specified groups as per Madhya Pradesh rules. The reckoning date is set in the advertisement.

## Exam pattern

The exam is offline and OMR based, with two papers on the same day in separate sessions.

| Paper | Content | Session | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| Paper 1 | General Studies | 10:00 am to 11:00 am | 1 hour |
| Paper 2 | Subject specific | 1:00 pm to 4:00 pm | 3 hours |

## Paper 1: what General Studies covers

Paper 1 draws on the standard Madhya Pradesh state exam general studies base: Indian history with emphasis on the freedom movement, Indian and Madhya Pradesh geography, Indian polity and the Constitution, the Indian and state economy, general science and technology, current affairs at national and state level, and Madhya Pradesh specific general knowledge covering the state's districts, rivers, tribes, festivals, historical sites and current schemes.

Higher education policy topics appear as well, including the National Education Policy, UGC regulations, and the structure of higher education administration in the state, which are directly relevant to the post being filled.

For a candidate with a research background and no recent state-exam preparation, this paper needs deliberate work over a few weeks. It is a single hour of the day, but it is the part of the exam where the marginal marks are easiest to gain.

## Paper 2: the subject paper

Paper 2 tests your subject at the level expected of someone about to teach it in an undergraduate and postgraduate setting. In practice the syllabus tracks the UGC NET syllabus for the subject fairly closely, extended in places to reflect the Madhya Pradesh university curriculum.

The most efficient preparation is to work from your own postgraduate syllabus and the UGC NET syllabus for the subject together, since between them they cover almost everything MPPSC asks. Past MPPSC papers for your subject, where available, tell you which areas the commission favours, and those preferences tend to persist across cycles.

## Salary and what the post actually pays

The post is placed at Academic Level 10 of the 7th Pay Commission structure for teachers, with a pay range of Rs 57,700 to Rs 1,82,400.

Entry pay is Rs 57,700 a month as basic. Dearness allowance applies at the rate for the state, house rent allowance depends on the classification of the posting city, and transport allowance applies. Gross monthly pay at entry works out substantially above the basic figure, and the position carries the leave, medical and pension entitlements of a Madhya Pradesh government post.

Compared with the constable and clerical recruitments that dominate state hiring, this is a materially different pay bracket: entry basic here is roughly two and a half times that of a state police constable, which reflects the postgraduate and NET or PhD requirement.

## Career progression

Assistant Professor is the entry rung of the academic ladder, and progression runs through the Career Advancement Scheme rather than through a promotion exam.

| Position | Academic level |
|---|---|
| Assistant Professor (entry) | Level 10 |
| Assistant Professor (senior scale) | Level 11 |
| Assistant Professor (selection grade) | Level 12 |
| Associate Professor | Level 13A |
| Professor | Level 14 |

Movement up this ladder depends on years of service, academic performance including publications and research, refresher and orientation courses, and the screening or selection committee process laid down in the UGC regulations. Unlike a departmental promotion in an administrative service, progression here is substantially in your own hands: publication record and qualifications drive it.

## After the written exam: interview and verification

Clearing the written exam does not complete the process. Shortlisted candidates go to an interview, and then to document verification.

The interview for an academic post is not a general personality test in the way a police or administrative interview is. Expect questions on your subject, your postgraduate and doctoral work, your publications if you have any, your teaching approach, and your reasons for wanting a college post in Madhya Pradesh. Document verification is where conditional eligibility gets tested properly. The two things that fail candidates here are a Master's percentage that falls below the 55 per cent bar once the university's own conversion formula is applied rather than the candidate's estimate, and a PhD claimed for NET exemption that does not meet the UGC regulation conditions. Both are worth checking against your actual certificates now rather than assuming.

Candidates with a NET or a PhD usually have several options open at once, and they are not equivalent.

|---|---|---|---|
| MPPSC Assistant Professor | Madhya Pradesh Public Service Commission | Academic Level 10 | Written exam, interview, document verification |
| Central university Assistant Professor | Individual university | Academic Level 10 | Application screening and interview, usually no written exam |
| Other state PSC Assistant Professor | State commissions | Academic Level 10 | Varies, many use written plus interview |
| Guest or contract faculty | College or university directly | Fixed monthly rate, much lower | Interview, often local |

The pay is the same across the permanent routes, so the real difference is the selection mechanism. Central universities generally shortlist on academic record and interview, which favours candidates with strong publications. State commissions like MPPSC use a written exam, which favours candidates who prepare systematically and gives a chance to those whose research record is thinner. Guest faculty work is a different proposition entirely, paid at a fixed monthly rate well below the permanent scale and without the tenure, and it is best treated as a stopgap while pursuing the permanent routes rather than as a career.

## What to carry on exam day

Take the printed admit card and a valid original photo identity document, being an Aadhaar card, voter ID, PAN card or driving licence, along with a black or blue pen. The exam is OMR based, so the pen matters.

Mobile phones, calculators, bags, books, jewellery and electronic devices are not allowed at the centre. Centres do not always provide a waiting area, and you cannot carry a bag in, so arrange food and water for the break in advance and avoid travelling back and forth. Candidates who spend that gap anxiously reviewing Paper 1 arrive at the three-hour subject paper already tired, which is the paper that carries the weight.

The examination was scheduled for 30 August 2026. If you are preparing for a later MPPSC Assistant Professor cycle, the allocation of your final month should not be even.

Give the first stretch to Paper 1, since it is the paper you are least likely to have prepared and the one where a few weeks of focused study moves your score most. In the final week, shift to full-length practice under exam timing, since the three-hour subject paper is a stamina exercise as much as a knowledge one, and few candidates have written for three hours at a stretch since their own university exams.

|---|---|

| Grade | Post |
|---|---|
| E-1 | Junior Telecom Officer |

## What the CBT covers

Applications ran from 29 May 2026 and closed on 25 June 2026 after an extension from the original date of 18 June. Vacancy figures have been reported at various points as around 2,285, then 2,516 following an increase, and 2,587, so the position is best described as roughly 2,500 posts with the exact figure confirmed in the commission's own notices rather than in secondary reporting.

The PET is the real bottleneck. Around a lakh candidates were shortlisted here from a PET field that is far larger, so the PET determines who reaches the door and this examination determines who gets through it.

Your PET score has a validity period, and within that window it opens every UPSSSC recruitment advertised. A good PET score is therefore an asset across multiple recruitments rather than a single one, which is why it deserves serious preparation in its own right.

| Advertisement | 07-Exam/2026 |
| Applications opened | 29 May 2026 |
| Applications closed | 25 June 2026, extended from 18 June |

Applications for 11,403 Customer Service Associate posts close on 21 August 2026. IBPS opened the window on 1 August, which leaves a short runway, and the single decision that will affect your odds more than any amount of preparation has to be made inside the application form itself: which state you apply to.

This recruitment runs under the code CRP CSA-XVI. If you have been searching for "IBPS Clerk 2026" and finding inconsistent information, that is why.

## The rename from Clerk to Customer Service Associate

IBPS changed the job title for the clerical cadre to Customer Service Associate, and the recruitment is now officially the Common Recruitment Process for Customer Service Associates, abbreviated CRP-CSA. The current cycle is CRP CSA-XVI.

Older material still calls it IBPS Clerk and refers to CRP Clerks XV or earlier. The post is the same, the work is the same, and the pay scale is the same. Only the name changed. When you search for study material or previous year papers, material labelled IBPS Clerk remains valid.

The practical catch is that some sites have not updated and are still describing the previous cycle's vacancy count and dates as though they were current. Check the cycle code and the notification date on anything you read, including this page.

## Key dates

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Notification released | 1 August 2026 |
| Application window opens | 1 August 2026 |
| Application last date | 21 August 2026 |
| Prelims exam | 10 and 11 October 2026 |
| Mains exam | 27 December 2026 |
| Provisional allotment | Expected in the following financial year cycle |

The recruitment is for the 2027-28 vacancy year, which is why the gap between application and allotment is long. Candidates sometimes read the year in the notification title and conclude they have applied to the wrong cycle. You have not.

## The state choice that decides your odds

IBPS allots Customer Service Associate vacancies state by state, not as one national pool. You apply for one state or union territory only, and you compete solely against other candidates who chose that same state. You cannot change it after submission.

Two things follow from that, and most candidates underweight both.

The first is that competition varies enormously between states. A state with a large vacancy allocation and a smaller applicant base produces a lower cutoff than a state with few vacancies and heavy applicant volume. Two candidates with identical marks can get opposite results purely on the state they picked. The state-wise vacancy table sits in the annexure of the official notification PDF, and reading it before you submit is the highest-return 20 minutes in this entire process.

The second is the local language requirement. You must be proficient in the official language of the state you apply to, and IBPS verifies this. Candidates who studied the state's official language as a subject at Class 10 or Class 12 generally satisfy it through their marksheet. Everyone else faces a language proficiency test at the provisional allotment stage, and failing it cancels the candidature outright, no matter how well you scored in the Mains.

That combination is what makes the state field a binding commitment rather than a preference. Picking a state with a soft cutoff is worthless if you cannot clear its language test, and picking your home state is worthless if it has 40 vacancies and 90,000 applicants. Weigh both together before you submit, because there is no correction window for this field once the application closes.

## Eligibility

You need a bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognised university, held on the date you register. A degree expected later in the year does not qualify.

The age band is 20 to 28 years, calculated against the cutoff date stated in the notification. Standard relaxation applies: 5 years for SC and ST candidates, 3 years for OBC in the non-creamy layer, 10 years for candidates with benchmark disabilities in the unreserved category, with further relaxation stacking for reserved categories, and separate provisions for ex-servicemen and for candidates domiciled in Jammu and Kashmir during the notified period.

Computer literacy is a stated requirement. A certificate or diploma in computer operations, or having studied computing as a subject at school or degree level, covers it.

The local language proficiency requirement described above applies to the state you select.

## How to apply

Registration runs at ibps.in and closed on 21 August 2026. The process is a single online form with document uploads and an online fee payment, and there is no offline route.

Register with a working email address and mobile number, because IBPS sends the registration number and password there and every later communication, including the call letter, depends on that login. Keep the credentials somewhere you will still have them in December.

Uploads have to meet a specification: a recent photograph, a signature, a left thumb impression and a handwritten declaration, each within stated dimensions and file sizes. Rejections at this step are common and almost always avoidable. Prepare the four files before you start the form rather than scrambling mid-session.

Application fee is Rs 175 for SC, ST and candidates with disabilities, and Rs 850 for all other categories, paid online. Your application is not complete until the payment succeeds, and an incomplete payment leaves you unregistered even though the form appears filled.

Do not leave this to 21 August. The IBPS portal slows badly on the closing day of every cycle, and payment gateway failures on the final evening are a recurring complaint.

## Prelims exam pattern

| Section | Questions | Marks | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| English Language | 30 | 30 | 20 min |
| Numerical Ability | 35 | 35 | 20 min |
| Reasoning Ability | 35 | 35 | 20 min |
| Total | 100 | 100 | 60 min |

Each section is separately timed at 20 minutes and closes when that time expires. Negative marking is 0.25 marks for each wrong answer.

Prelims is a screening stage. Your marks here decide only whether you sit the Mains, and they do not carry into the final merit list. IBPS calls forward a multiple of the vacancy count in each state, which is another reason the state you chose shapes your experience of the same exam.

Sectional timing means the old habit of banking minutes from English to spend on Numerical Ability does not work. Twenty minutes for 35 numerical questions is roughly 34 seconds each, so selection matters more than speed: identify the questions you can finish quickly and leave the long calculation-heavy ones alone.

## Mains exam pattern and the reported revision

The Mains carries 200 marks across four sections: General and Financial Awareness, General English, Reasoning Ability with Computer Aptitude, and Quantitative Aptitude. The question count and duration are not. IBPS is reported to have revised the Mains pattern for this cycle, and the coverage disagrees on what the revision actually is. Some sites state 160 questions across 125 minutes. Others state 155 questions across 120 minutes. The reported section splits also differ, with Reasoning quoted at both 60 and 50 questions and Quantitative Aptitude at both 40 and 50.

The official notification PDF at ibps.in is the authority, and it is the document you should open before building a sectional time plan. Confident Mains tables published without a source are worth checking against the notification, since several currently contradict each other.

The Customer Service Associate selection has no interview stage. Prelims screens, and the Mains score alone produces the merit list and the provisional allotment.

It also means General and Financial Awareness deserves more respect than candidates usually give it. It is the one section where preparation converts to marks almost linearly, it has no time-pressure problem in the way Quantitative Aptitude does, and in an exam decided entirely on one paper, a section you can reliably bank is worth a great deal. ## Salary and what you take home

The Customer Service Associate pay scale runs from Rs 24,050 to Rs 64,480 in basic pay, with increments at defined stages. Promotion runs from Customer Service Associate to Officer Scale I through internal written examination, and then upward through the officer grades. Candidates who take the internal promotion route seriously tend to reach officer grade considerably faster than the direct-recruitment competition would allow.

Eleven public sector banks participate in this cycle. The list has shifted over the years as bank mergers consolidated the sector, so a list you find in older material may name banks that no longer exist as separate entities.

Candidates preparing for banking exams usually sit more than one, and the three most common are worth putting side by side because the preparation overlaps heavily but the selection design does not.

| | IBPS Clerk (CSA) | IBPS PO | SBI Clerk |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cadre | Clerical | Officer, Scale I | Clerical |
| Interview stage | None | Yes | None |
| Entry basic pay | Rs 24,050 | Higher, officer scale | Comparable to IBPS Clerk |
| Allotment | State-wise, one state | All India | State and circle-wise |
| Employer | 11 participating banks | Participating banks | State Bank of India only |
| Local language | Required for chosen state | Applies at allotment | Required for chosen state |

The syllabus for the written stages is close enough that preparing for one prepares you substantially for the others, so sitting several in the same year is normal and sensible. What differs is the endgame. IBPS PO adds an interview, which means a written score can be recovered or lost late. Both clerical exams end on the written paper, which front-loads all the pressure onto one day.

If you are applying to more than one, note that the exam calendar can collide and that each recruitment charges its own fee. Budget for that rather than being surprised in October.

## Call letters and what to keep

IBPS releases call letters for each stage on its portal, downloadable with the registration number and password you created during the application. They appear roughly one to two weeks before the relevant exam, and they carry the centre address, date, shift and reporting time.

Keep four things until the process ends: your registration number and password, the application form printout, the fee payment receipt, and the photograph you uploaded. You will need the same photograph at the exam centre and again at document verification, and a candidate who arrives with a visibly different photograph creates a problem that takes time to resolve. Save the whole set somewhere you will still be able to reach in December, because this recruitment runs across five months.

## A working plan up to 10 October

Prelims is on 10 and 11 October 2026. However many weeks are left when you read this, the order below holds, because it is enough time to build prelims-level speed if you use it on the right things.

Spend the first three weeks on accuracy rather than speed, working through the three prelims sections without a timer and fixing the topics where you are getting things wrong rather than slow. Speed built on a shaky method collapses under sectional timing.

Move to sectionally-timed practice for the next three weeks. Twenty-minute blocks, one section at a time, scored honestly with the 0.25 penalty applied. The goal is to learn what your realistic attempt count is per section, not to maximise attempts.

Use the final two weeks for full mocks under real conditions and for revision of your error log. Do not learn new topics in this window.

Start General and Financial Awareness for the Mains now, in parallel, at a low daily volume. It is the only part of the Mains that rewards early slow accumulation, and leaving it until after prelims results compresses it into an impossible window.

## Mistakes that cost candidates the application

Applying on the closing day. The portal slows and payment gateways fail on 21 August, and there is no extension for a failed transaction.

Choosing a state on sentiment rather than on the vacancy annexure and the language requirement together. This field cannot be corrected and it shapes your cutoff.

Assuming the local language requirement is a formality. It is verified at allotment, and failing it cancels the candidature regardless of your Mains score.

Preparing photograph, signature, thumb impression and declaration files during the form session rather than before it. Specification mismatches cause rejections that surface late.

Treating prelims marks as part of the final score. They are not. The Mains is the entire merit list.

Building a Mains time plan from an aggregator table. Sources currently contradict each other on the revised pattern. Use the notification PDF.

21 August 2026. Applications opened on 1 August 2026 at ibps.in. There is no offline route and no late window, and the fee payment must complete successfully for the application to count.

No. The selection has no interview stage. Prelims screens candidates for the Mains, and the Mains score alone decides the merit list and provisional allotment. Prelims marks do not count towards the final ranking.

**What is the age limit for IBPS Clerk 2026?**

20 to 28 years, against the cutoff date stated in the notification. Relaxation is 5 years for SC and ST, 3 years for OBC in the non-creamy layer, and 10 years for candidates with benchmark disabilities in the unreserved category, with further provisions for ex-servicemen and other notified categories.

**What is the application fee?**

Rs 175 for SC, ST and candidates with disabilities, and Rs 850 for all other categories, paid online. The application is incomplete until payment succeeds, so confirm the transaction rather than assuming it went through.

**What is the IBPS Clerk salary in 2026?**

The pay scale runs from Rs 24,050 to Rs 64,480 in basic pay. Reported in-hand pay at entry is around Rs 28,000 to Rs 32,000 per month, varying by posting city because house rent allowance is banded by city classification. The post also carries pension under the National Pension System, medical benefits and concessional staff loan rates.

**Has the IBPS Clerk mains pattern changed for 2026?**

IBPS is reported to have revised the Mains pattern, but published sources contradict each other on the detail, quoting both 160 questions across 125 minutes and 155 questions across 120 minutes, with different section splits. What is consistent: four sections, 200 marks, separate sectional timing and 0.25 negative marking. Check the official notification PDF at ibps.in before building a sectional time plan.

**Do I need to know the local language?**

Yes. You must be proficient in the official language of the state you apply to. Candidates who studied that language at Class 10 or Class 12 usually satisfy the requirement through their marksheet. Others face a language proficiency test at the provisional allotment stage, and failing it cancels the candidature.

## Official sources

- Institute of Banking Personnel Selection: https://www.ibps.in
- The CRP CSA-XVI notification PDF, which is the authority on the state-wise vacancy annexure, the Mains pattern and the language requirement
- Participating bank websites for pay scale and service condition detail

Where a figure on this page conflicts with the notification PDF, the PDF is correct. This page was written on 14 August 2026 and IBPS does amend notifications mid-cycle.

Start General and Financial Awareness for the Mains now, in parallel, at a low daily volume. It is the only part of the Mains that rewards early slow accumulation, and leaving it until after prelims results compresses it into an impossible window.

## Mistakes that cost candidates the application

Applying on the closing day. The portal slows and payment gateways fail on 21 August, and there is no extension for a failed transaction.

Choosing a state on sentiment rather than on the vacancy annexure and the language requirement together. This field cannot be corrected and it shapes your cutoff.

Assuming the local language requirement is a formality. It is verified at allotment, and failing it cancels the candidature regardless of your Mains score.

Preparing photograph, signature, thumb impression and declaration files during the form session rather than before it. Specification mismatches cause rejections that surface late.

Treating prelims marks as part of the final score. They are not. The Mains is the entire merit list.

Building a Mains time plan from an aggregator table. Sources currently contradict each other on the revised pattern. Use the notification PDF.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is the last date to apply for IBPS Clerk 2026?**

21 August 2026. Applications opened on 1 August 2026 at ibps.in. There is no offline route and no late window, and the fee payment must complete successfully for the application to count.

**How many vacancies are there in IBPS Clerk 2026?**

11,403 Customer Service Associate vacancies across 11 participating public sector banks, under the recruitment code CRP CSA-XVI. Vacancies are allotted state by state, and the state-wise breakdown is in the annexure of the official notification PDF.

**Why is IBPS Clerk now called Customer Service Associate?**

IBPS renamed the clerical cadre to Customer Service Associate, and the recruitment is officially the Common Recruitment Process for Customer Service Associates, or CRP-CSA. The post, work and pay scale are unchanged. Study material labelled IBPS Clerk is still valid.

**When are the IBPS Clerk 2026 prelims and mains exams?**

Prelims is on 10 and 11 October 2026, and the Mains is on 27 December 2026. Call letters are released on the IBPS portal ahead of each stage and are downloaded using the registration number and password created during the application.

**Can I apply for more than one state?**

No. You may apply for only one state or union territory, and the choice cannot be changed after submission. You compete only against candidates who selected the same state, and you must be proficient in that state's official language.

**Is there an interview in IBPS Clerk 2026?**

No. The selection has no interview stage. Prelims screens candidates for the Mains, and the Mains score alone decides the merit list and provisional allotment. Prelims marks do not count towards the final ranking.

**What is the age limit for IBPS Clerk 2026?**

20 to 28 years, against the cutoff date stated in the notification. Relaxation is 5 years for SC and ST, 3 years for OBC in the non-creamy layer, and 10 years for candidates with benchmark disabilities in the unreserved category, with further provisions for ex-servicemen and other notified categories.

**What is the application fee?**

Rs 175 for SC, ST and candidates with disabilities, and Rs 850 for all other categories, paid online. The application is incomplete until payment succeeds, so confirm the transaction rather than assuming it went through.

**What is the IBPS Clerk salary in 2026?**

The pay scale runs from Rs 24,050 to Rs 64,480 in basic pay. Reported in-hand pay at entry is around Rs 28,000 to Rs 32,000 per month, varying by posting city because house rent allowance is banded by city classification. The post also carries pension under the National Pension System, medical benefits and concessional staff loan rates.

**Has the IBPS Clerk mains pattern changed for 2026?**

IBPS is reported to have revised the Mains pattern, but published sources contradict each other on the detail, quoting both 160 questions across 125 minutes and 155 questions across 120 minutes, with different section splits. What is consistent: four sections, 200 marks, separate sectional timing and 0.25 negative marking. Check the official notification PDF at ibps.in before building a sectional time plan.

**Do I need to know the local language?**

Yes. You must be proficient in the official language of the state you apply to. Candidates who studied that language at Class 10 or Class 12 usually satisfy the requirement through their marksheet. Others face a language proficiency test at the provisional allotment stage, and failing it cancels the candidature.

## Official sources

- Institute of Banking Personnel Selection: https://www.ibps.in
- The CRP CSA-XVI notification PDF, which is the authority on the state-wise vacancy annexure, the Mains pattern and the language requirement
- Participating bank websites for pay scale and service condition detail

Where a figure on this page conflicts with the notification PDF, the PDF is correct. This page was written on 14 August 2026 and IBPS does amend notifications mid-cycle.

## SSC MTS 2026 at a glance

The Staff Selection Commission released the SSC MTS and Havaldar 2026 notification on 30 June 2026 for 7,948 posts, and the online application window closed on 31 July 2026. It is one of the few large central government recruitments that asks only for a Class 10 pass and has no interview stage, which is why it draws the volume it does.

The recruitment fills two post groups: Multi-Tasking (Non-Technical) Staff across central government departments, and Havaldar in the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) and the Central Bureau of Narcotics (CBN). Of the 7,948 vacancies, roughly 6,810 are MTS posts and 1,138 are Havaldar posts, per the SSC MTS 2026 notification.

One number sets the tone for how competitive this is. In the 2024 cycle SSC received well over 50 lakh applications for a similar vacancy pool, which works out to more than 600 candidates chasing each seat. The exam is Class 10 standard, but the cutoff is high precisely because the paper is easy and the field is enormous.

For candidates who have finished Class 10 and want a stable central government job without a graduation requirement or an interview, SSC MTS is one of the shortest routes in. The trade-off is that the entry pay is modest and the competition is heavy, so the difference between a seat and a near-miss usually comes down to a handful of marks in the second session. The rest of this guide covers every stage in detail, from the vacancy split and eligibility to the exam pattern, the worked in-hand salary, the cutoff trend, and how the job compares with SSC GD and CHSL.

## Important dates for SSC MTS 2026

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Notification released | 30 June 2026 |
| Online application begins | 30 June 2026 |
| Last date to apply | 31 July 2026 |
| Last date for fee payment | 31 July 2026 (11:00 PM) |
| Application correction window | Early August 2026 (per SSC notice) |
| Computer Based Test (Session I and II) | September to November 2026, per the SSC Exam Calendar |
| Age reckoned as on | 1 August 2026 |

Dates for the correction window and the exact CBT day are announced on ssc.gov.in through separate notices, so keep checking the login dashboard after you submit the form.

## Vacancy details

The 7,948 vacancies split across two age bands and the Havaldar cadre. The two MTS age groups exist because certain user departments set an 18 to 25 band while others use 18 to 27.

| Post | Age group | Approx vacancies |
|---|---|---|
| Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS) | 18 to 25 years | 6,078 |
| Multi-Tasking Staff (MTS) | 18 to 27 years | 732 |
| Havaldar (CBIC and CBN) | 18 to 27 years | 1,138 |
| Total | | 7,948 |

For context on the trend, SSC notified 7,948 posts in the 2025 cycle, 11,518 in 2024, and 11,788 in 2023, per successive SSC notifications. The count moves with departmental demand each year, so treat the 2026 figure as the confirmed number and ignore any inflated projections you see on coaching pages.

## Eligibility for SSC MTS 2026

Age limit reads off the age group you apply for. Most MTS posts need 18 to 25 years as on 1 August 2026. Havaldar and some MTS posts allow 18 to 27 years. Category relaxation follows standard government norms.

| Category | Age relaxation |
|---|---|
| OBC (non-creamy layer) | 3 years |
| SC and ST | 5 years |
| PwBD (unreserved) | 10 years |
| PwBD (OBC) | 13 years |
| PwBD (SC and ST) | 15 years |
| Ex-servicemen | As per service rules |

On qualification, the bar is a Class 10 (Matriculation) pass from a recognised board. A higher degree does not help or hurt your eligibility, and there is no minimum percentage. Nationality rules follow the usual clauses for Indian citizens plus the standard provisions for subjects of Nepal and Bhutan and Tibetan refugees who settled in India before 1962.

## Application fee

The fee is modest and waived for several categories, including all women candidates.

| Category | Fee |
|---|---|
| General, OBC, EWS | Rs 100 |
| SC, ST, PwBD, ex-servicemen | Nil |
| All women candidates | Nil |

Pay online through BHIM UPI, net banking, or a debit or credit card. There is no offline challan option in the current cycle.

## Selection process

The MTS and Havaldar selection runs on a Computer Based Test with two sessions on the same day. There is no interview and no descriptive paper.

The stages are:

1. Computer Based Test, Session I and Session II, both compulsory for every candidate.
2. Physical Efficiency Test and Physical Standard Test (PET and PST), for Havaldar applicants only. This stage is qualifying.
3. Document verification, for candidates who clear the earlier stages.

Session I carries no negative marking, which makes it a section where you attempt everything. Session II carries a penalty of 1 mark for each wrong answer, so guesswork there costs you. That single design choice decides a lot of strategy, and most candidates who miss the cutoff do so by over-attempting Session II.

## Exam pattern

Both sessions run back to back. The full paper is 90 questions for 270 marks in 90 minutes, offered in English, Hindi, and 13 regional languages.

| Session | Subject | Questions | Marks | Duration | Negative marking |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| I | Numerical and mathematical ability | 20 | 60 | 45 min | None |
| I | Reasoning ability and problem solving | 20 | 60 | 45 min | None |
| II | General awareness | 25 | 75 | 45 min | 1 mark per wrong answer |
| II | English language and comprehension | 25 | 75 | 45 min | 1 mark per wrong answer |
| Total | | 90 | 270 | 90 min | Session II only |

Candidates who use a scribe get 60 minutes per session instead of 45. Session I acts as a screening qualifier and Session II decides the merit position within your category and age group.

## Syllabus for SSC MTS 2026

The paper stays at Class 10 standard across all four subjects. Depth matters less than speed and accuracy.

Numerical and mathematical ability covers integers, LCM and HCF, decimals and fractions, BODMAS, percentage, ratio and proportion, profit and loss, simple interest, averages, time and work, time speed and distance, and basic mensuration.

Reasoning ability and problem solving covers analogies, series completion, coding and decoding, classification, non-verbal patterns, direction sense, and blood relations.

General awareness covers current affairs (usually 7 to 8 questions), biology, history, polity, geography, economics, static general knowledge, sports, and awards. This is the section that separates candidates, since it rewards steady daily reading.

English language and comprehension covers reading comprehension, grammar, vocabulary, spotting errors, sentence structure, and synonyms and antonyms.

## SSC MTS 2026 salary and in-hand pay

MTS and Havaldar posts sit at Pay Level 1 of the 7th Pay Commission, with a basic pay of Rs 18,000 and a scale of Rs 18,000 to Rs 56,900. The number that matters to you is the in-hand figure after dearness allowance, house rent allowance, and transport allowance, minus deductions.

Dearness allowance rose to 60 percent of basic pay effective 1 January 2026, per the Finance Ministry order. Many coaching pages still show a stale 17 to 50 percent DA, which understates the salary. Here is the worked in-hand pay at the current 60 percent DA, split by city class (X, Y, Z), for a Level 1 recruit.

| Component | X city (metro) | Y city | Z city |
|---|---|---|---|
| Basic pay | Rs 18,000 | Rs 18,000 | Rs 18,000 |
| Dearness allowance (60%) | Rs 10,800 | Rs 10,800 | Rs 10,800 |
| House rent allowance (30 / 20 / 10%) | Rs 5,400 | Rs 3,600 | Rs 1,800 |
| Transport allowance (with DA) | Rs 2,160 | Rs 2,160 | Rs 1,440 |
| Gross | Rs 36,360 | Rs 34,560 | Rs 32,040 |
| Deductions (NPS, CGEGIS, CGHS) | about Rs 3,200 | about Rs 3,200 | about Rs 3,100 |
| Approx in-hand | about Rs 33,200 | about Rs 31,400 | about Rs 28,900 |

So a fresh MTS recruit posted in a metro takes home roughly Rs 33,000 a month, and the figure climbs every time DA is revised. Havaldar pay sits at the same Level 1, with the added duty profile of customs and narcotics field work.

## Havaldar PET and PST standards

Havaldar applicants clear a Physical Efficiency Test and a Physical Standard Test after the CBT. This stage is qualifying, not merit-deciding, but you cannot be appointed without passing it.

| Test | Male | Female |
|---|---|---|
| PET walk | 1,600 m in 15 minutes | 1 km in 20 minutes |
| PST height | 157.5 cm | 152 cm |
| PST chest (male) | 81 cm with 5 cm expansion | Not applicable |

Height relaxations of about 5 cm for men and 2.5 cm for women apply to candidates from hill communities such as Garhwalis, Assamese, and Gorkhas, and to Scheduled Tribe candidates.

## SSC MTS cutoff trend

Cutoffs vary by category, state, and age group, and they run high because the paper is easy. As a reference point, the All India unreserved cutoff for the 18 to 25 group sat near 147.78 marks in a recent cycle, per SSC result data.

| Category | Indicative cutoff (out of 270) |
|---|---|
| Unreserved (UR) | 142 to 152 |
| OBC | 138 to 145 |
| EWS | 134 to 140 |
| SC | 128 to 138 |
| ST | 120 to 132 |

Treat these as a planning band, not a promise. Your state and age group shift the exact figure, and the 18 to 27 pool usually closes at a slightly different mark than the 18 to 25 pool.

## SSC MTS vs SSC GD vs SSC CHSL

Candidates eligible for MTS often weigh it against [SSC GD Constable](/sarkari-naukri/ssc-gd-constable-2026) and [SSC CHSL](/sarkari-naukri/ssc-chsl-2026). This comparison sets out the real differences.

| Factor | SSC MTS | SSC GD Constable | SSC CHSL |
|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum qualification | Class 10 | Class 10 | Class 12 |
| Pay Level | Level 1 (Rs 18,000) | Level 3 (about Rs 21,700) | Level 2 or 4 (Rs 19,900 to Rs 25,500) |
| Approx in-hand | Rs 29,000 to 33,000 | Rs 30,000 to 36,000 | Rs 30,000 to 40,000 |
| Nature of work | Office and support duties | Uniformed CAPF service | Clerical and data entry |
| Physical test | Havaldar posts only | Yes, for all posts | No |
| Promotion path | MTS to LDC to UDC to Section Officer | Constable to Head Constable to ASI | LDC or DEO to UDC to divisional cadre |

MTS suits candidates who want a stable desk job close to home with no physical test. SSC GD suits those ready for uniformed field service, and CHSL fits Class 12 pass candidates who want clerical roles at a slightly higher pay level.

## Career growth and promotions

An MTS recruit does not stay at Level 1. The typical ladder runs from MTS to Lower Division Clerk after about three years of service, then Upper Division Clerk, then Divisional Clerk, and up to Section Officer over a full career, with pay increments at each step. Havaldar recruits in CBIC and CBN handle field duties tied to customs checks and narcotics control, and they follow their own promotion track within those departments.

## Choosing your post and centre preference

The application form asks you to rank your post and department preferences and pick an examination centre. Two things are worth thinking about before you fill this in. First, the two MTS age bands (18 to 25 and 18 to 27) draw from different departmental vacancy pools, so your date of birth decides which posts you compete for. Second, Havaldar carries the physical test, so opt for it only if you can clear the walk and the height and chest standards, since a good CBT score is wasted if you fail the PET or PST. Pick a centre you can reach comfortably on exam day, because SSC rarely changes it once allotted, and a long commute on the morning of a two-session paper works against you.

## How to apply for SSC MTS 2026

1. Register on the SSC OTR (One Time Registration) portal at ssc.gov.in if you have not already.
2. Log in and open the SSC MTS and Havaldar 2026 application link.
3. Fill in personal, educational, and category details, and select your post preference and examination centre.
4. Upload a recent photograph and signature in the specified format.
5. Pay the Rs 100 fee if you fall in the paying category. Women and reserved categories pay nothing.
6. Submit before 31 July 2026 and save the confirmation page for your records.

## Documents required for the application

Keep these ready before you open the form, since the portal times out if you hunt for files midway.

1. A scanned passport-size photograph taken recently, in the size and format SSC specifies.
2. A scanned signature on white paper.
3. Your Class 10 certificate for the date of birth and qualification details.
4. A category certificate (OBC, SC, ST, EWS, or PwBD) if you claim relaxation.
5. Aadhaar or another government photo ID for the One Time Registration.
6. A working email and mobile number, since all admit card and result alerts go there.

## Admit card and exam day

SSC releases the admit card region by region, roughly 7 to 10 days before your CBT date, through the regional SSC website and your login dashboard. Download it, check that your name, photograph, category, and centre are correct, and carry a printout with the same photo ID you used at registration. Reach the centre early, since biometric and frisking checks take time and latecomers are turned away. Rough sheets are provided inside, and you must hand them back before leaving.

## Answer key, normalization, and result

After the CBT, SSC publishes a provisional answer key with an objection window, where you can challenge a wrong key for a small per-question fee that is refunded if your objection is upheld. Because the exam runs across many shifts and days, SSC applies normalization: your raw score is adjusted for the relative difficulty of your shift, so two candidates with the same raw marks in different shifts can end with different normalized scores. The merit list uses these normalized Session II scores within your category and age group. Keep an eye on the SSC website for the result, the marks release, and the document verification schedule, since each is announced through a separate notice.

## Building a study plan

Treat the last eight to ten weeks as a rehearsal, not a first read. Give the first half of that window to finishing every topic once and building speed on maths and reasoning, where Session I has no negative marking and rewards a full attempt. Give the second half to full-length mock tests taken at the same time of day as your slot, followed by a careful review of every wrong answer. For general awareness, a single daily current affairs source plus a static general knowledge booklet covers most of what the paper asks. English improves fastest through daily reading and a fixed set of grammar rules rather than memorising word lists. The candidates who convert this exam are rarely the ones who studied the most. They are the ones who made the fewest careless errors in Session II.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is the last date to apply for SSC MTS 2026?**
The last date to apply for SSC MTS 2026 is 31 July 2026, with fee payment also closing on the same day at 11:00 PM. The notification was released on 30 June 2026.

**How many vacancies are there in SSC MTS 2026?**
SSC MTS 2026 has 7,948 vacancies, split into roughly 6,810 Multi-Tasking Staff posts and 1,138 Havaldar posts in CBIC and CBN, per the SSC MTS 2026 notification.

**Is there negative marking in SSC MTS 2026?**
Yes, but only in Session II. General awareness and English carry a penalty of 1 mark per wrong answer, while Session I (maths and reasoning) has no negative marking, so you can attempt every question there.

**What is the in-hand salary of SSC MTS in 2026?**
A Level 1 MTS recruit takes home about Rs 33,000 a month in a metro (X city) at the 60 percent dearness allowance effective 1 January 2026, and about Rs 29,000 in a Z-class city, after standard deductions.

**What is the qualification needed for SSC MTS?**
A Class 10 (Matriculation) pass from a recognised board is the only qualification needed for SSC MTS. There is no minimum percentage and no upper degree requirement.

**Who has to appear for the PET and PST in SSC MTS?**
Only Havaldar applicants appear for the Physical Efficiency Test and Physical Standard Test. Multi-Tasking Staff posts have no physical test, and the Havaldar PET and PST are qualifying rather than merit-deciding.

**How is the SSC MTS age limit calculated?**
Age is reckoned as on 1 August 2026. Most MTS posts need 18 to 25 years, while Havaldar and some MTS posts allow 18 to 27 years, with category relaxations of 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, and up to 15 years for PwBD.

**What is the difference between MTS and Havaldar?**
MTS involves office and support duties across central government departments at Pay Level 1, while Havaldar is a field role in customs (CBIC) and narcotics control (CBN) at the same pay level, with an added physical test at selection.

## SSC MTS vs SSC GD vs SSC CHSL

Candidates eligible for MTS often weigh it against [SSC GD Constable](/sarkari-naukri/ssc-gd-constable-2026) and [SSC CHSL](/sarkari-naukri/ssc-chsl-2026). This comparison sets out the real differences.

| Factor | SSC MTS | SSC GD Constable | SSC CHSL |
|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum qualification | Class 10 | Class 10 | Class 12 |
| Pay Level | Level 1 (Rs 18,000) | Level 3 (about Rs 21,700) | Level 2 or 4 (Rs 19,900 to Rs 25,500) |
| Approx in-hand | Rs 29,000 to 33,000 | Rs 30,000 to 36,000 | Rs 30,000 to 40,000 |
| Nature of work | Office and support duties | Uniformed CAPF service | Clerical and data entry |
| Physical test | Havaldar posts only | Yes, for all posts | No |
| Promotion path | MTS to LDC to UDC to Section Officer | Constable to Head Constable to ASI | LDC or DEO to UDC to divisional cadre |

MTS suits candidates who want a stable desk job close to home with no physical test. SSC GD suits those ready for uniformed field service, and CHSL fits Class 12 pass candidates who want clerical roles at a slightly higher pay level.

## Career growth and promotions

An MTS recruit does not stay at Level 1. The typical ladder runs from MTS to Lower Division Clerk after about three years of service, then Upper Division Clerk, then Divisional Clerk, and up to Section Officer over a full career, with pay increments at each step. Havaldar recruits in CBIC and CBN handle field duties tied to customs checks and narcotics control, and they follow their own promotion track within those departments.

## Choosing your post and centre preference

The application form asks you to rank your post and department preferences and pick an examination centre. Two things are worth thinking about before you fill this in. First, the two MTS age bands (18 to 25 and 18 to 27) draw from different departmental vacancy pools, so your date of birth decides which posts you compete for. Second, Havaldar carries the physical test, so opt for it only if you can clear the walk and the height and chest standards, since a good CBT score is wasted if you fail the PET or PST. Pick a centre you can reach comfortably on exam day, because SSC rarely changes it once allotted, and a long commute on the morning of a two-session paper works against you.

## How to apply for SSC MTS 2026

1. Register on the SSC OTR (One Time Registration) portal at ssc.gov.in if you have not already.
2. Log in and open the SSC MTS and Havaldar 2026 application link.
3. Fill in personal, educational, and category details, and select your post preference and examination centre.
4. Upload a recent photograph and signature in the specified format.
5. Pay the Rs 100 fee if you fall in the paying category. Women and reserved categories pay nothing.
6. Submit before 31 July 2026 and save the confirmation page for your records.

## Documents required for the application

Keep these ready before you open the form, since the portal times out if you hunt for files midway.

1. A scanned passport-size photograph taken recently, in the size and format SSC specifies.
2. A scanned signature on white paper.
3. Your Class 10 certificate for the date of birth and qualification details.
4. A category certificate (OBC, SC, ST, EWS, or PwBD) if you claim relaxation.
5. Aadhaar or another government photo ID for the One Time Registration.
6. A working email and mobile number, since all admit card and result alerts go there.

## Admit card and exam day

SSC releases the admit card region by region, roughly 7 to 10 days before your CBT date, through the regional SSC website and your login dashboard. Download it, check that your name, photograph, category, and centre are correct, and carry a printout with the same photo ID you used at registration. Reach the centre early, since biometric and frisking checks take time and latecomers are turned away. Rough sheets are provided inside, and you must hand them back before leaving.

## Answer key, normalization, and result

After the CBT, SSC publishes a provisional answer key with an objection window, where you can challenge a wrong key for a small per-question fee that is refunded if your objection is upheld. Because the exam runs across many shifts and days, SSC applies normalization: your raw score is adjusted for the relative difficulty of your shift, so two candidates with the same raw marks in different shifts can end with different normalized scores. The merit list uses these normalized Session II scores within your category and age group. Keep an eye on the SSC website for the result, the marks release, and the document verification schedule, since each is announced through a separate notice.

## Building a study plan

Treat the last eight to ten weeks as a rehearsal, not a first read. Give the first half of that window to finishing every topic once and building speed on maths and reasoning, where Session I has no negative marking and rewards a full attempt. Give the second half to full-length mock tests taken at the same time of day as your slot, followed by a careful review of every wrong answer. For general awareness, a single daily current affairs source plus a static general knowledge booklet covers most of what the paper asks. English improves fastest through daily reading and a fixed set of grammar rules rather than memorising word lists. The candidates who convert this exam are rarely the ones who studied the most. They are the ones who made the fewest careless errors in Session II.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is the last date to apply for SSC MTS 2026?**
The last date to apply for SSC MTS 2026 is 31 July 2026, with fee payment also closing on the same day at 11:00 PM. The notification was released on 30 June 2026.

**How many vacancies are there in SSC MTS 2026?**
SSC MTS 2026 has 7,948 vacancies, split into roughly 6,810 Multi-Tasking Staff posts and 1,138 Havaldar posts in CBIC and CBN, per the SSC MTS 2026 notification.

**Is there negative marking in SSC MTS 2026?**
Yes, but only in Session II. General awareness and English carry a penalty of 1 mark per wrong answer, while Session I (maths and reasoning) has no negative marking, so you can attempt every question there.

**What is the in-hand salary of SSC MTS in 2026?**
A Level 1 MTS recruit takes home about Rs 33,000 a month in a metro (X city) at the 60 percent dearness allowance effective 1 January 2026, and about Rs 29,000 in a Z-class city, after standard deductions.

**What is the qualification needed for SSC MTS?**
A Class 10 (Matriculation) pass from a recognised board is the only qualification needed for SSC MTS. There is no minimum percentage and no upper degree requirement.

**Who has to appear for the PET and PST in SSC MTS?**
Only Havaldar applicants appear for the Physical Efficiency Test and Physical Standard Test. Multi-Tasking Staff posts have no physical test, and the Havaldar PET and PST are qualifying rather than merit-deciding.

**How is the SSC MTS age limit calculated?**
Age is reckoned as on 1 August 2026. Most MTS posts need 18 to 25 years, while Havaldar and some MTS posts allow 18 to 27 years, with category relaxations of 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, and up to 15 years for PwBD.

**What is the difference between MTS and Havaldar?**
MTS involves office and support duties across central government departments at Pay Level 1, while Havaldar is a field role in customs (CBIC) and narcotics control (CBN) at the same pay level, with an added physical test at selection.

## GATE 2027 registration, exam date, and what the score unlocks

GATE 2027 (Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering) is the single most important exam for Indian engineering graduates who want either a Master's degree from an IIT, NIT, or IIIT, or a direct-recruitment PSU job. IIT Madras is the organising institute for the 2027 cycle. Registration opened on 2 September 2026 and closes on 27 September, or 5 October with a late fee. The exam runs across six days: February 6, 7, 13, 14, 20 and 21, 2027. A valid GATE score stays valid for 3 years and is accepted by 30+ major Public Sector Undertakings including ONGC, BHEL, IOCL, GAIL, NTPC, and Power Grid.

## Important dates for GATE 2027

| Event | Date (expected) |
|---|---|
| Official notification | July 2026 |
| Registration opens | **2 September 2026** |
| Last date to apply (no late fee) | **27 September 2026** |
| Last date with late fee | **5 October 2026** |
| Correction window | Third week of October 2026 |
| Admit card release | First week of January 2027 |
| Exam dates | **February 7, 8, 14, 15, 2027** |
| Provisional answer key | Third week of February 2027 |
| Objection window | Late February 2027 |
| Result declaration | March 20, 2027 (approximate) |
| Scorecard download | Late March 2027 |
| Score validity | 3 years from result date |

Cross-check every date on gate.iitm.ac.in once the official notification is released.

## How to apply for GATE 2027 step by step

Applications happen only online at gate.iitm.ac.in through the GOAPS (GATE Online Application Processing System) portal.

1. Visit gate.iitm.ac.in and click the GOAPS registration link.
2. Register with your name, date of birth, email, and mobile number. You receive an enrolment ID.
3. Log in with the enrolment ID and fill personal details, academic qualification, paper choice, and 3 preferred exam cities.
4. Upload photograph (200 KB max, JPEG), signature (150 KB max, JPEG), category certificate (if applicable), and PwD certificate (if applicable). Format specifics are on the portal.
5. Pay the application fee online via UPI, net banking, debit card, or credit card.
6. Download the submitted application PDF for your records. Print two copies before the exam day.

If you want to appear in two papers, both must be listed in the official allowed-combination list. Second paper choice is available at the time of application, and the fee doubles.

## Eligibility for GATE 2027

You are eligible if you are in the final year of, or have already completed, any of the following:

- 4-year B.Tech, BE, B.Pharm, or equivalent
- 5-year integrated dual degree (BS + MS or B.Tech + M.Tech)
- MSc, MCA, MA in relevant disciplines (for corresponding GATE papers)
- 3-year B.Sc followed by 2-year M.Sc (must be in the final year of M.Sc)

There is no upper age limit and no cap on the number of attempts. You can appear every year until you clear or get a rank you are happy with.

### Three quick worked examples

- **Rohit, final-year B.Tech Computer Science**: eligible for GATE 2027 CS paper. He can also target the DA (Data Science and AI) paper as a second choice.
- **Priya, MSc Chemistry, cleared 2025**: eligible. She can appear in the CY (Chemistry) paper. Her BSc marks do not affect eligibility.
- **Rahul, 3rd-year integrated dual degree**: not eligible for 2027. He must complete or reach the final year of his integrated programme.

## GATE 2027 papers list

GATE 2027 offers 30 discipline-specific papers. The most popular ones by candidate count are:

**Engineering streams**
- CS: Computer Science and Information Technology
- EC: Electronics and Communication Engineering
- EE: Electrical Engineering
- ME: Mechanical Engineering
- CE: Civil Engineering
- CH: Chemical Engineering
- IN: Instrumentation Engineering
- BT: Biotechnology
- MT: Metallurgical Engineering
- AE: Aerospace Engineering
- AG: Agricultural Engineering
- MN: Mining Engineering
- PE: Petroleum Engineering
- PI: Production and Industrial Engineering
- TF: Textile Engineering and Fibre Science

**Science and interdisciplinary**
- DA: Data Science and Artificial Intelligence
- ST: Statistics
- MA: Mathematics
- PH: Physics
- CY: Chemistry
- XE: Engineering Sciences (multi-section)
- XL: Life Sciences (multi-section)
- ES: Environmental Science and Engineering
- GG: Geology and Geophysics
- EY: Ecology and Evolution

**Humanities**
- XH: Humanities and Social Sciences (multi-section)
- AR: Architecture and Planning

You can appear in one or two papers, subject to the allowed-combination list published every year.

## GATE 2027 exam pattern and marking

Each paper is a 3-hour computer-based test with 65 questions and 100 total marks. The paper structure:

- General Aptitude (GA): 10 questions, 15 marks (compulsory across all papers)
- Core subject: 55 questions, 85 marks
- Question types: Multiple Choice Questions (MCQ), Multiple Select Questions (MSQ), Numerical Answer Type (NAT)

Marking scheme:
- MCQ: 1 or 2 marks correct, 1/3 or 2/3 negative for wrong answers.
- MSQ: 1 or 2 marks correct, no negative marking.
- NAT: 1 or 2 marks correct, no negative marking. You type the answer directly.

There is a mandatory virtual calculator on screen. Physical calculators are not allowed.

## Preparation strategy for GATE 2027

GATE 2027 is in February 2027. The timeline below assumes a twelve-month run at it, which is what a candidate starting in early 2026 had. Compress each phase proportionally if you are starting later.

**Months 1 to 4 (July to October 2026): concept building**
- Complete standard textbooks for your subject syllabus (see book list below).
- Solve every solved example. Aim for 60 percent problem-solving accuracy at the end of this phase.
- Give one topic-wise quiz every week to check retention.

**Months 5 to 8 (November 2026 to February 2027): problem-solving intensity**
- Move to previous year GATE papers, 10 to 15 years back.
- Solve at least 5 previous year papers per week under timed conditions.
- Maintain an error notebook. Common mistakes will start repeating.
- Start attempting full-length mock tests, one every two weeks.

**Wait, this timeline overlaps with the exam. If you started in July 2026, the compressed version is:**

**Months 1 to 6 (July to December 2026): concept + problem solving overlap**
- Blend concept building with previous year practice. Do not wait for concepts to finish before starting practice.

**Months 7 to 8 (January to February 2027): full mocks + revision**
- Full-length mock test every alternate day.
- Aim for 55 to 65 marks in mocks. That range typically translates to 800+ score in the actual exam.
- Revise your error notebook thoroughly. Do not learn new topics in the last month.

For repeaters, the 6-month version is: months 1 to 3 for revision and error correction, months 4 to 6 for intensive mock tests and previous year papers.

## Recommended books by subject

**General Aptitude (all papers)**
- R.S. Aggarwal Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning for baseline concepts.
- Made Easy GA workbook for GATE-specific practice.

**Computer Science (CS paper)**
- Cormen (CLRS) for algorithms, Silberschatz for DBMS, Tanenbaum for operating systems, and Made Easy handwritten notes for a quick revision layer.

**Mechanical Engineering (ME paper)**
- Made Easy notes cover 80 percent. Supplement with S.K. Mondal notes for thermodynamics.

**Electrical Engineering (EE paper)**
- Made Easy notes and RK Rajput textbook combination. Ace Academy notes are strong for power systems.

**Civil Engineering (CE paper)**
- Made Easy notes and B.C. Punmia textbook for structural analysis and geotechnical engineering.

**Electronics and Communication (EC paper)**
- Kanodia previous year solved book plus Ace Academy or Made Easy notes.

For all subjects, the single most important book is the previous year GATE papers with detailed solutions. Kanodia or Made Easy publishes the best-known compilations.

## PSU recruitment through GATE 2027

A valid GATE score is accepted by these PSUs for direct executive-level recruitment. Starting salaries typically fall in the ₹50,000 to ₹1,00,000 per month range depending on the PSU and posting.

| PSU | Starting salary (approx per month) | Typical GATE cutoff percentile |
|---|---|---|
| ONGC (Oil and Natural Gas Corporation) | ₹70,000 to ₹95,000 | 95+ percentile |
| BHEL (Bharat Heavy Electricals) | ₹60,000 to ₹80,000 | 90+ percentile |
| IOCL (Indian Oil Corporation) | ₹75,000 to ₹1,00,000 | 96+ percentile |
| GAIL (Gas Authority of India) | ₹70,000 to ₹90,000 | 94+ percentile |
| NTPC (National Thermal Power) | ₹65,000 to ₹85,000 | 90+ percentile |
| PGCIL (Power Grid Corporation) | ₹70,000 to ₹90,000 | 92+ percentile |
| BEL (Bharat Electronics) | ₹60,000 to ₹80,000 | 88+ percentile |
| HPCL (Hindustan Petroleum) | ₹70,000 to ₹95,000 | 94+ percentile |
| BPCL (Bharat Petroleum) | ₹72,000 to ₹95,000 | 94+ percentile |
| NHPC (National Hydroelectric Power) | ₹60,000 to ₹80,000 | 88+ percentile |

PSU application windows open shortly after GATE results (March to May 2027). Each PSU publishes its own advertisement and cutoff. You apply separately to each PSU using your GATE registration ID and score.

## M.Tech admissions through GATE 2027

Two parallel counselling processes run after the GATE result.

**COAP for IITs**: The Common Offer Acceptance Portal is used by all IITs for M.Tech admissions. You register at coap.iitm.ac.in after the GATE result. Each IIT publishes offers based on your GATE score and interview. You accept or reject offers in rounds.

**CCMT for NITs and IIITs**: The Centralized Counselling for M.Tech is used by all NITs, IIITs, and select GFTIs. Registration happens at ccmt.admissions.nic.in. Seat allotment is based on GATE score, category, and choice-filling.

Both processes typically run May through July 2027.

## GATE cutoff trends by branch

Approximate qualifying GATE 2025 cutoff scores by branch (out of 100 marks) for general category:

- Computer Science (CS): 26.28
- Electronics (EC): 25.4
- Electrical (EE): 25.2
- Mechanical (ME): 28.6
- Civil (CE): 28.3
- Chemical (CH): 25.0

Cutoffs vary by 2 to 4 points year over year. The qualifying score is separate from the M.Tech admission cutoff (which is usually much higher, 55+ marks) and PSU cutoff (which is typically 60+ marks).

## Application fee for GATE 2027

| Category | Regular fee | Late fee |
|---|---|---|
| Female / SC / ST / PwD | ₹900 | ₹1,400 |
| All others | ₹1,800 | ₹2,300 |

Fees are non-refundable. If you appear in two papers, the fee doubles for each category.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- Choosing the wrong paper. Your paper choice must match your undergraduate discipline, otherwise the syllabus overlap is minimal and preparation becomes twice as hard.
- Skipping previous year papers. Every serious GATE aspirant solves at least 10 years of previous papers. Skipping this step is the single biggest reason for low ranks.
- Ignoring General Aptitude. 15 marks are up for grabs from GA, and it is the easiest section. Aspirants who skip GA lose 12 to 15 easy marks.
- Overusing coaching material and skipping textbooks. Standard textbooks build concepts. Coaching notes are best used as revision layers, not primary sources.
- Applying to PSUs late. PSU advertisements go up quickly after GATE results. Set alerts on the official career pages of ONGC, IOCL, BHEL, and PGCIL by early March 2027.

## Frequently asked questions

**When is GATE 2027 exam date?**
GATE 2027 will be held on February 7, 8, 14, and 15, 2027, in a computer-based test format across two sessions per day. Confirm your specific date and slot from your admit card in January 2027.

**How many times can I appear for GATE?**
There is no limit on the number of attempts. You can appear in GATE every year for as long as you meet the eligibility criteria. Each attempt is independent.

**Is GATE 2027 syllabus different from GATE 2026?**
GATE syllabus changes are extremely rare, and any change is announced with the official notification. IIT Madras is expected to keep the 2026 syllabus with minor topic-level updates. Confirm from the official notification in July 2026.

**Can I do M.Tech from IIT with just a GATE qualifying score?**
No. IIT M.Tech admissions typically require a GATE score in the top 20 percent of your paper's candidates, plus an interview or written test at the IIT. The qualifying cutoff is only the minimum to be considered.

**What is the difference between qualifying score and admission cutoff?**
The qualifying score is the minimum GATE score needed to be considered "GATE qualified". The admission cutoff at IITs and PSUs is typically much higher. For example, CS qualifying score is around 26, but IIT M.Tech admission usually needs 55+ marks.

**Which PSU pays the highest starting salary through GATE?**
As of the 2026 recruitment cycle, IOCL, HPCL, and ONGC offered the highest starting salaries, generally in the ₹75,000 to ₹1,00,000 per month range including basic pay, DA, and location allowances.

**Can I appear in two GATE papers?**
Yes, but both must be in the official allowed-combination list published every year. Common combinations include CS with DA, and ME with XE. You pay the application fee for both papers.

**Is a virtual calculator available in the GATE exam?**
Yes. A virtual scientific calculator is available on the exam screen for every paper. Physical calculators are not allowed inside the exam hall.

## Official website

gate.iitm.ac.in. Always cross-check any date, syllabus, or eligibility detail you see elsewhere against this official portal.

PSU application windows open shortly after GATE results (March to May 2027). Each PSU publishes its own advertisement and cutoff. You apply separately to each PSU using your GATE registration ID and score.

## M.Tech admissions through GATE 2027

Two parallel counselling processes run after the GATE result.

**COAP for IITs**: The Common Offer Acceptance Portal is used by all IITs for M.Tech admissions. You register at coap.iitm.ac.in after the GATE result. Each IIT publishes offers based on your GATE score and interview. You accept or reject offers in rounds.

**CCMT for NITs and IIITs**: The Centralized Counselling for M.Tech is used by all NITs, IIITs, and select GFTIs. Registration happens at ccmt.admissions.nic.in. Seat allotment is based on GATE score, category, and choice-filling.

Both processes typically run May through July 2027.

## GATE cutoff trends by branch

Approximate qualifying GATE 2025 cutoff scores by branch (out of 100 marks) for general category:

- Computer Science (CS): 26.28
- Electronics (EC): 25.4
- Electrical (EE): 25.2
- Mechanical (ME): 28.6
- Civil (CE): 28.3
- Chemical (CH): 25.0

Cutoffs vary by 2 to 4 points year over year. The qualifying score is separate from the M.Tech admission cutoff (which is usually much higher, 55+ marks) and PSU cutoff (which is typically 60+ marks).

## Application fee for GATE 2027

| Category | Regular fee | Late fee |
|---|---|---|
| Female / SC / ST / PwD | ₹900 | ₹1,400 |
| All others | ₹1,800 | ₹2,300 |

Fees are non-refundable. If you appear in two papers, the fee doubles for each category.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- Choosing the wrong paper. Your paper choice must match your undergraduate discipline, otherwise the syllabus overlap is minimal and preparation becomes twice as hard.
- Skipping previous year papers. Every serious GATE aspirant solves at least 10 years of previous papers. Skipping this step is the single biggest reason for low ranks.
- Ignoring General Aptitude. 15 marks are up for grabs from GA, and it is the easiest section. Aspirants who skip GA lose 12 to 15 easy marks.
- Overusing coaching material and skipping textbooks. Standard textbooks build concepts. Coaching notes are best used as revision layers, not primary sources.
- Applying to PSUs late. PSU advertisements go up quickly after GATE results. Set alerts on the official career pages of ONGC, IOCL, BHEL, and PGCIL by early March 2027.

## Frequently asked questions

**When is GATE 2027 exam date?**
GATE 2027 will be held on February 7, 8, 14, and 15, 2027, in a computer-based test format across two sessions per day. Confirm your specific date and slot from your admit card in January 2027.

**How many times can I appear for GATE?**
There is no limit on the number of attempts. You can appear in GATE every year for as long as you meet the eligibility criteria. Each attempt is independent.

**Is GATE 2027 syllabus different from GATE 2026?**
GATE syllabus changes are extremely rare, and any change is announced with the official notification. IIT Madras is expected to keep the 2026 syllabus with minor topic-level updates. Confirm from the official notification in July 2026.

**Can I do M.Tech from IIT with just a GATE qualifying score?**
No. IIT M.Tech admissions typically require a GATE score in the top 20 percent of your paper's candidates, plus an interview or written test at the IIT. The qualifying cutoff is only the minimum to be considered.

**What is the difference between qualifying score and admission cutoff?**
The qualifying score is the minimum GATE score needed to be considered "GATE qualified". The admission cutoff at IITs and PSUs is typically much higher. For example, CS qualifying score is around 26, but IIT M.Tech admission usually needs 55+ marks.

**Which PSU pays the highest starting salary through GATE?**
As of the 2026 recruitment cycle, IOCL, HPCL, and ONGC offered the highest starting salaries, generally in the ₹75,000 to ₹1,00,000 per month range including basic pay, DA, and location allowances.

**Can I appear in two GATE papers?**
Yes, but both must be in the official allowed-combination list published every year. Common combinations include CS with DA, and ME with XE. You pay the application fee for both papers.

**Is a virtual calculator available in the GATE exam?**
Yes. A virtual scientific calculator is available on the exam screen for every paper. Physical calculators are not allowed inside the exam hall.

## Official website

gate.iitm.ac.in. Always cross-check any date, syllabus, or eligibility detail you see elsewhere against this official portal.
