Every year, millions of farmers across India receive ₹6,000 directly in their bank accounts through **PM Kisan Samman Nidhi** — no middlemen, no paperwork after registration, no trips to a government office. The money just arrives.

But here's the thing — many eligible farmers either don't know they qualify, haven't completed the eKYC step, or are confused about why their installment didn't come. If you're a farmer or helping a farmer in your family, this guide covers everything you need to know about PM Kisan in 2026.

---

## What is PM Kisan Samman Nidhi?

**PM Kisan Samman Nidhi** (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi) is a central government scheme that gives **₹6,000 per year** to small and marginal farmers across India. The money is transferred in **3 equal installments of ₹2,000 each**, directly into the farmer's Aadhaar-linked bank account.

| Detail | Info |
|--------|------|
| **Annual Benefit** | ₹6,000 (₹2,000 × 3 installments) |
| **Transfer Method** | Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) to bank account |
| **Installment Schedule** | April–July, August–November, December–March |
| **Official Website** | pmkisan.gov.in |
| **Launched** | December 2018 |

Since its launch, the scheme has transferred crores of rupees to farmers across every state in India. It's one of the largest direct cash transfer programmes in the world.

---

## Who is Eligible for PM Kisan?

Before checking your status or applying, make sure you actually qualify. Here's who is eligible:

**You ARE eligible if:**
- You are a small or marginal farmer
- Your family owns cultivable land (any amount — the 2 hectare limit was removed in 2019)
- You have an Aadhaar card
- You have a bank account linked to Aadhaar
- Your name appears in the land records of your state

**You are NOT eligible if:**
- You or your spouse holds a constitutional post (President, Minister, MP, MLA, etc.)
- You are a current or retired government employee (Central or State) drawing a pension above ₹10,000/month
- You are an income tax payer
- You are a professional (doctor, lawyer, CA, engineer) registered with a professional body
- You are a retired officer or employee of Central/State PSUs and autonomous bodies

If you're a regular farmer with land in your name and none of the above applies — you qualify.

---

## How to Check PM Kisan Payment Status (Step by Step)

If you're already registered and want to check whether your installment has been released or credited:

**Step 1** — Go to the official website: **pmkisan.gov.in**

**Step 2** — On the homepage, look for **"Farmer Corner"** section (usually in the middle or top-right of the page)

**Step 3** — Click on **"Beneficiary Status"**

**Step 4** — Enter any one of the following:
- Aadhaar Number, OR
- Account Number, OR
- Mobile Number

**Step 5** — Click **"Get Data"**

You will see your installment history — which installments were sent, which were credited to your account, and the dates of transfer.

### What the Status Means

| Status Shown | What it Means |
|-------------|---------------|
| **FTO is Generated and Payment Confirmation is Pending** | Money is on its way, not yet in your account |
| **Rft Signed** | File approved, payment will be processed soon |
| **Payment Released** | Money has been sent to your bank |
| **Payment Credited** | Money is in your bank account |
| **Beneficiary Not Found** | Name not in PM Kisan database — need to register |

---

## How to Check Your Name in the Beneficiary List

Want to confirm you're in the official list for your village or district?

1. Go to **pmkisan.gov.in**
2. Click **"Farmer Corner"** → **"Beneficiary List"**
3. Select your **State → District → Sub-District → Block → Village**
4. Click **"Get Report"**

A full list of registered farmers in your village will appear. If your name is there, you're registered. If not, you need to apply.

---

## How to Register for PM Kisan (New Registration)

If you're eligible but not yet registered, here's how to apply:

### Option 1 — Online (Self Registration)

1. Go to **pmkisan.gov.in**
2. Click **"Farmer Corner"** → **"New Farmer Registration"**
3. Choose **Rural Farmer** or **Urban Farmer**
4. Enter your **Aadhaar Number** and **Mobile Number**
5. Complete OTP verification
6. Fill in your personal details — name, father's name, date of birth, gender, category
7. Enter your **bank account details** (account number, IFSC code)
8. Enter your **land details** — survey number, khasra number, area in hectares
9. Submit the form

### Option 2 — Through CSC Centre

If you're not comfortable doing it online, visit your nearest **Common Service Centre (CSC)** or **Gram Panchayat** office. Bring:
- Aadhaar card
- Bank passbook (showing account number and IFSC)
- Land record / Khasra-Khatauni document
- Mobile number linked to Aadhaar

The CSC operator will register you at a nominal charge (usually ₹0 — it's a free service).

---

## eKYC — Why Your Installment May Be Stuck

This is the most common reason farmers miss their PM Kisan installments in 2026.

**eKYC is mandatory.** If you haven't completed eKYC, your installment will be held even if you're a registered beneficiary. The government made this compulsory to remove fake beneficiaries from the system.

### How to Complete PM Kisan eKYC

**Method 1 — OTP-based (Online)**
1. Go to **pmkisan.gov.in** → **"Farmer Corner"** → **"eKYC"**
2. Enter your Aadhaar number
3. An OTP will be sent to the mobile number linked to your Aadhaar
4. Enter the OTP and submit

*This works only if your mobile number is linked to Aadhaar.*

**Method 2 — Biometric (at CSC Centre)**
1. Visit the nearest CSC centre
2. Carry your Aadhaar card
3. The operator will do fingerprint/iris biometric verification
4. eKYC will be completed on the spot

If your mobile is not linked to Aadhaar, go to the CSC centre — biometric eKYC doesn't require a linked mobile.

---

## How to Update Bank Account or Mobile Number

Made a mistake in your bank details? Changed your mobile number? Here's how to fix it:

**To update bank account:**
1. Visit your nearest **PM Kisan nodal officer** at the Block or Tehsil level
2. Or raise a query through the PM Kisan helpline: **155261 / 1800115526** (toll-free)
3. Correction requests can also be submitted at the CSC centre

**To update Aadhaar-linked mobile number:**
Visit your nearest **Aadhaar enrolment centre** (post office or bank) to update the mobile number in your Aadhaar — that will automatically fix the OTP issue for eKYC.

---

## Land Seeding — Another Common Reason for Rejection

Many farmers registered correctly but their installments were stopped because of **land seeding failure** — meaning the land records in the scheme database don't match the state's land records (Bhulekh).

If your status shows **"Land Seeding Pending"**:
1. Visit your **Lekhpal / Patwari** (revenue officer) at the village or block level
2. They are authorised to seed your land records with the PM Kisan portal
3. Once seeded and verified, your pending installments will be released

This is a process that requires offline intervention — you can't fix it online yourself.

---

## PM Kisan Installment Schedule 2026

| Installment | Period | Approximate Release |
|-------------|--------|---------------------|
| 1st Installment | December – March | April 2026 |
| 2nd Installment | April – July | August 2026 |
| 3rd Installment | August – November | December 2026 |

The government typically announces the installment release with a formal event. Keep an eye on news and the official PM Kisan portal for exact dates.

---

## Common Problems & Quick Fixes

| Problem | Likely Cause | Solution |
|---------|-------------|----------|
| Installment not received | eKYC not done | Complete eKYC on pmkisan.gov.in |
| Name not in beneficiary list | Not registered | Do new registration at CSC or online |
| Payment sent but not in bank | Bank account details wrong | Contact nodal officer or helpline |
| Status shows "Rejected" | Land records mismatch | Visit Patwari / Lekhpal for land seeding |
| OTP not received for eKYC | Mobile not linked to Aadhaar | Go to CSC for biometric eKYC |
| Registered but no installment for 2+ years | Account may be frozen | Visit your bank branch and unfreeze it |

---

## PM Kisan Helpline & Contact

If you're stuck and can't resolve the issue online, reach out directly:

- **PM Kisan Helpline:** 155261 or 1800115526 *(toll-free)*
- **Email:** pmkisan-ict@gov.in
- **Official Website:** pmkisan.gov.in
- **PM Kisan App:** Available on Google Play Store — search "PM Kisan Mobile App"

The helpline is available on working days and the staff can help you check your status, raise correction requests, and guide you on eKYC issues.

---

## Is ₹6,000/Year Enough?

Honestly? No — ₹6,000 a year barely covers seed costs for one crop season. But that's not really the point of PM Kisan. It was designed as a **supplementary income** to ease the cash flow pressure that farmers face between harvests, not to replace farm income entirely.

What matters is that it's **guaranteed, direct, and consistent**. For millions of small farmers in India, having ₹2,000 arrive in April, August, and December — without asking anyone for anything — has made a real difference.

If you qualify, make sure you're getting it.

---

*Last updated: June 2026. The PM Kisan scheme details are based on official government guidelines. Visit pmkisan.gov.in for the most current information and installment dates.*

---

Medical emergencies have a way of arriving without warning — and in India, a single major hospitalisation can wipe out years of savings. That's the exact problem **Ayushman Bharat** was built to solve.

If your family is eligible, you get **₹5 lakh per year in health coverage** — completely free. No premium. No paperwork at the hospital. Just walk in, show your card, and get treated.

But here's the problem: millions of eligible families still haven't claimed their card. Some don't know they qualify. Some got confused by the process and gave up. This guide will walk you through everything — checking eligibility, applying, downloading the card, and actually using it when you need it.

---

## What is Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY?

**Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY)** is the world's largest government-funded health insurance scheme. Launched in 2018, it provides:

- **₹5 lakh health cover** per family per year
- **Cashless treatment** at government and private empanelled hospitals
- Coverage for **1,929+ medical procedures** including surgery, ICU, chemotherapy, dialysis, and more
- **Pre and post hospitalisation** expenses covered (up to 3 days before and 15 days after)
- **No cap on family size** — the entire family is covered under one card
- **Portable across India** — use it in any empanelled hospital anywhere in the country

| Detail | Info |
|--------|------|
| **Annual Coverage** | ₹5 lakh per family |
| **Premium** | Zero — completely free for beneficiaries |
| **Beneficiaries** | ~55 crore people (about 12 crore families) |
| **Official Website** | pmjay.gov.in / beneficiary.nha.gov.in |
| **Helpline** | 14555 (toll-free) |

This is not a reimbursement scheme — you don't pay and claim later. Treatment is **cashless at the hospital** from day one.

---

## Who is Eligible for Ayushman Bharat?

Eligibility is based on the **Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) 2011** data and state government lists. You don't apply for eligibility — either your family is already in the list, or it isn't.

### Automatically Eligible (Rural Families)

If your family falls into any of these categories in the SECC data, you're likely eligible:

- Families with no permanent house (living in kutcha house with one room)
- Families with no adult member aged 16–59
- Female-headed households with no adult male member aged 16–59
- Families with a disabled member and no able-bodied adult earner
- SC/ST households
- Landless agricultural labourers with manual casual labour as primary income

### Automatically Eligible (Urban Families)

Urban workers in these occupations are covered:

- Rag pickers, beggars, domestic workers
- Street vendors, cobblers, hawkers
- Construction workers, plumbers, masons, painters
- Washermen, sanitation workers, sweepers
- Home-based artisans, handicraft workers
- Transport workers — drivers, conductors, helpers
- Shop workers, delivery assistants, peons, security guards

### Also Covered

- All **RSBY (Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana)** beneficiaries are included
- Many **state governments** have extended coverage beyond SECC — check your state's merged scheme (e.g., Maharashtra's Mahatma Jyotirao Phule Jan Arogya Yojana, Delhi's merged scheme)

---

## Step 1 — Check If You Are Eligible

Before applying for the card, first verify your eligibility.

**Online Method:**
1. Go to **pmjay.gov.in**
2. Click **"Am I Eligible?"**
3. Enter your mobile number → get OTP → verify
4. Enter your **State**, then search by:
   - Name + Date of Birth + Mobile
   - Name + Mobile Number
   - Name + Ration Card Number
   - RSBY URN Number
5. If your family is in the database, it will show your details

**By Calling:**
- Call **14555** (toll-free) and ask if your name is in the PM-JAY beneficiary list

**At the Hospital:**
- Any Ayushman Mitra (help desk) at an empanelled hospital can check your eligibility for free

If your name appears — great, move to the next step. If not, check whether your state has its own extended scheme that might cover you.

---

## Step 2 — How to Apply and Get the Ayushman Bharat Card

Getting the card is straightforward. You don't need to fill long forms or submit documents at a government office.

### Method 1 — Ayushman App (Easiest)

1. Download **"Ayushman App"** from the Google Play Store
2. Open the app → click **"Beneficiary"**
3. Log in with your **Aadhaar-linked mobile number**
4. Verify with OTP
5. Your family details and eligibility will appear
6. Select your name → click **"Download Card"**
7. Complete **eKYC** — either OTP-based (if mobile linked to Aadhaar) or face authentication via the app camera
8. Your Ayushman card is generated and ready to download

### Method 2 — Common Service Centre (CSC)

1. Visit your nearest **CSC / Jan Seva Kendra**
2. Carry: Aadhaar card + Ration card (if available) + Mobile number
3. The operator will verify your eligibility and complete biometric eKYC
4. The card is printed on the spot or sent to your registered mobile

### Method 3 — Empanelled Hospital Help Desk

Every empanelled hospital has an **Ayushman Mitra** — a dedicated help desk. You can:
1. Walk in and ask the Ayushman Mitra to check your eligibility
2. If eligible, they'll complete the eKYC and generate your card right there
3. This is particularly useful if you need treatment urgently and don't have the card yet

---

## Step 3 — How to Download Your Ayushman Card Online

If you're already registered and just need to download or reprint your card:

1. Go to **beneficiary.nha.gov.in**
2. Click **"Login"** → select **"Beneficiary"**
3. Enter your **Aadhaar-linked mobile number**
4. Verify with OTP
5. Your family member list will appear
6. Click on your name → **"Download Card"**
7. Complete face authentication or OTP verification
8. The card downloads as a PDF — save it and print it

The card has your name, photo, Ayushman ID, and a QR code. Keep a printed copy *and* a photo on your phone — hospitals accept both.

---

## What Does the Ayushman Card Cover?

The scheme covers a wide range of medical procedures across **1,929 packages**. Here's a broad look at what's included:

### Covered 
- **Surgery** — heart surgery, knee replacement, hip replacement, cataract, appendix, hernia, and more
- **Cancer treatment** — chemotherapy, radiation, surgery
- **Dialysis** — kidney failure treatment covered per session
- **ICU and ventilator** charges
- **Maternity and newborn care** — delivery, C-section, neonatal ICU
- **Mental health** hospitalisation
- **COVID-19** treatment (as per government guidelines)
- **Pre-hospitalisation** diagnostics (up to 3 days before admission)
- **Post-hospitalisation** follow-up (up to 15 days after discharge)
- **Medicines and consumables** during hospitalisation
- **Transport allowance** — ₹100 to ₹300 per visit (in some states)

### Not Covered 
- **OPD (Outpatient)** consultations — routine doctor visits are not covered
- **Cosmetic surgery** unless medically required
- **Dental procedures** (unless from injury/accident)
- **Drug de-addiction** treatment
- **Organ transplant** (donor costs)
- **Fertility treatments**
- Procedures not in the approved 1,929 package list

---

## How to Use the Card at a Hospital

This is where most people get confused. Here's exactly what happens when you go to a hospital with your Ayushman card:

**Step 1** — Find an **empanelled hospital** (government or private). Search on pmjay.gov.in → "Find Hospital" or use the Ayushman app.

**Step 2** — Go to the hospital's **Ayushman Mitra desk** (not the regular reception — look for the specific PM-JAY help desk).

**Step 3** — Show your **Ayushman card** (printed or on phone) + **Aadhaar card**.

**Step 4** — The Ayushman Mitra scans your card, verifies your identity via OTP or biometric, and checks the procedure you need is covered.

**Step 5** — If approved, you are **admitted as a cashless patient**. You pay nothing — not for the bed, surgery, medicines, or doctor fees (within the scheme limits).

**Step 6** — At discharge, the hospital directly claims reimbursement from the government. You walk out without paying a bill.

**Important:** Always insist on going to the Ayushman Mitra desk first. Some hospital staff at the general reception may not be aware of the process or may direct you to pay first. The Ayushman Mitra is specifically trained to handle PM-JAY cases.

---

## How to Find Empanelled Hospitals Near You

Not every hospital accepts the Ayushman card — only **empanelled** ones do.

1. Go to **pmjay.gov.in** → **"Find Hospital"**
2. Select your **State → District → Speciality**
3. A list of empanelled hospitals with their address and contact will appear

You can also call **14555** and ask for empanelled hospitals near your location.

In most districts, government hospitals (District Hospital, CHC, PHC) are empanelled by default. Private hospitals vary — always confirm before going.

---

## Common Problems & How to Fix Them

| Problem | Likely Cause | Solution |
|---------|-------------|----------|
| Name not found in eligibility check | Not in SECC list | Check state-specific scheme or contact 14555 |
| OTP not received for eKYC | Mobile not linked to Aadhaar | Go to CSC for biometric eKYC |
| Card downloaded but hospital not accepting | Hospital not empanelled | Find another empanelled hospital via pmjay.gov.in |
| Hospital asking for money despite card | Overcharging or process error | Call 14555 immediately and report it |
| Card shows expired or inactive | Account issue | Visit CSC or Ayushman Mitra to reactivate |
| Face authentication failing | Poor lighting or camera quality | Try at CSC with proper setup |
| ₹5 lakh limit exhausted | High-cost treatment used up limit | Limit resets every year on April 1 |

---

## Ayushman Bharat vs State Health Schemes

Many states run their own health schemes alongside PM-JAY. In several states, both schemes are **merged** — meaning your Ayushman card works for both, and your coverage can effectively be higher:

| State | State Scheme | Combined Benefit |
|-------|-------------|-----------------|
| Maharashtra | Mahatma Jyotirao Phule Jan Arogya Yojana | ₹5 lakh (PM-JAY) + ₹1.5 lakh (state) |
| Tamil Nadu | Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance | Merged with PM-JAY |
| Andhra Pradesh | YSR Aarogyasri | Works alongside PM-JAY |
| Rajasthan | Chiranjeevi Yojana | Separate, broader coverage |
| Gujarat | MA Yojana | Integrated with PM-JAY |

Check your state health department website or call 14555 to know what applies in your state.

---

## Important Documents to Keep Ready

When going to a hospital for Ayushman treatment, carry these:

1. **Ayushman card** (printed or digital)
2. **Aadhaar card** (original)
3. **Ration card** (if available — helps with family verification)
4. **Doctor's referral / prescription** if it's a planned procedure
5. **Previous medical records** related to the condition being treated

---

## Ayushman Bharat Helpline & Contact

- **PM-JAY Helpline:** **14555** *(toll-free, 24×7)*
- **Official Website:** pmjay.gov.in
- **Beneficiary Portal:** beneficiary.nha.gov.in
- **App:** Ayushman App on Google Play Store
- **Email:** pmjay@nha.gov.in

If a hospital is denying cashless treatment despite your valid card, or asking for money illegally, call 14555 immediately. There are strict penalties for hospitals that overcharge PM-JAY patients.

---

## The Bigger Picture

₹5 lakh in health coverage sounds like a lot — and for most illnesses, it genuinely is. A bypass surgery that costs ₹2–3 lakh in a private hospital, a dialysis programme running ₹10,000/month, a cancer treatment package — all covered without the family having to sell land or take loans.

But for families who qualify, this card is arguably the most valuable government document you can carry — more than your ration card, more than your voter ID. Get it, keep it safe, and make sure every eligible member of your family has theirs.

## What is Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY?

**Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY)** is the world's largest government-funded health insurance scheme. Launched in 2018, it provides:

- **₹5 lakh health cover** per family per year
- **Cashless treatment** at government and private empanelled hospitals
- Coverage for **1,929+ medical procedures** including surgery, ICU, chemotherapy, dialysis, and more
- **Pre and post hospitalisation** expenses covered (up to 3 days before and 15 days after)
- **No cap on family size** — the entire family is covered under one card
- **Portable across India** — use it in any empanelled hospital anywhere in the country

| Detail | Info |
|--------|------|
| **Annual Coverage** | ₹5 lakh per family |
| **Premium** | Zero — completely free for beneficiaries |
| **Beneficiaries** | ~55 crore people (about 12 crore families) |
| **Official Website** | pmjay.gov.in / beneficiary.nha.gov.in |

- Families with no adult member aged 16–59
- Female-headed households with no adult male member aged 16–59
- Families with a disabled member and no able-bodied adult earner
- SC/ST households
- Landless agricultural labourers with manual casual labour as primary income

### Automatically Eligible (Urban Families)

Urban workers in these occupations are covered:

- Rag pickers, beggars, domestic workers
- Street vendors, cobblers, hawkers
- Construction workers, plumbers, masons, painters
- Washermen, sanitation workers, sweepers
- Home-based artisans, handicraft workers
- Transport workers — drivers, conductors, helpers
- Shop workers, delivery assistants, peons, security guards

- All **RSBY (Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana)** beneficiaries are included

   - Name + Mobile Number
   - Name + Ration Card Number
   - RSBY URN Number
5. If your family is in the database, it will show your details

**By Calling:**

- Any Ayushman Mitra (help desk) at an empanelled hospital can check your eligibility for free

If your name appears — great, move to the next step. If not, check whether your state has its own extended scheme that might cover you.

---

## Step 2 — How to Apply and Get the Ayushman Bharat Card

Getting the card is straightforward. You don't need to fill long forms or submit documents at a government office.

2. Open the app → click **"Beneficiary"**
3. Log in with your **Aadhaar-linked mobile number**
4. Verify with OTP
5. Your family details and eligibility will appear
6. Select your name → click **"Download Card"**
7. Complete **eKYC** — either OTP-based (if mobile linked to Aadhaar) or face authentication via the app camera
8. Your Ayushman card is generated and ready to download

### Method 2 — Common Service Centre (CSC)

1. Visit your nearest **CSC / Jan Seva Kendra**
2. Carry: Aadhaar card + Ration card (if available) + Mobile number
3. The operator will verify your eligibility and complete biometric eKYC
4. The card is printed on the spot or sent to your registered mobile

Every empanelled hospital has an **Ayushman Mitra** — a dedicated help desk. You can:
1. Walk in and ask the Ayushman Mitra to check your eligibility
2. If eligible, they'll complete the eKYC and generate your card right there
3. This is particularly useful if you need treatment urgently and don't have the card yet

---

## Step 3 — How to Download Your Ayushman Card Online

If you're already registered and just need to download or reprint your card:

1. Go to **beneficiary.nha.gov.in**
2. Click **"Login"** → select **"Beneficiary"**
3. Enter your **Aadhaar-linked mobile number**
4. Verify with OTP
5. Your family member list will appear
6. Click on your name → **"Download Card"**
7. Complete face authentication or OTP verification
8. The card downloads as a PDF — save it and print it

The card has your name, photo, Ayushman ID, and a QR code. Keep a printed copy *and* a photo on your phone — hospitals accept both.

---

The scheme covers a wide range of medical procedures across **1,929 packages**. Here's a broad look at what's included:

### Covered ✓

- **Surgery** — heart surgery, knee replacement, hip replacement, cataract, appendix, hernia, and more
- **Cancer treatment** — chemotherapy, radiation, surgery
- **Dialysis** — kidney failure treatment covered per session
- **ICU and ventilator** charges
- **Maternity and newborn care** — delivery, C-section, neonatal ICU
- **Mental health** hospitalisation
- **COVID-19** treatment (as per government guidelines)

- **Post-hospitalisation** follow-up (up to 15 days after discharge)
- **Medicines and consumables** during hospitalisation
- **Transport allowance** — ₹100 to ₹300 per visit (in some states)

- **OPD (Outpatient)** consultations — routine doctor visits are not covered

Most people who fail UPSC don't fail because they weren't smart enough. They fail because they studied the wrong things in the wrong order for too long. This guide is for people who want to avoid that. If you're preparing for UPSC CSE for the first time, or just appeared in Prelims 2026 and are now figuring out what's next, read this before you open another book.

---

## UPSC CSE 2026: What the Numbers Look Like

The Union Public Service Commission released the official notification for UPSC CSE 2026 on **February 4, 2026**. Here are the key facts you need to know:

| Detail | Information |
|---|---|
| Total Vacancies | **933** (IAS, IPS, IFS, IRS, IAAS, and other central services) |
| Prelims Date | May 24, 2026 (held, results awaited) |
| Mains Date | **August 21, 2026** |
| Application Closed | February 27, 2026 |

If you appeared in Prelims on May 24, results are expected in late June or early July 2026. **Do not wait for results before starting Mains preparation.** The overlap between Prelims and Mains is barely 6 to 8 weeks: candidates who start Mains prep only after seeing their Prelims result lose a month they cannot recover.

---

## The Three Stages: What Each One Demands

UPSC Civil Services is a three-stage process. Each stage tests a different skill set. Most aspirants understand this in theory but don't prepare differently for each.

### Stage 1: Prelims (Qualifying, Not Ranking)

Prelims is a screening exam. Your Prelims marks are **not added** to your final merit: you just need to cross the cutoff. The exam has two papers:

| Paper | Questions | Marks | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| GS Paper 1 | 100 | 200 | Counts for screening |
| CSAT Paper 2 | 80 | 200 | Qualifying, 33% (66 marks) needed |

Negative marking: **1/3rd of marks** per wrong answer in both papers.

**GS Paper 1** covers: Current Affairs, Indian History, World History, Indian and World Geography, Indian Polity and Governance, Economy, Environment and Ecology, General Science.

**What most people get wrong about Prelims:** They over-prepare for it. Prelims is not won by reading everything: it is won by reading the right things correctly. NCERT books (Class 6 to 12 for History, Geography, Polity, Economy), one good current affairs source, and consistent previous year paper solving is enough. Coaching notes without NCERT foundation is a trap.

Approximate Prelims cutoff (recent years, subject to change each year):
- General: 95 to 102 marks (out of 200)
- OBC: 88 to 95 marks
- SC: 78 to 85 marks
- ST: 72 to 80 marks

---

### Stage 2: Mains (Where the Real Race Is)

This is where UPSC actually separates candidates. Your Mains marks determine your rank.

**Mains has 9 papers:**

| Paper | Marks | Counts for Rank? |
|---|---|---|
| Paper A, Indian Language | 300 | Qualifying only |
| Paper B, English | 300 | Qualifying only |
| Essay | 250 | Yes |
| GS 1 (History, Geography, Society) | 250 | Yes |
| GS 2 (Polity, Governance, IR) | 250 | Yes |
| GS 3 (Economy, Environment, Science, Security) | 250 | Yes |
| GS 4 (Ethics, Integrity, Aptitude) | 250 | Yes |
| Optional Paper 1 | 250 | Yes |
| Optional Paper 2 | 250 | Yes |

**Total marks for ranking: 1750**
**Interview: 275 marks**
**Grand Total: 2025 marks**

The two qualifying papers (Indian Language + English) just need a pass. Focus all your energy on the 7 papers that count.

---

### Stage 3: Personality Test (Interview)

The interview is 275 marks and tests your personality, not your knowledge. The board assesses intellectual curiosity, honesty, communication, and suitability for civil services. In practical terms, most candidates score between 140 to 190 in the interview. Extreme scores are rare in either direction.

One thing that is true but rarely said: your DAF (Detailed Application Form) becomes the blueprint for your interview. Interviewers read it closely and ask about every claim you've made, hobbies, background, optional subject, work experience. Fill it carefully and be prepared to defend everything in it.

---

## Eligibility

**Educational Qualification:** Bachelor's degree in any subject from a recognised university. Even a final-year student appearing in their degree exam can apply provisionally.

**Age Limit (as on August 1, 2026):**
- Minimum: 21 years
- Maximum: 32 years (General/EWS)

**Age Relaxation:**
| Category | Relaxation | Upper Age |
|---|---|---|
| OBC | 3 years | 35 years |
| SC / ST | 5 years | 37 years |
| Defence disabled in operations | 3 years | 35 years |
| Ex-servicemen | 5 years | 37 years |
| PwBD | 10 years | 42 years |

**Number of Attempts:**
| Category | Attempts |
|---|---|
| General / EWS | 6 |
| OBC | 9 |
| SC / ST | Unlimited (until age limit) |

---

## Optional Subject: The Decision That Shapes Your Rank

The optional subject contributes 500 marks out of 1750, roughly 28% of your total Mains score. Picking the wrong optional is one of the most common reasons first-attempt candidates underperform in Mains.

**Popular choices and why they work:**

| Optional | Why Candidates Choose It |
|---|---|
| Political Science & IR (PSIR) | Overlaps heavily with GS 2 (Polity + IR). Saves time. Most popular optional. |
| Geography | Strong overlap with GS 1 (Geography). High scoring for map-based questions. |
| History | Huge overlap with GS 1. But answer writing demands are high. |
| Sociology | Short syllabus, predictable questions, writing-friendly. Good for new aspirants. |
| Public Administration | Overlaps with GS 2 (Governance). Easy to study alongside GS. |
| Mathematics / Science subjects | High scoring but needs a strong subject background. Risky without domain expertise. |

**How to choose your optional:**

1. Pick something you genuinely enjoy reading, you will read it for 6 to 12 months
2. Check overlap with GS, the more overlap, the less extra time you spend
3. Check the previous 5 years' question papers, does the pattern suit your writing style?
4. Look for good study material availability, online or coaching notes

Do not pick an optional just because a topper cleared with it. Their background is different from yours.

---

## First Attempt Strategy: Month by Month

Most first-attempt toppers spent 12 to 18 months preparing. Here is a realistic framework:

**Months 1 to 3: NCERT Foundation**

Read Class 6 to 12 NCERT books for:
- History (Class 6 to 12)
- Geography (Class 6 to 12)
- Polity (Class 9, 10, 11)
- Economy (Class 9, 10, 11, 12)
- Science (Class 9, 10)

This sounds basic. It is not. UPSC questions at Prelims level and Mains factual accuracy level trace back to NCERT. Skip this phase at your own risk.

**Months 4 to 6: Standard References + Optional Start**

After NCERT, move to standard reference books for each GS paper:
- History: Bipin Chandra's Modern India + Spectrum's Brief History of Modern India
- Polity: M. Laxmikanth's Indian Polity (the most important book in UPSC preparation)
- Economy: NCERT + Economic Survey summary
- Geography: G.C. Leong + NCERT Atlas
- Environment: Shankar IAS Environment

Start your optional subject study in parallel from Month 4 onwards.

**Months 7 to 9: Answer Writing + Current Affairs**

This is the phase most aspirants delay, and that delay costs them in Mains.

Answer writing is a skill. You do not become good at it by reading. You become good at it by writing, getting feedback, and writing again. Start writing at least 2 answers daily from Month 7. Use a timer, Mains answers must be written in 7 to 10 minutes each.

For current affairs: Read one national newspaper daily (The Hindu or Indian Express). Focus on editorials. Make short notes on themes, don't copy-paste articles.

**Months 10 to 12: Mock Tests + Revision**

Take full-length Prelims mocks every weekend. Analyse every wrong answer, don't just check the score.

For Mains, write at least 2 full mock papers (timed, pen on paper). If you are self-studying, the Insights on India test series and Forum IAS answer writing programs are respected resources.

---

## Books That Actually Matter

Don't buy everything. These are the ones that count:

| Subject | Book |
|---|---|
| Polity | M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity |
| Modern History | Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence |
| Ancient/Medieval | NCERT Class 11 and 12 History |
| Economy | NCERT + Ramesh Singh (Indian Economy) |
| Geography | NCERT + G.C. Leong (Physical Geography) |
| Environment | Shankar IAS Environment book |
| Ethics (GS 4) | Lexicon for Ethics (or UPSC specific ethics notes) |
| Current Affairs | The Hindu / Indian Express (daily) + any monthly magazine |

For Optional, identify the 3 to 4 standard books for your chosen subject and stick to them. Changing books every few months is a productivity killer.

---

## Three Mistakes That Kill First Attempts

**1. Treating Prelims and Mains as the same exam**

Prelims needs speed and accuracy. Mains needs depth and structured writing. Aspirants who only study for Prelims and then try to pivot for Mains in 6 weeks almost always struggle. You need to build Mains preparation alongside Prelims, not after.

**2. Not writing answers until very late**

The single biggest differentiator between candidates who clear Mains and those who don't is answer writing practice. Most aspirants start writing only 2 to 3 months before Mains. That is not enough. Start from Month 7 of your preparation. Write daily.

**3. Changing strategy based on someone else's results**

Every topper's interview is different. Their optional worked for them because of their specific background, strengths, and study hours. Read topper strategies as data points, not as instructions. Your strategy needs to fit your reality, your available hours, your existing knowledge base, your writing speed.

---

## What Happens After You Clear

933 vacancies across services are filled in this order of preference (approximate, depends on your rank and preferences):

1. Indian Administrative Service (IAS)
2. Indian Foreign Service (IFS)
3. Indian Police Service (IPS)
4. Group A Central Services: Indian Revenue Service (IRS), Indian Audit & Accounts Service (IAAS), Indian Railway Management Service, Indian Postal Service, and others
5. Group B Central Services

Your rank determines which service you get. IAS/IFS/IPS typically go to ranks under 100 to 150 in the General category (varies each year). Group A and B services fill the remaining ranks up to 933.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can a working professional crack UPSC in first attempt?**
Yes, but it requires discipline. 4 to 5 hours of focused daily study is more productive than 8 hours of distracted study. Working professionals who clear UPSC typically have a strict daily schedule, study on weekends extensively, and take at least 2 to 3 months of leave before Mains and the interview.

**Q: Is coaching necessary for UPSC?**
No. Roughly 40 to 50% of recent selections have been self-study candidates. Coaching helps with structure and peer pressure. But it is not a substitute for reading, thinking, and writing on your own. If you can self-motivate and self-evaluate, coaching is optional.

**Q: What is the best optional subject for arts graduates?**
Political Science & IR (PSIR) is the most popular among arts backgrounds because it overlaps significantly with GS 2. History and Geography are also strong choices. Sociology is recommended for candidates who find PSIR too heavily theoretical.

**Q: How many hours per day should I study?**
Quality matters more than quantity. 5 to 6 focused hours daily for 12 months is enough for most first-attempt toppers. More is not always better, fatigue compounds over months and reduces output quality.

**Q: I just appeared in Prelims 2026. Should I start Mains prep now?**
Yes, immediately. Mains was scheduled for 21 August 2026, which gives a prelims-qualified candidate roughly ten weeks in any cycle. Focus on GS answer writing, essay practice, and your optional. Don't start anything new, strengthen what you've already covered.

---

## Official Links

- UPSC Official Site: [upsc.gov.in](https://upsc.gov.in)
- Results and Notifications: [upsconline.nic.in](https://upsconline.nic.in)

---

*Disclaimer: All information in this article is based on the official UPSC CSE 2026 notification released on February 4, 2026 at upsc.gov.in. Vacancy counts, dates, and eligibility criteria are subject to revision, always verify from the official notification before applying.*

Prelims is a screening exam. Your Prelims marks are **not added** to your final merit: you just need to cross the cutoff. The exam has two papers:

| Paper | Questions | Marks | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| GS Paper 1 | 100 | 200 | Counts for screening |
| CSAT Paper 2 | 80 | 200 | Qualifying, 33% (66 marks) needed |

Negative marking: **1/3rd of marks** per wrong answer in both papers.

**GS Paper 1** covers: Current Affairs, Indian History, World History, Indian and World Geography, Indian Polity and Governance, Economy, Environment and Ecology, General Science.

**What most people get wrong about Prelims:** They over-prepare for it. Prelims is not won by reading everything: it is won by reading the right things correctly. NCERT books (Class 6 to 12 for History, Geography, Polity, Economy), one good current affairs source, and consistent previous year paper solving is enough. Coaching notes without NCERT foundation is a trap.

Approximate Prelims cutoff (recent years, subject to change each year):
- General: 95 to 102 marks (out of 200)
- OBC: 88 to 95 marks
- SC: 78 to 85 marks
- ST: 72 to 80 marks

---

### Stage 2: Mains (Where the Real Race Is)

This is where UPSC actually separates candidates. Your Mains marks determine your rank.

**Mains has 9 papers:**

| Paper | Marks | Counts for Rank? |
|---|---|---|
| Paper A, Indian Language | 300 | Qualifying only |
| Paper B, English | 300 | Qualifying only |
| Essay | 250 | ✅ Yes |
| GS 1 (History, Geography, Society) | 250 | ✅ Yes |
| GS 2 (Polity, Governance, IR) | 250 | ✅ Yes |
| GS 3 (Economy, Environment, Science, Security) | 250 | ✅ Yes |
| GS 4 (Ethics, Integrity, Aptitude) | 250 | ✅ Yes |
| Optional Paper 1 | 250 | ✅ Yes |
| Optional Paper 2 | 250 | ✅ Yes |

**Total marks for ranking: 1750**
**Interview: 275 marks**
**Grand Total: 2025 marks**

The two qualifying papers (Indian Language + English) just need a pass. Focus all your energy on the 7 papers that count.

---

### Stage 3: Personality Test (Interview)

The interview is 275 marks and tests your personality, not your knowledge. The board assesses intellectual curiosity, honesty, communication, and suitability for civil services. In practical terms, most candidates score between 140 to 190 in the interview. Extreme scores are rare in either direction.

One thing that is true but rarely said: your DAF (Detailed Application Form) becomes the blueprint for your interview. Interviewers read it closely and ask about every claim you've made, hobbies, background, optional subject, work experience. Fill it carefully and be prepared to defend everything in it.

---

## Eligibility

**Educational Qualification:** Bachelor's degree in any subject from a recognised university. Even a final-year student appearing in their degree exam can apply provisionally.

**Age Limit (as on August 1, 2026):**
- Minimum: 21 years
- Maximum: 32 years (General/EWS)

**Age Relaxation:**
| Category | Relaxation | Upper Age |
|---|---|---|
| OBC | 3 years | 35 years |
| SC / ST | 5 years | 37 years |
| Defence disabled in operations | 3 years | 35 years |
| Ex-servicemen | 5 years | 37 years |
| PwBD | 10 years | 42 years |

**Number of Attempts:**
| Category | Attempts |
|---|---|
| General / EWS | 6 |
| OBC | 9 |
| SC / ST | Unlimited (until age limit) |

---

## Optional Subject: The Decision That Shapes Your Rank

The optional subject contributes 500 marks out of 1750, roughly 28% of your total Mains score. Picking the wrong optional is one of the most common reasons first-attempt candidates underperform in Mains.

**Popular choices and why they work:**

| Optional | Why Candidates Choose It |
|---|---|
| Political Science & IR (PSIR) | Overlaps heavily with GS 2 (Polity + IR). Saves time. Most popular optional. |
| Geography | Strong overlap with GS 1 (Geography). High scoring for map-based questions. |
| History | Huge overlap with GS 1. But answer writing demands are high. |
| Sociology | Short syllabus, predictable questions, writing-friendly. Good for new aspirants. |
| Public Administration | Overlaps with GS 2 (Governance). Easy to study alongside GS. |
| Mathematics / Science subjects | High scoring but needs a strong subject background. Risky without domain expertise. |

**How to choose your optional:**

1. Pick something you genuinely enjoy reading, you will read it for 6 to 12 months
2. Check overlap with GS, the more overlap, the less extra time you spend
3. Check the previous 5 years' question papers, does the pattern suit your writing style?
4. Look for good study material availability, online or coaching notes

Do not pick an optional just because a topper cleared with it. Their background is different from yours.

---

## First Attempt Strategy: Month by Month

Most first-attempt toppers spent 12 to 18 months preparing. Here is a realistic framework:

**Months 1 to 3: NCERT Foundation**

Read Class 6 to 12 NCERT books for:
- History (Class 6 to 12)
- Geography (Class 6 to 12)
- Polity (Class 9, 10, 11)
- Economy (Class 9, 10, 11, 12)
- Science (Class 9, 10)

This sounds basic. It is not. UPSC questions at Prelims level and Mains factual accuracy level trace back to NCERT. Skip this phase at your own risk.

**Months 4 to 6: Standard References + Optional Start**

After NCERT, move to standard reference books for each GS paper:
- History: Bipin Chandra's Modern India + Spectrum's Brief History of Modern India
- Polity: M. Laxmikanth's Indian Polity (the most important book in UPSC preparation)
- Economy: NCERT + Economic Survey summary
- Geography: G.C. Leong + NCERT Atlas
- Environment: Shankar IAS Environment

Start your optional subject study in parallel from Month 4 onwards.

**Months 7 to 9: Answer Writing + Current Affairs**

This is the phase most aspirants delay, and that delay costs them in Mains.

Answer writing is a skill. You do not become good at it by reading. You become good at it by writing, getting feedback, and writing again. Start writing at least 2 answers daily from Month 7. Use a timer, Mains answers must be written in 7 to 10 minutes each.

For current affairs: Read one national newspaper daily (The Hindu or Indian Express). Focus on editorials. Make short notes on themes, don't copy-paste articles.

**Months 10 to 12: Mock Tests + Revision**

Take full-length Prelims mocks every weekend. Analyse every wrong answer, don't just check the score.

For Mains, write at least 2 full mock papers (timed, pen on paper). If you are self-studying, the Insights on India test series and Forum IAS answer writing programs are respected resources.

---

## Books That Actually Matter

Don't buy everything. These are the ones that count:

| Subject | Book |
|---|---|
| Polity | M. Laxmikanth, Indian Polity |
| Modern History | Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence |
| Ancient/Medieval | NCERT Class 11 and 12 History |
| Economy | NCERT + Ramesh Singh (Indian Economy) |
| Geography | NCERT + G.C. Leong (Physical Geography) |
| Environment | Shankar IAS Environment book |
| Ethics (GS 4) | Lexicon for Ethics (or UPSC specific ethics notes) |
| Current Affairs | The Hindu / Indian Express (daily) + any monthly magazine |

For Optional, identify the 3 to 4 standard books for your chosen subject and stick to them. Changing books every few months is a productivity killer.

---

## Three Mistakes That Kill First Attempts

**1. Treating Prelims and Mains as the same exam**

Prelims needs speed and accuracy. Mains needs depth and structured writing. Aspirants who only study for Prelims and then try to pivot for Mains in 6 weeks almost always struggle. You need to build Mains preparation alongside Prelims, not after.

**2. Not writing answers until very late**

The single biggest differentiator between candidates who clear Mains and those who don't is answer writing practice. Most aspirants start writing only 2 to 3 months before Mains. That is not enough. Start from Month 7 of your preparation. Write daily.

**3. Changing strategy based on someone else's results**

Every topper's interview is different. Their optional worked for them because of their specific background, strengths, and study hours. Read topper strategies as data points, not as instructions. Your strategy needs to fit your reality, your available hours, your existing knowledge base, your writing speed.

---

## What Happens After You Clear

933 vacancies across services are filled in this order of preference (approximate, depends on your rank and preferences):

1. Indian Administrative Service (IAS)
2. Indian Foreign Service (IFS)
3. Indian Police Service (IPS)
4. Group A Central Services: Indian Revenue Service (IRS), Indian Audit & Accounts Service (IAAS), Indian Railway Management Service, Indian Postal Service, and others
5. Group B Central Services

Your rank determines which service you get. IAS/IFS/IPS typically go to ranks under 100 to 150 in the General category (varies each year). Group A and B services fill the remaining ranks up to 933.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Can a working professional crack UPSC in first attempt?**
Yes, but it requires discipline. 4 to 5 hours of focused daily study is more productive than 8 hours of distracted study. Working professionals who clear UPSC typically have a strict daily schedule, study on weekends extensively, and take at least 2 to 3 months of leave before Mains and the interview.

**Q: Is coaching necessary for UPSC?**
No. Roughly 40 to 50% of recent selections have been self-study candidates. Coaching helps with structure and peer pressure. But it is not a substitute for reading, thinking, and writing on your own. If you can self-motivate and self-evaluate, coaching is optional.

**Q: What is the best optional subject for arts graduates?**
Political Science & IR (PSIR) is the most popular among arts backgrounds because it overlaps significantly with GS 2. History and Geography are also strong choices. Sociology is recommended for candidates who find PSIR too heavily theoretical.

**Q: How many hours per day should I study?**
Quality matters more than quantity. 5 to 6 focused hours daily for 12 months is enough for most first-attempt toppers. More is not always better, fatigue compounds over months and reduces output quality.

**Q: I just appeared in Prelims 2026. Should I start Mains prep now?**
Yes, immediately. Mains was scheduled for 21 August 2026, which gives a prelims-qualified candidate roughly ten weeks in any cycle. Focus on GS answer writing, essay practice, and your optional. Don't start anything new, strengthen what you've already covered.

---

## Official Links

- UPSC Official Site: [upsc.gov.in](https://upsc.gov.in)
- Results and Notifications: [upsconline.nic.in](https://upsconline.nic.in)

---

*Disclaimer: All information in this article is based on the official UPSC CSE 2026 notification released on February 4, 2026 at upsc.gov.in. Vacancy counts, dates, and eligibility criteria are subject to revision, always verify from the official notification before applying.*

## RRB Group D 2026: the CBT is over and the answer key is out

RRB Group D 2026, advertised as CEN 09/2025, fills 22,195 Level 1 posts in Indian Railways. Its Computer Based Test ran from 3 to 25 August 2026 across 16 days, in three shifts a day at more than 200 centres, and the Railway Recruitment Boards published the provisional answer key on 7 September 2026. The objection window that followed it has closed.

What is left is the result, which the RRBs have not dated. Normalisation can only be applied once every shift is accounted for, so the result is expected towards the end of October 2026. The admit card was released from 31 July 2026 and the city intimation slip from 24 July 2026, both on rrbapply.gov.in and the regional RRB websites.

This is one of the largest recruitment exercises anywhere. Reported applicant figures vary widely across sources, from around 58 lakh to close to a crore, and the exact number is not something any secondary site can confirm. Either way, 22,195 posts against a field that size means the Computer Based Test is decided on a handful of marks, and the negative marking on this paper is the reason many candidates lose them.

## The CBT schedule as it ran

The Railway Recruitment Board revised this schedule once during the cycle. These are the days the exam was held on.

| Week | Dates in August 2026 |
|---|---|
| First | 3, 4, 5, 6 |
| Second | 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 |
| Third | 17, 18, 19, 20, 21 |
| Fourth | 25 |

Sixteen days, three shifts each, which means a large number of distinct question papers. Because of that, RRB applies normalisation across shifts, so your final score is adjusted for the relative difficulty of the paper you sat rather than taken as a raw total. A candidate who gets a harder shift is not penalised for it, and equally a raw score from an easier shift does not carry the advantage it appears to.

## Why you are seeing two sets of contradictory dates

Search for RRB Group D right now and you will find pages announcing that the CBT is starting alongside pages announcing that PET dates are out and results have been declared. Both are accurate. They describe different recruitment cycles.

| Cycle | Stage in September 2026 |
|---|---|
| CEN 08/2024 | Result declared, at the Physical Efficiency Test and later stages |
| CEN 09/2025 | CBT completed 25 August 2026, answer key out, result awaited |

If you applied in the current round, yours is CEN 09/2025 and the result is your live stage. The PET notices circulating now belong to the earlier cycle and do not apply to you. Check the CEN number on your admit card if you are unsure, because acting on the wrong cycle's notice is the most common avoidable error in railway recruitment.

## Exam day: what to carry and what to expect

Take the printed admit card and the original photo identity document whose details you entered in your application. RRB is strict on the identity document matching the application, and a mismatch is grounds for being turned away.

Reach the centre by the reporting time on the admit card, not the exam start time. Gates close well before the paper begins, and RRB does not admit latecomers. Biometric verification and document checks take time, which is why the reporting window opens so far ahead.

Electronic items are prohibited: mobile phones, smart watches, calculators, Bluetooth devices and any storage media. So are bags, written material and, at most centres, metallic items and jewellery. Centres do not reliably provide storage, so carry as little as possible.

The paper is 90 minutes, extended to 120 minutes for candidates with a disability who have been granted a scribe or compensatory time.

## Exam pattern

The CBT is a single objective paper of 100 questions.

| Section | Questions | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| General Intelligence and Reasoning | 30 | 30 |
| Mathematics | 25 | 25 |
| General Science | 25 | 25 |
| General Awareness and Current Affairs | 20 | 20 |
| Total | 100 | 100 |

Duration is 90 minutes. Each correct answer carries 1 mark, and one third of a mark is deducted for each wrong answer.

That negative marking deserves attention, because several other recruitments carry none and the habits do not transfer. Work the arithmetic. A correct answer gains 1, a wrong one costs 0.33. Guessing blindly among four options gives you one correct and three wrong on average, so 1 minus 0.99, which is essentially break-even with added variance and no real gain. Eliminate one option and the odds tilt in your favour. Eliminate two and answering is clearly correct.

The practical rule: answer everything you know or can narrow to two options, and leave alone the questions where you have no basis at all. Candidates who carry an attempt-everything habit from exams like UP Police or Bihar Police, where there is no penalty, hand back marks here.

## Qualifying marks

Clearing the paper requires a minimum percentage that varies by category, commonly applied as 40 per cent for unreserved and EWS candidates, 30 per cent for OBC and SC, and 25 per cent for ST, with relaxation for candidates with disabilities where there is a shortfall.

Meeting that minimum is not selection. It makes you eligible to be ranked, and the actual shortlisting for the PET is done on normalised merit against the vacancy position in your region, which sits far above the qualifying floor.

## Syllabus

The paper is pitched at Class 10 level and rewards coverage more than depth.

Reasoning carries the most questions at 30 and covers analogies, series completion, coding and decoding, mathematical operations, relationships, syllogism, Venn diagrams, data interpretation, statement and conclusion, directions and analytical reasoning. It is the most trainable section, since the question types repeat and practice converts directly into speed.

Mathematics covers number systems, decimals and fractions, LCM and HCF, ratio and proportion, percentages, mensuration, time and work, time and distance, simple and compound interest, profit and loss, algebra, geometry and trigonometry basics, elementary statistics, and age and calendar problems.

General Science covers physics, chemistry and life sciences at Class 10 level. Physics and chemistry tend to carry more weight than biology in recent papers.

General Awareness and Current Affairs covers science and technology, sports, culture, personalities, economics, politics and general current affairs, with a bias towards the last year and towards railway-related developments.

## What the Level 1 posts actually are

Level 1 covers six categories of post, and they are different jobs despite sharing an entry route.

Pointsman operates points and signals at stations and yards, a safety-critical outdoor role often on night shifts. Track Maintainer Grade IV maintains the permanent way, which is physically demanding outdoor work on the track itself. Assistant posts in the Loco Shed, in Operations, and in TL and AC support maintenance and operations in depots and on trains. The remaining assistant categories cover workshop and departmental support roles.

Post preference is exercised during the application and allocation follows merit, region and vacancy position. Almost all of these involve shift work, outdoor conditions and a physical component, which is why the recruitment carries a Physical Efficiency Test at all.

## Physical Efficiency Test

The PET is pass or fail. It adds no marks to your merit position, and failing it removes you regardless of your CBT score.

| Candidates | Lifting and carrying | Running |
|---|---|---|
| Male | 35 kg carried over 100 metres in under 2 minutes, in one go without setting it down | 1000 metres in 4 minutes 15 seconds |
| Female | 20 kg carried over 100 metres in under 2 minutes, in one go without setting it down | 1000 metres in 5 minutes 40 seconds |

The lifting event is the one candidates underestimate, and the condition attached to it is what makes it hard: the weight has to be carried the full 100 metres in a single attempt without being put down. That is a grip strength and carrying endurance problem more than a maximal strength one, and it is not something general gym work prepares you for specifically. Loaded carries, farmer's walks and grip work are the training that transfers.

The running standard is more forgiving. 1000 metres in 4 minutes 15 seconds for men works out to about 4 minutes 15 seconds per kilometre, which is demanding but well short of the 800 metre standards in state police recruitment.

Both events are attempted in sequence and both must be cleared.

## Selection process

| Stage | Role |
|---|---|
| Computer Based Test | Decides merit, after normalisation across shifts |
| Physical Efficiency Test | Qualifying only |
| Document Verification | Eligibility check |
| Medical Examination | Fitness against the medical standard for the post |

The medical standard varies by post, and it is stricter than candidates expect for safety-related categories. Vision requirements for Pointsman and other safety posts in particular rule out candidates who would pass the standard for a clerical role, so check the medical classification for the posts you have preferenced.

## Salary of an RRB Group D employee

Level 1 of the 7th Pay Commission matrix carries a basic pay of Rs 18,000 a month, with an annual increment of about Rs 500 at the entry stage.

On top of basic pay come dearness allowance at the prevailing rate, house rent allowance at 8, 16 or 24 per cent of basic depending on the classification of your posting city, transport allowance, and railway-specific allowances including running or shift allowances where the post attracts them. Taking those together, in-hand pay at entry commonly works out in the region of Rs 22,500 to Rs 25,380 a month depending on posting and the current DA rate.

The non-cash side matters in railway service more than in most government jobs. Railway quarters where available, the free or concessional pass entitlement for the employee and family, railway medical facilities through railway hospitals, and pension benefits under the applicable rules all carry real value that the headline figure understates.

## Career progression

Level 1 is the entry rung and progression runs through departmental channels.

| Stage | Route |
|---|---|
| Level 1 entry post | Direct recruitment |
| Level 2 and 3 | Departmental promotion and departmental examinations |
| Higher technical and supervisory grades | Selection posts through departmental examination |

Indian Railways runs an internal promotion system with a defined quota of higher posts filled from serving employees through the General Departmental Competitive Examination and other departmental routes. A Level 1 entrant who prepares for those examinations can move up materially over a career, and many technical supervisors began at this level.

## How to use the remaining exam days

Because the CBT runs to 25 August, a large share of candidates still have days or weeks before they sit it, and that time is better spent on the paper's specific demands than on fresh study.

Reasoning is where the marginal marks are. It carries the most questions at 30, the question types repeat across cycles, and speed on them is a trained skill rather than a knowledge one. Working timed sets of past reasoning questions is the highest-return use of a remaining week.

Practise at the real pace. 100 questions in 90 minutes gives you 54 seconds per question, and the paper is not designed for careful deliberation on every item. Candidates lose more to poor time allocation, spending four minutes on a hard maths question, than to gaps in knowledge.

Rehearse the marking decision. Take a full mock, mark each answer as confident, narrowed to two, or pure guess, then score it both ways: once counting your guesses and once leaving them blank. Doing that twice tells you your own accuracy rate on narrowed questions, which is a better guide to exam-day behaviour than any general rule about negative marking.

Revise general science and current affairs last, since those are recall-heavy and benefit from being fresh.

## Eligibility

On age, the band for the cycle is set in the CEN, commonly 18 to 36 years for Level 1 posts with relaxation of 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, and further relaxation for ex-servicemen and other specified categories.

On education, the requirement is Class 10 pass, or an ITI certificate from an institution recognised by NCVT or SCVT, or an equivalent National Apprenticeship Certificate. A Class 10 pass alone is sufficient for most Level 1 posts.

On medical fitness, each post carries a medical classification and candidates must meet the standard for the post allotted, with vision requirements being the most common ground for rejection in safety categories.

## What happens after the CBT

The last shift was held on 25 August 2026 and the provisional answer key came out on 7 September 2026, with objections closing after it. The result follows once normalisation is applied across every shift, which the RRBs have not dated and which past cycles put at roughly two months after the final shift.

Shortlisted candidates are called for the PET, then document verification, then the medical. Use the intervening period rather than waiting on the result. The lifting standard in particular takes weeks of specific training to build, and candidates who begin only after the shortlist is published arrive underprepared for an event that is pass or fail.

Keep your documents ready in the meantime: Class 10 certificate, ITI or NAC certificate where relied on, category certificate in the central government format with a current non-creamy layer certificate for OBC candidates, and the identity documents matching your application.

## Vacancy tables: zone-wise and category-wise

The 22,195 posts are split across 17 zonal railways and the Metro Railway Kolkata. Some zones dominate the intake, and choosing a zone with more posts materially improves your appointment odds.

Zone-wise vacancy distribution per rrbapply.gov.in notification:

The 3 percent PwBD horizontal reservation is distributed across the four sub-categories: locomotor disability, visual impairment, hearing impairment, and other specified categories per the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act 2016.

Zones with lower vacancy shares (Northeast Frontier, Southern) also have lower cutoffs, but competition from local candidates keeps them from being cakewalks.

Set your target score at 5 to 7 points above the historical UR cutoff in your preferred zone. For Northern Railway UR, that's 79 to 82 marks in the CBT.

---

## Merit tie-breaking rules

When two candidates score identical normalised marks, RRB uses a fixed tie-breaking sequence per the CEN 09/2025 notification:

1. Higher score in Mathematics section.
2. If still tied, higher score in General Intelligence and Reasoning.
3. If still tied, higher score in General Science.
4. If still tied, higher score in General Awareness and Current Affairs.
5. If still tied, older date of birth (the older candidate is ranked higher).
6. If still tied, alphabetical order of first name in English.

Rule 5 (age) means candidates near the upper age boundary get a small advantage in ties. Rule 6 is rarely invoked, mainly for identical siblings with the same date of birth appearing in the same cycle.

---

## PET disqualification reasons

Common PET failures at the actual ground, based on RRB Chandigarh's 2018 and 2019 PET reports:

1. Dropping the weight at any point during the 100 m carry, even at the 99 m mark, counts as a fail. There's no second chance in the same event.
2. Running outside the marked track. Some candidates step out of the lane on curves and are disqualified without warning.
3. False start on the 1,000 m run. Two false starts in the same event end your PET.
4. Foot fault at the 100 m weight-carry start line. Your leading foot must be behind the line, not on it.
5. Bailing out mid-run because of stitches or dizziness. Once you stop, the event is over.
6. Medical disqualification during warm-up if the RRB medical officer observes any abnormal breathing, uncontrolled hypertension, or physical injury.
7. Weight not matching the specified figure. RRB weighs the sack in front of you before the event. Any dispute about weight must be raised before you lift it.
8. Time exceeded on the run: 4 minutes 15 seconds for males, 5 minutes 40 seconds for females, measured to the split second.

The margin between qualifying and failing is thin. Train to hit 3 minutes 55 seconds on the 1,000 m and 1 minute 45 seconds on the weight carry. A 20-second buffer accounts for grip fumbles, uneven ground, and warm-up shortfalls.

## Frequently asked questions

**When is the RRB Group D 2026 exam?**
The Computer Based Test for CEN 09/2025 runs across 16 days in August 2026: the 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, 9th, 10th, 11th, 12th, 13th, 14th, 17th, 18th, 19th, 20th, 21st and 25th, in three shifts a day at more than 200 centres. ## RRB Group D 2026: the CBT is over and the answer key is out

RRB Group D 2026, advertised as CEN 09/2025, fills 22,195 Level 1 posts in Indian Railways. Its Computer Based Test ran from 3 to 25 August 2026 across 16 days, in three shifts a day at more than 200 centres, and the Railway Recruitment Boards published the provisional answer key on 7 September 2026. The objection window that followed it has closed.

What is left is the result, which the RRBs have not dated. Normalisation can only be applied once every shift is accounted for, so the result is expected towards the end of October 2026. The admit card was released from 31 July 2026 and the city intimation slip from 24 July 2026, both on rrbapply.gov.in and the regional RRB websites.

This is one of the largest recruitment exercises anywhere. Reported applicant figures vary widely across sources, from around 58 lakh to close to a crore, and the exact number is not something any secondary site can confirm. Either way, 22,195 posts against a field that size means the Computer Based Test is decided on a handful of marks, and the negative marking on this paper is the reason many candidates lose them.

## The CBT schedule as it ran

The Railway Recruitment Board revised this schedule once during the cycle. These are the days the exam was held on.

| Week | Dates in August 2026 |
|---|---|
| First | 3, 4, 5, 6 |
| Second | 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 |
| Third | 17, 18, 19, 20, 21 |
| Fourth | 25 |

Sixteen days, three shifts each, which means a large number of distinct question papers. Because of that, RRB applies normalisation across shifts, so your final score is adjusted for the relative difficulty of the paper you sat rather than taken as a raw total. A candidate who gets a harder shift is not penalised for it, and equally a raw score from an easier shift does not carry the advantage it appears to.

## Why you are seeing two sets of contradictory dates

Search for RRB Group D right now and you will find pages announcing that the CBT is starting alongside pages announcing that PET dates are out and results have been declared. Both are accurate. They describe different recruitment cycles.

| Cycle | Stage in September 2026 |
|---|---|
| CEN 08/2024 | Result declared, at the Physical Efficiency Test and later stages |
| CEN 09/2025 | CBT completed 25 August 2026, answer key out, result awaited |

If you applied in the current round, yours is CEN 09/2025 and the result is your live stage. The PET notices circulating now belong to the earlier cycle and do not apply to you. Check the CEN number on your admit card if you are unsure, because acting on the wrong cycle's notice is the most common avoidable error in railway recruitment.

## Exam day: what to carry and what to expect

Take the printed admit card and the original photo identity document whose details you entered in your application. RRB is strict on the identity document matching the application, and a mismatch is grounds for being turned away.

Reach the centre by the reporting time on the admit card, not the exam start time. Gates close well before the paper begins, and RRB does not admit latecomers. Biometric verification and document checks take time, which is why the reporting window opens so far ahead.

Electronic items are prohibited: mobile phones, smart watches, calculators, Bluetooth devices and any storage media. So are bags, written material and, at most centres, metallic items and jewellery. Centres do not reliably provide storage, so carry as little as possible.

The paper is 90 minutes, extended to 120 minutes for candidates with a disability who have been granted a scribe or compensatory time.

## Exam pattern

The CBT is a single objective paper of 100 questions.

| Section | Questions | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| General Intelligence and Reasoning | 30 | 30 |
| Mathematics | 25 | 25 |
| General Science | 25 | 25 |
| General Awareness and Current Affairs | 20 | 20 |
| Total | 100 | 100 |

Duration is 90 minutes. Each correct answer carries 1 mark, and one third of a mark is deducted for each wrong answer.

That negative marking deserves attention, because several other recruitments carry none and the habits do not transfer. Work the arithmetic. A correct answer gains 1, a wrong one costs 0.33. Guessing blindly among four options gives you one correct and three wrong on average, so 1 minus 0.99, which is essentially break-even with added variance and no real gain. Eliminate one option and the odds tilt in your favour. Eliminate two and answering is clearly correct.

The practical rule: answer everything you know or can narrow to two options, and leave alone the questions where you have no basis at all. Candidates who carry an attempt-everything habit from exams like UP Police or Bihar Police, where there is no penalty, hand back marks here.

## Qualifying marks

Clearing the paper requires a minimum percentage that varies by category, commonly applied as 40 per cent for unreserved and EWS candidates, 30 per cent for OBC and SC, and 25 per cent for ST, with relaxation for candidates with disabilities where there is a shortfall.

Meeting that minimum is not selection. It makes you eligible to be ranked, and the actual shortlisting for the PET is done on normalised merit against the vacancy position in your region, which sits far above the qualifying floor.

## Syllabus

The paper is pitched at Class 10 level and rewards coverage more than depth.

Reasoning carries the most questions at 30 and covers analogies, series completion, coding and decoding, mathematical operations, relationships, syllogism, Venn diagrams, data interpretation, statement and conclusion, directions and analytical reasoning. It is the most trainable section, since the question types repeat and practice converts directly into speed.

Mathematics covers number systems, decimals and fractions, LCM and HCF, ratio and proportion, percentages, mensuration, time and work, time and distance, simple and compound interest, profit and loss, algebra, geometry and trigonometry basics, elementary statistics, and age and calendar problems.

General Science covers physics, chemistry and life sciences at Class 10 level. Physics and chemistry tend to carry more weight than biology in recent papers.

General Awareness and Current Affairs covers science and technology, sports, culture, personalities, economics, politics and general current affairs, with a bias towards the last year and towards railway-related developments.

## What the Level 1 posts actually are

Level 1 covers six categories of post, and they are different jobs despite sharing an entry route.

Pointsman operates points and signals at stations and yards, a safety-critical outdoor role often on night shifts. Track Maintainer Grade IV maintains the permanent way, which is physically demanding outdoor work on the track itself. Post preference is exercised during the application and allocation follows merit, region and vacancy position. Almost all of these involve shift work, outdoor conditions and a physical component, which is why the recruitment carries a Physical Efficiency Test at all.

The PET is pass or fail. It adds no marks to your merit position, and failing it removes you regardless of your CBT score.

| Candidates | Lifting and carrying | Running |
|---|---|---|
| Male | 35 kg carried over 100 metres in under 2 minutes, in one go without setting it down | 1000 metres in 4 minutes 15 seconds |
| Female | 20 kg carried over 100 metres in under 2 minutes, in one go without setting it down | 1000 metres in 5 minutes 40 seconds |

The lifting event is the one candidates underestimate, and the condition attached to it is what makes it hard: the weight has to be carried the full 100 metres in a single attempt without being put down. That is a grip strength and carrying endurance problem more than a maximal strength one, and it is not something general gym work prepares you for specifically. Loaded carries, farmer's walks and grip work are the training that transfers.

The running standard is more forgiving. 1000 metres in 4 minutes 15 seconds for men works out to about 4 minutes 15 seconds per kilometre, which is demanding but well short of the 800 metre standards in state police recruitment.

Both events are attempted in sequence and both must be cleared.
