## SBI PO 2026 at a glance

State Bank of India is recruiting 1,500 Probationary Officers under advertisement CRPD/PO/2026-27/09, notified on 18 June 2026. This is the single most chased banking job in India, and the numbers show why: SBI PO draws several lakh applicants for a fixed intake, so the real contest is not eligibility but clearing a high cut-off across three demanding stages.

Both written stages are done. The preliminary examination was held on 1 and 2 August 2026, SBI declared the prelims result on 28 August 2026 and published scorecards with category-wise cut-offs on 1 September 2026. The main examination followed on 12 September 2026. What is left for candidates who sat the mains is the mains result, then the psychometric test, the interview and the group exercise. Applications for this cycle opened on 18 June and closed on 8 July 2026. If you are researching for the next cycle, this page lays out exactly what the exam demands.

Of the 1,500 posts, 1,446 are regular vacancies and 54 are backlog vacancies. The recruitment is for Junior Management Grade Scale I officers, a permanent SBI officer-cadre role with a fast promotion track and a starting in-hand pay that clears most other clerical and officer bank jobs.

## Important dates for SBI PO 2026

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Notification released | 18 June 2026 |
| Online application begins | 18 June 2026 |
| Last date to apply | 8 July 2026 |
| Prelims call letter | Available (July 2026) |
| Preliminary exam | 1 and 2 August 2026 |
| Mains exam | September 2026 (expected) |
| Phase III (Psychometric, Group Exercise, Interview) | After mains result |

The mains date is not yet officially fixed, so treat September 2026 as expected until SBI confirms it on the careers portal. SBI usually announces the mains date and releases the mains call letter only after the prelims result, so keep checking your login dashboard through August 2026.

## Vacancy details

The 1,500 posts split into 1,446 regular and 54 backlog vacancies. The category-wise breakup of the regular posts is below.

| Category | Vacancies |
|---|---|
| Unreserved (UR) | 588 |
| OBC | 390 |
| SC | 234 |
| ST | 144 |
| EWS | 144 |
| Total (regular) | 1,500 |

## Eligibility for SBI PO 2026

Age and qualification are the two gates, and both are checked as on 1 April 2026.

On age, you must be between 21 and 30 years, that is, born between 2 April 1996 and 1 April 2005, both inclusive. Category relaxation applies over the upper limit: 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC and ST, and 10 years for PwBD candidates.

On qualification, you need a graduation in any discipline from a recognised university, with no minimum percentage. Final-year students can apply provisionally but must produce proof of graduation before the interview stage. If your marks are in CGPA, convert them to a percentage using your college formula for the form.

On attempts, SBI limits the number of times General and EWS candidates can appear, while OBC and reserved candidates get more or no cap. The exact attempt limits change between cycles, so confirm the figure in the CRPD/PO/2026-27/09 notification rather than assuming a past cycle's rule.

## Application fee

| Category | Fee |
|---|---|
| General, OBC, EWS | Rs 750 |
| SC, ST, PwBD | Nil |

Payment is online through debit card, credit card, or net banking. The fee is not refundable once paid, so confirm your eligibility on age, qualification, and category before you complete the payment step.

## Selection process

SBI PO runs through three phases, and unlike most bank exams it adds a psychometric test and a group exercise on top of the interview.

1. Preliminary examination: a qualifying screen. Its marks do not count toward the final merit.
2. Main examination: objective plus descriptive. This decides your position going into the final phase.
3. Phase III: a psychometric test, a group exercise, and a personal interview.

The final merit is built from the mains score and the Phase III score. Prelims only decides who moves to the mains.

## Preliminary exam pattern

The prelims is a 100-mark test of 100 questions in one hour, with 20-minute sectional timing and a penalty of 0.25 marks per wrong answer.

| Section | Questions | Marks | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| English Language | 30 | 30 | 20 min |
| Quantitative Aptitude | 35 | 35 | 20 min |
| Reasoning Ability | 35 | 35 | 20 min |
| Total | 100 | 100 | 60 min |

The sectional timing is the catch: you cannot carry saved minutes from one section into another, so pace within each 20-minute block decides your score as much as accuracy.

## Main exam pattern

The mains has an objective paper of 200 marks and a descriptive paper of 30 marks, with sectional timing throughout and the same 0.25 penalty on objective questions.

| Section | Questions | Marks | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reasoning and Computer Aptitude | 40 | 60 | 50 min |
| Data Analysis and Interpretation | 30 | 60 | 45 min |
| General, Economy and Banking Awareness | 60 | 60 | 45 min |
| English Language | 40 | 20 | 40 min |
| Objective total | 170 | 200 | 3 hr |
| Descriptive (letter and essay) | 2 | 30 | 30 min |

The descriptive paper tests a letter and an essay, and it is evaluated only if you clear the objective cut-off. General and banking awareness carries the most weight relative to preparation time, so a daily current affairs and banking-news habit pays off directly here.

## Syllabus

Quantitative Aptitude and Data Interpretation cover simplification, number series, quadratic equations, arithmetic (percentage, ratio, time and work, profit and loss), and data interpretation sets. Reasoning covers puzzles, seating arrangement, syllogism, coding and decoding, inequalities, and data sufficiency, with computer aptitude in the mains. English covers reading comprehension, cloze test, error spotting, sentence rearrangement, and vocabulary. General, Economy and Banking Awareness covers current affairs of the last six months, banking and financial terms, RBI and monetary policy basics, and static general knowledge.

## SBI PO 2026 salary and in-hand pay

SBI PO is a Junior Management Grade Scale I officer post on SBI's own pay scale, not the central government pay scale, so its dearness allowance follows SBI's bipartite settlement rather than the 7th Pay Commission. The starting basic is Rs 48,480, and a graduate entrant gets four advance increments of Rs 2,000, which lifts the effective starting basic to about Rs 56,480 a month.

Here is a worked in-hand estimate at the SBI bipartite scale. On an effective basic near Rs 56,480, dearness allowance under the SBI settlement adds roughly Rs 15,300, house rent allowance adds about Rs 4,500, and a special allowance plus city and other allowances add close to Rs 16,000. That is a gross near Rs 93,000 to Rs 98,000 a month. After deductions for provident fund, the pension contribution, and professional tax (together around Rs 13,000), the in-hand lands at about Rs 80,000 to Rs 82,000 a month in a metro. The annual cost to company works out near Rs 22 lakh in a metro posting. In-hand varies with the posting city because house rent allowance changes by location.

## SBI PO cut-off trend

Cut-offs move year to year with the difficulty of the paper. As a reference, the 2025 cycle closed near these marks.

| Stage | General | OBC | SC | ST | EWS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Prelims (out of 100) | 66.75 | 65.50 | 59.25 | 51.50 | 64.50 |
| Mains (out of 250) | 75 | 69.50 | 62.75 | 62.51 | 75 |

The general-category mains cut-off has swung from about 94.85 in 2021 to 70 in 2023, 87.50 in 2024, and 75 in 2025, per SBI result data, which is why comparing your target with a single past year is misleading. Remember that prelims marks do not carry into the final merit; the mains and Phase III decide selection.

## SBI PO vs IBPS PO

Candidates preparing for SBI PO usually also weigh [IBPS PO](/sarkari-naukri/ibps-po-2026). This comparison sets out the real differences.

| Factor | SBI PO | IBPS PO |
|---|---|---|
| Recruiter | State Bank of India only | 11 or more public-sector banks |
| Recent vacancies | 1,500 (2026) | Several thousand (varies by year) |
| Starting basic | Rs 48,480 (about Rs 56,480 with increments) | Rs 36,000 |
| Final stage | Psychometric, group exercise, and interview | Interview |
| Descriptive test | Yes, in the mains | No |
| Difficulty | Higher, tougher reasoning and a descriptive paper | Moderate |

SBI PO pays more from day one and promotes fast, but its exam is tougher and its intake is a fraction of IBPS PO. IBPS PO spreads your chance across many banks with a slightly gentler paper. Most serious aspirants prepare for both, since the syllabi overlap heavily.

## What a bank PO actually does

A Probationary Officer starts as a scale I officer and, after a probation and training period, handles branch operations, customer relationships, loan processing, and supervision of clerical staff. The role carries decision-making responsibility from early on, which is why the selection tests aptitude, communication, and a group exercise rather than rote knowledge alone. Postings are all India at the bank's discretion, so a willingness to relocate is part of the job. Early years often mean a rural or semi-urban branch, which builds the ground-level banking experience that later officer roles are built on, and the exposure counts toward faster promotion.

## Career growth at SBI

SBI PO is one of the fastest promotion tracks in Indian banking. An officer moves from Junior Management Grade Scale I to Middle Management Grade Scale II and III, then into Senior Management and Top Executive grades over a career, through a mix of promotion exams and performance. The bank also offers postings abroad and specialised roles in treasury, credit, and risk as you rise. This mobility, combined with the pay that starts higher than most other bank jobs, is why SBI PO stays the most competitive banking exam year after year.

## Phase III explained: psychometric, group exercise, and interview

The final phase is where SBI PO differs most from other bank exams, and candidates who prepare only for the written stages often stumble here. The psychometric test profiles your personality traits and behaviour tendencies, and its output is used as an input to the interview rather than as a separate scored round. The group exercise puts you in a small group to discuss or solve a given situation, and the panel watches how you contribute, listen, and lead without dominating. The personal interview then probes your background, banking awareness, and reasoning under questioning. Together the group exercise and interview carry the Phase III marks that combine with your mains score for the final merit. The practical lesson is that strong communication and composure matter as much as your written score, so mock interviews and group discussions in the weeks before the final phase are time well spent.

## Documents you will need

Keep these ready for the application and the later stages, since the process pauses if you cannot produce them on time.

1. A recent passport-size photograph and a scanned signature in the SBI-specified format.
2. Your graduation degree and mark sheets, or a final-year provisional proof.
3. A category certificate (OBC, SC, ST, EWS, or PwBD) where you claim relaxation.
4. A valid photo ID that matches your registration details.
5. An active email and mobile number, since every call letter and result alert goes there.

## Admit card and exam day

SBI releases the call letter stage by stage, roughly a week before each exam, on the careers portal. Download it, check that your name, photograph, and centre are correct, and carry a printout with the same photo ID you used at registration. Reach the centre early, because biometric verification and document checks take time and latecomers are refused entry. The exam is computer based, so no rough paper of your own is allowed; the centre provides sheets that you return before leaving. Electronic devices, smart watches, and written material lead to disqualification, so leave them out.

## How to score the descriptive paper

The mains descriptive paper of 30 marks is small but decisive, because many candidates cluster within a few marks in the objective section and the descriptive score breaks the tie. It tests a letter and an essay, usually on a banking, economy, or general social topic. For the letter, follow the standard format, keep the tone appropriate to the recipient, and stay within the word limit. For the essay, spend the first few minutes planning a clear structure of introduction, two or three body points with an example each, and a short conclusion, rather than writing whatever comes first. Correct grammar and a clean structure score better than long, unfocused writing. Because it is typed on screen, practising a few timed essays and letters on a keyboard before the exam removes a real disadvantage on the day.

## How to prepare for SBI PO

With prelims on 1 and 2 August 2026, the near-term task for applicants is speed under sectional timing, so daily timed drills in all three sections beat long untimed study. For the mains, data interpretation, general and banking awareness, and the descriptive paper carry the weight, so build a six-month current-affairs base and practise letter and essay writing under time. ## TNPSC Group 2 and 2A 2026: the dates and the distinction

TNPSC Group 2 and 2A is the Combined Civil Services Examination II, run by the Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission, and it fills clerical and supervisory posts across the state government. For the 2026 cycle, TNPSC released the notification on 11 August 2026 and the preliminary examination is scheduled for 1 November 2026.

Before the dates, the distinction, because it decides how you prepare. Group 2 and Group 2A are advertised together, use the same preliminary examination, and then diverge completely at the mains stage. Group 2 posts have a descriptive mains paper and an interview. Group 2A posts have an objective mains paper and no interview.

Candidates routinely apply to both, clear the same prelims, and then discover in the mains hall that they have prepared for the wrong format. Writing a 300-mark descriptive General Studies paper and answering a 300-mark objective one are different skills, and the gap between knowing a fact and being able to write about it under time pressure is where the Group 2 mains separates candidates.

## Important dates

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Notification expected | 11 August 2026 |
| Preliminary examination (CCSE-II) | 1 November 2026 |
| Mains examination | To be announced after the prelims result |

The previous cycle gives a sense of the rhythm. It was notified on 15 July 2025 for 659 vacancies, its mains was revised to 15 March 2026, and the mains result has been declared. So the gap from notification to prelims runs a few months, and from prelims to mains several more, which makes this a year-long process rather than a quick one.

Because the 2026 notification is not out at the time of writing, the vacancy count for this cycle is not known. Treat 659 as an indication of scale from the previous cycle rather than a figure for 2026.

## What Group 2 and Group 2A posts actually are

Both groups sit in the same broad band of state government service, but the roles differ in character.

Group 2, the interview posts, are supervisory and field-facing roles. They include Deputy Commercial Tax Officer, Sub Registrar Grade II, Probation Officer, Senior Inspector of Cooperative Societies, Municipal Commissioner Grade II, and Assistant Inspector of Labour. These carry public dealing, inspection powers, and decision-making responsibility, which is why the commission attaches an interview.

Group 2A, the non-interview posts, are largely office and secretariat roles, including Assistant Section Officer in the Secretariat and assistant posts across departments and the Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission itself. The work is file-based rather than field-based.

The exact post list is set in each notification, so check the advertisement for the cycle you are applying to rather than assuming last year's list carries over.

## Preliminary examination pattern

One paper, common to both groups.

| Element | Detail |
|---|---|
| Total questions | 200 |
| Total marks | 300 |
| Duration | 3 hours |
| Negative marking | None |
| Minimum qualifying | 90 marks out of 300 |
| Composition | 100 questions General Tamil or General English, 100 questions General Studies and Aptitude |

Two features shape strategy here. There is no negative marking, so every one of the 200 questions should carry an answer. And the prelims is purely a screening stage: your prelims marks do not carry into the final merit list. Clearing it at a comfortable margin is all that is required, and marks beyond that buy nothing.

The 90 out of 300 qualifying figure is the floor, not the real bar. The actual cutoff for being called to the mains is set by the number of vacancies and the number of candidates, and it sits well above the qualifying minimum in most cycles.

## Mains examination: two different exams

This is where the groups separate.

| | Group 2 (interview posts) | Group 2A (non-interview posts) |
|---|---|---|
| Paper I | Tamil eligibility test, SSLC standard, descriptive, 100 marks | Tamil eligibility test, SSLC standard, descriptive, 100 marks |
| Paper I role | Qualifying only | Qualifying only |
| Paper II | General Studies, degree standard, DESCRIPTIVE, 300 marks | General Studies with reasoning and language, OBJECTIVE, 300 marks |
| Interview | Yes | No |
| Merit built from | Paper II and interview | Paper II alone |

Paper I is a mandatory Tamil eligibility paper at SSLC standard, and it is qualifying. Its 100 marks do not enter your merit position. A candidate who writes a strong Paper I and a weak Paper II gains nothing from the former.

Paper II carries the entire weight. For Group 2A that means a 300-mark objective paper where accuracy and coverage decide your rank. For Group 2 it means a 300-mark descriptive paper, written by hand, under time pressure, on general studies at degree standard.

## Preparing for a descriptive paper

Candidates who have only ever written objective exams underestimate what the Group 2 descriptive mains asks, so it is worth being concrete about the difference.

In an objective paper, recognising the right option among four is enough. In a descriptive paper you have to produce the content from memory, structure it into a coherent answer, and do it inside a word and time budget across many questions. Knowing a topic well enough to identify the correct statement about it does not mean you can write 150 useful words on it in six minutes.

The preparation that works is writing practice, not more reading. Take past questions, write full answers by hand under a clock, and review them against the source material for accuracy, structure and length. Handwriting speed and legibility matter, since an evaluator reads what you actually wrote. Candidates who start writing practice a month before the mains rarely close the gap.

For Group 2A, the objective paper rewards a different discipline: broad coverage, quick recall, and accuracy across general studies, reasoning and language, with the same no-penalty logic applying so that everything gets an answer.

## Syllabus

The prelims and mains draw on a common base, with the mains going deeper.

General Studies covers Indian polity and the Constitution, Indian history with emphasis on the freedom movement, Indian and Tamil Nadu geography, the Indian economy and Tamil Nadu's economy, general science, current affairs at national and state level, and a substantial Tamil Nadu component covering the state's history, culture, social reform movements, administration and current schemes.

The Tamil Nadu portion is the section that separates local candidates from others, and it is also the most predictable part of the paper. Tamil society, the Dravidian movement, Tamil literature and the state's development schemes recur across cycles.

Aptitude and mental ability at the prelims stage covers arithmetic, data interpretation, logical reasoning and basic numeracy at a level that a graduate can prepare in a few focused weeks.

General Tamil covers grammar, literature and comprehension. Candidates may opt for General English instead where the notification allows, and that choice should be made on genuine strength rather than on assumptions about which is scored more leniently.

## How TNPSC Group 2 compares with Group 1 and Group 4

Tamil Nadu aspirants usually consider several TNPSC groups at once, and the differences are more than a matter of seniority.

| | Group 1 | Group 2 and 2A | Group 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Typical posts | Deputy Collector, Deputy Superintendent of Police, Assistant Commissioner | Deputy Commercial Tax Officer, Sub Registrar, Assistant Section Officer | Village Administrative Officer, Junior Assistant, Typist |
| Education | Graduate degree | Graduate degree | Class 10 or Class 12 depending on post |
| Stages | Prelims, descriptive mains, interview | Prelims, mains, interview for Group 2 only | Single written exam |
| Competition | Highest, very few posts | High | Very high volume, but lower bar |

Group 1 is the state's senior administrative entry with a small number of posts and the longest process. Group 4 needs no degree and is decided on a single paper, which draws enormous numbers of applicants. Group 2 and 2A sit between them, and for a graduate they usually offer the best ratio of posts to realistic competition.

The preparation overlaps substantially across all three, since the general studies base and the Tamil Nadu component are common. A candidate preparing for Group 2 can appear for Group 4 with little extra work, and can build towards Group 1 by adding the descriptive depth and the optional-subject requirements.

## Mistakes that cost candidates

A few patterns repeat every cycle, and each of them is avoidable.

Preparing only for the objective format when applying to Group 2. The mains for the interview posts is descriptive, and that has to be trained for separately.

Treating the prelims as a scoring exam. Its marks do not count, so effort spent pushing a comfortable prelims score higher is effort taken from the mains, which is where selection happens.

Leaving questions blank in the prelims. With no negative marking, an unanswered question is a certain zero against a free chance at a mark.

Neglecting the Tamil eligibility paper. It is qualifying, so it adds nothing to your rank, but failing it ends the attempt regardless of how well Paper II went.

Ignoring the Tamil Nadu component of general studies. It is the most predictable and most repeated part of the syllabus, and candidates who focus only on national-level material give away marks that are available to anyone willing to study the state material.

Choosing the language paper on hearsay rather than on strength. Candidates pick General Tamil or General English based on which one other aspirants claim is scored more generously, and then lose marks in a section they could have secured by choosing the language they actually read and write better.

Waiting for the notification to start. The notification appeared on 11 August 2026 and the prelims falls on 1 November 2026, which leaves about twelve weeks between the two, and applications closed on 9 September within that span. Candidates who begin after the advertisement appears are preparing a year-long syllabus in a quarter of that time.

## Salary and pay

Pay for Group 2 and 2A posts is set under the Tamil Nadu Revised Pay Rules, 2017, with each post assigned a level in the state pay matrix.

Most of the commonly recruited posts, including Sub Registrar, Deputy Commercial Tax Officer, Probation Officer and Senior Revenue Inspector, sit at Pay Level 18, with a basic pay of Rs 37,200 and a range running to about Rs 1,17,600. In-hand pay at entry, after dearness allowance, house rent allowance and city compensatory allowance and before deductions, works out in the region of Rs 45,000 to Rs 55,000 a month depending on the posting.

Levels vary by post within the group, so confirm the figure for the specific post in the notification rather than assuming a single number covers all of them. Alongside pay, the posts carry the leave, medical and pension entitlements of Tamil Nadu government service.

## Eligibility

On education, a graduate degree from a recognised university is the requirement for both groups. Some posts carry additional subject or qualification requirements set out in the notification.

On age, the limits are set per cycle and vary by category and by post, with relaxation for backward classes, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes as per Tamil Nadu rules. Check the notification for the reckoning date and the exact bands.

On language, the mains includes a mandatory Tamil eligibility paper at SSLC standard, so a working command of written Tamil is a practical requirement of the process even where the general studies preparation is done in English.

## How to apply

Applications are filed on tnpsc.gov.in.

1. Complete the TNPSC One Time Registration if you have not already. This profile is reused across TNPSC examinations and is valid for five years.
2. TNPSC released the notification on 11 August 2026. Read the advertisement for the post list, vacancy count and eligibility for this cycle.
3. Apply online within the window, selecting your group and post preferences and your language paper option.
4. Upload photograph and signature in the specified format.
5. Pay the examination fee online, noting the fee concessions available to candidates who have not exhausted their free-chance entitlement under TNPSC rules.
6. Submit, save the application, and download the hall ticket when it is released ahead of the 1 November 2026 prelims.

## Documents you will need

1. Class 10 certificate as proof of date of birth.
2. Degree certificate and mark sheets.
3. Community certificate for candidates claiming reservation.
4. Nativity or residence documents where required.
5. Certificates for any additional claims such as differently abled status, ex-servicemen status, destitute widow status, or sports.
6. Photograph, signature, and a photo identity document matching the application.

## TNPSC Group 2 and 2A 2026: the dates and the distinction

TNPSC Group 2 and 2A is the Combined Civil Services Examination II, run by the Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission, and it fills clerical and supervisory posts across the state government. For the 2026 cycle, TNPSC released the notification on 11 August 2026 and the preliminary examination is scheduled for 1 November 2026.

Before the dates, the distinction, because it decides how you prepare. Group 2 and Group 2A are advertised together, use the same preliminary examination, and then diverge completely at the mains stage. Group 2 posts have a descriptive mains paper and an interview. Group 2A posts have an objective mains paper and no interview.

Candidates routinely apply to both, clear the same prelims, and then discover in the mains hall that they have prepared for the wrong format. Writing a 300-mark descriptive General Studies paper and answering a 300-mark objective one are different skills, and the gap between knowing a fact and being able to write about it under time pressure is where the Group 2 mains separates candidates.

## Important dates

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Notification expected | 11 August 2026 |
| Preliminary examination (CCSE-II) | 1 November 2026 |
| Mains examination | To be announced after the prelims result |

The previous cycle gives a sense of the rhythm. It was notified on 15 July 2025 for 659 vacancies, its mains was revised to 15 March 2026, and the mains result has been declared. So the gap from notification to prelims runs a few months, and from prelims to mains several more, which makes this a year-long process rather than a quick one.

Because the 2026 notification is not out at the time of writing, the vacancy count for this cycle is not known. Treat 659 as an indication of scale from the previous cycle rather than a figure for 2026.

## What Group 2 and Group 2A posts actually are

Both groups sit in the same broad band of state government service, but the roles differ in character.

Group 2, the interview posts, are supervisory and field-facing roles. They include Deputy Commercial Tax Officer, Sub Registrar Grade II, Probation Officer, Senior Inspector of Cooperative Societies, Municipal Commissioner Grade II, and Assistant Inspector of Labour. These carry public dealing, inspection powers, and decision-making responsibility, which is why the commission attaches an interview.

Group 2A, the non-interview posts, are largely office and secretariat roles, including Assistant Section Officer in the Secretariat and assistant posts across departments and the Tamil Nadu Public Service Commission itself. The work is file-based rather than field-based.

The exact post list is set in each notification, so check the advertisement for the cycle you are applying to rather than assuming last year's list carries over.

## Preliminary examination pattern

One paper, common to both groups.

| Element | Detail |
|---|---|
| Total questions | 200 |
| Total marks | 300 |
| Duration | 3 hours |
| Negative marking | None |
| Minimum qualifying | 90 marks out of 300 |
| Composition | 100 questions General Tamil or General English, 100 questions General Studies and Aptitude |

Two features shape strategy here. There is no negative marking, so every one of the 200 questions should carry an answer. And the prelims is purely a screening stage: your prelims marks do not carry into the final merit list. Clearing it at a comfortable margin is all that is required, and marks beyond that buy nothing.

The 90 out of 300 qualifying figure is the floor, not the real bar. The actual cutoff for being called to the mains is set by the number of vacancies and the number of candidates, and it sits well above the qualifying minimum in most cycles.

## Mains examination: two different exams

This is where the groups separate.

| | Group 2 (interview posts) | Group 2A (non-interview posts) |
|---|---|---|
| Paper I | Tamil eligibility test, SSLC standard, descriptive, 100 marks | Tamil eligibility test, SSLC standard, descriptive, 100 marks |
| Paper I role | Qualifying only | Qualifying only |
| Paper II | General Studies, degree standard, DESCRIPTIVE, 300 marks | General Studies with reasoning and language, OBJECTIVE, 300 marks |
| Interview | Yes | No |
| Merit built from | Paper II and interview | Paper II alone |

Paper I is a mandatory Tamil eligibility paper at SSLC standard, and it is qualifying. Its 100 marks do not enter your merit position. A candidate who writes a strong Paper I and a weak Paper II gains nothing from the former.

Paper II carries the entire weight. For Group 2A that means a 300-mark objective paper where accuracy and coverage decide your rank. For Group 2 it means a 300-mark descriptive paper, written by hand, under time pressure, on general studies at degree standard.

Candidates who have only ever written objective exams underestimate what the Group 2 descriptive mains asks, so it is worth being concrete about the difference.

In an objective paper, recognising the right option among four is enough. In a descriptive paper you have to produce the content from memory, structure it into a coherent answer, and do it inside a word and time budget across many questions. Knowing a topic well enough to identify the correct statement about it does not mean you can write 150 useful words on it in six minutes.

The preparation that works is writing practice, not more reading. | Stages | Prelims, descriptive mains, interview | Prelims, mains, interview for Group 2 only | Single written exam |
| Competition | Highest, very few posts | High | Very high volume, but lower bar |

Group 1 is the state's senior administrative entry with a small number of posts and the longest process. Group 4 needs no degree and is decided on a single paper, which draws enormous numbers of applicants. Group 2 and 2A sit between them, and for a graduate they usually offer the best ratio of posts to realistic competition.

Preparing only for the objective format when applying to Group 2. The mains for the interview posts is descriptive, and that has to be trained for separately.

Treating the prelims as a scoring exam. Its marks do not count, so effort spent pushing a comfortable prelims score higher is effort taken from the mains, which is where selection happens.

Leaving questions blank in the prelims. With no negative marking, an unanswered question is a certain zero against a free chance at a mark.

Neglecting the Tamil eligibility paper. It is qualifying, so it adds nothing to your rank, but failing it ends the attempt regardless of how well Paper II went.

Ignoring the Tamil Nadu component of general studies. It is the most predictable and most repeated part of the syllabus, and candidates who focus only on national-level material give away marks that are available to anyone willing to study the state material.

Choosing the language paper on hearsay rather than on strength. Candidates pick General Tamil or General English based on which one other aspirants claim is scored more generously, and then lose marks in a section they could have secured by choosing the language they actually read and write better.

Waiting for the notification to start. The notification appeared on 11 August 2026 and the prelims falls on 1 November 2026, which leaves about twelve weeks between the two, and applications closed on 9 September within that span. Candidates who begin after the advertisement appears are preparing a year-long syllabus in a quarter of that time.

Pay for Group 2 and 2A posts is set under the Tamil Nadu Revised Pay Rules, 2017, with each post assigned a level in the state pay matrix.

Most of the commonly recruited posts, including Sub Registrar, Deputy Commercial Tax Officer, Probation Officer and Senior Revenue Inspector, sit at Pay Level 18, with a basic pay of Rs 37,200 and a range running to about Rs 1,17,600. In-hand pay at entry, after dearness allowance, house rent allowance and city compensatory allowance and before deductions, works out in the region of Rs 45,000 to Rs 55,000 a month depending on the posting.

Levels vary by post within the group, so confirm the figure for the specific post in the notification rather than assuming a single number covers all of them. Alongside pay, the posts carry the leave, medical and pension entitlements of Tamil Nadu government service.

## Eligibility

On education, a graduate degree from a recognised university is the requirement for both groups. Some posts carry additional subject or qualification requirements set out in the notification.

On age, the limits are set per cycle and vary by category and by post, with relaxation for backward classes, Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes as per Tamil Nadu rules. Check the notification for the reckoning date and the exact bands.

On language, the mains includes a mandatory Tamil eligibility paper at SSLC standard, so a working command of written Tamil is a practical requirement of the process even where the general studies preparation is done in English.

## How to apply

Applications are filed on tnpsc.gov.in.

1. Complete the TNPSC One Time Registration if you have not already. This profile is reused across TNPSC examinations and is valid for five years.
2. Watch for the notification, expected on 11 August 2026, and read the advertisement for the post list, vacancy count and eligibility for this cycle.
3. Apply online within the window, selecting your group and post preferences and your language paper option.
4. Upload photograph and signature in the specified format.
5. Pay the examination fee online, noting the fee concessions available to candidates who have not exhausted their free-chance entitlement under TNPSC rules.
6. Submit, save the application, and download the hall ticket when it is released ahead of the 1 November 2026 prelims.

## Documents you will need

1. Class 10 certificate as proof of date of birth.
2. Degree certificate and mark sheets.
3. Community certificate for candidates claiming reservation.
4. Nativity or residence documents where required.
5. Certificates for any additional claims such as differently abled status, ex-servicemen status, destitute widow status, or sports.
6. Photograph, signature, and a photo identity document matching the application.

Working back from a 1 November 2026 prelims, the preparation window is what remains between today and that date.

Add aptitude practice in shorter, regular sessions rather than long blocks, and take full-length prelims mocks under the three-hour clock from about six weeks out, training yourself to answer all 200 questions given there is no penalty.

changes.content:
IBPS declared the CRP PO/MT-XVI preliminary result on 10 September 2026. The prelims was held on 22 and 23 August 2026 across multiple shifts, and candidates who cleared both the sectional and the overall cut-offs, which IBPS sets separately for each category, go to the mains on 4 October 2026.

If you qualified, the mains is the immediate concern and it is the stage that decides the merit: prelims marks do not carry forward. Applications for this cycle opened on 1 July and closed on 26 July 2026 after an extension from the original 21 July deadline, and the next notification is usually issued around the middle of the following year.

## Where this recruitment stands

| Stage | Date |
|---|---|
| Notification | 30 June 2026 |
| Application window | 1 July to 26 July 2026, closed |
| Prelims | 22 and 23 August 2026 |
| Prelims result | 10 September 2026 |
| Mains | 4 October 2026 |
| Interview | After the mains result |
| Provisional allotment | Following the interview stage |

The gap between prelims and mains is roughly six weeks. That is the window most candidates plan badly, and how to use it is covered below.

## How many vacancies, and why sources disagree

IBPS revised the vacancy count upward after the notification, and published figures now contradict each other. Several outlets report the revised total as 7,565. At least one reports 7,365. Both describe their figure as the post-revision number, so this is not a case of one source being out of date.

The authority is IBPS at ibps.in, and the revised figure appears in the corrigendum rather than in the original notification PDF.

What is not in dispute is the scale. This is a recruitment of well over seven thousand officer-grade posts, which makes it one of the largest single officer intakes in Indian banking, and considerably larger than the previous cycle.

If you saw a figure of 4,500 on this page previously, that was wrong and has been removed.

## Call letter and the eight days before prelims

IBPS releases the prelims call letter on its portal, downloaded with the registration number and password created during the application. It carries the centre address, date, shift and reporting time.

Download it now if you have not. With the exam on 22 and 23 August, there is no margin left for a login problem or a printing failure, and portal load rises sharply in the final days.

Check the shift on your call letter carefully. IBPS runs multiple shifts per day across both dates, and candidates have arrived for the wrong session.

Carry the printed call letter, one original photo identity document and the photocopy IBPS specifies in its instructions. Aadhaar, voter ID, PAN card, passport and driving licence are the usual accepted forms. Reporting time is well ahead of the exam start and gates close before the paper begins.

For the remaining days, do not learn new topics. Sit two or three full mocks under real conditions, revise your error log, and protect your sleep schedule for the shift you have been allotted. Cramming new material in the final week reliably costs more in accuracy than it adds in coverage.

## Prelims exam pattern

| Section | Questions | Marks | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| English Language | 30 | 30 | 20 min |
| Quantitative Aptitude | 35 | 35 | 20 min |
| Reasoning Ability | 35 | 35 | 20 min |
| Total | 100 | 100 | 60 min |

Each section is separately timed at 20 minutes and closes when that time expires. Negative marking is 0.25 marks per wrong answer.

Prelims is a screening stage. Its marks do not carry into the final merit list. IBPS calls forward a multiple of the vacancy count for the mains, so clearing prelims comfortably is the only objective. Marks above the cutoff are worth nothing.

Twenty minutes for 35 quantitative questions is roughly 34 seconds each, which means selection matters more than raw speed. Identify the questions you can finish quickly, complete them, and leave the long calculation-heavy ones untouched rather than half-solved. With 0.25 negative marking, a blank costs nothing and a low-confidence guess costs a quarter mark.

## Mains on 4 October and where the result is decided

The mains is the stage that determines your rank, alongside the interview.

It covers Reasoning and Computer Aptitude, General, Economy and Banking Awareness, English Language and Data Analysis and Interpretation, and it includes a descriptive English paper testing letter and essay writing, which is evaluated separately from the objective sections.

The descriptive paper is the part candidates most often neglect, on the reasoning that it carries fewer marks than the objective sections. That reasoning is wrong in a competitive field, because the descriptive paper is where a prepared candidate can separate themselves cheaply. Letter and essay formats are predictable, and practising a handful of each in timed conditions is a small investment against a stage most people walk into cold.

Banking and economy awareness deserves the bulk of your six weeks. It converts preparation into marks more directly than any other section, it has no time-pressure problem, and the scope is the six months of banking and financial news preceding the exam. Start compiling now rather than in the final fortnight.

## The interview stage, and why IBPS PO differs from IBPS Clerk

IBPS PO includes an interview. IBPS Clerk does not, and that single difference changes the shape of the whole recruitment.

The interview is conducted by participating banks in coordination with IBPS and nodal banks. Final merit combines the mains score and the interview score in a defined ratio, with the mains carrying the larger weight. A candidate with a moderate mains performance can recover ground at interview, and a strong written candidate can lose it there.

Because of that, the mains result is not the end of the process in the way the clerical mains is. Candidates who clear the mains and then wait passively for the interview date lose an opportunity, since interview preparation covering banking awareness, current affairs, your own academic and work background, and basic composure under questioning is entirely learnable.

## Eligibility

A bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognised university, held on the date specified in the notification. A degree expected later does not qualify.

The age band is 20 to 30 years against the cutoff date in the notification, with relaxation of 5 years for SC and ST, 3 years for OBC in the non-creamy layer, and 10 years for candidates with benchmark disabilities in the unreserved category, plus provisions for ex-servicemen and other notified categories.

Computer literacy is required, satisfied by a certificate or diploma in computer operations or by having studied computing as a subject at school or degree level.

Unlike IBPS Clerk, there is no single-state application restriction and no local language requirement binding you to one state. IBPS PO is an all-India recruitment, and you may be allotted to a participating bank anywhere in the country. Candidates who want to remain in a specific state should understand that IBPS PO does not offer that, and IBPS Clerk does.

## Salary and career progression

A Probationary Officer joins in Junior Management Grade Scale I, the entry officer grade in public sector banking. Basic pay at entry sits well above the clerical scale, and gross monthly pay is considerably higher once dearness allowance, house rent allowance, city compensatory allowance and other benefits are added. House rent allowance is banded by city classification, so the same post pays noticeably more in a metro.

Beyond pay, the post carries pension under the National Pension System, medical benefits, leave fare concession, and staff loan rates on housing and vehicle borrowing well below commercial rates. Those loan terms are worth a substantial amount across a career and are routinely underweighted when candidates compare a banking offer against a private sector alternative.

Progression runs from Scale I through Scale II and Scale III into senior and top management grades. A Probationary Officer who performs well and clears internal promotion processes reaches Scale II considerably faster than a clerical entrant reaching officer grade, which is the structural reason IBPS PO attracts heavier competition than IBPS Clerk despite the harder selection.

The probation period involves rotation across branch functions, and postings in the early years are frequently rural or semi-urban. Candidates expecting a metro posting from year one are usually disappointed.

## How IBPS PO compares with IBPS Clerk and SBI PO

| | IBPS PO | IBPS Clerk | SBI PO |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cadre | Officer, Scale I | Clerical | Officer |
| Interview | Yes | None | Yes, with group exercise |
| Allotment | All India | One state, binding | All India |
| Local language | Not binding | Required for chosen state | Applies at allotment |
| Employer | Participating banks | Participating banks | State Bank of India only |
| Descriptive paper | Yes, in mains | No | Yes |

The written syllabus across all three overlaps heavily, so preparing for one prepares you substantially for the others, and sitting several in a year is normal. What differs is the endgame and the geography. IBPS Clerk binds you to one state and ends on the written paper. IBPS PO and SBI PO are all-India and add an interview.

If your priority is remaining in a particular state, IBPS Clerk is the exam that offers it. If your priority is officer grade and faster progression, IBPS PO is the larger opportunity, and this cycle is an unusually large one.

## Participating banks and how allotment works

IBPS conducts the common recruitment process on behalf of participating public sector banks. The list has changed across cycles as bank mergers consolidated the sector, so a list you find in older material may name banks that no longer exist independently.

You do not apply to a bank. You apply to the common process, and allotment to a specific bank happens after the interview stage based on your merit position, your preferences and the vacancies each bank has reported. Candidates who join expecting to have chosen their employer have misread the process.

Because this is an all-India recruitment, geographic allotment follows the bank's own posting policy rather than a state you selected. Early postings are frequently rural or semi-urban regardless of where you sat the exam, and the probation period involves rotation across branch functions to build a working knowledge of operations.

## Normalisation and the scores you will see

IBPS normalises scores across shifts, because prelims runs in multiple sessions of differing difficulty and the mains is conducted at scale. Normalisation adjusts raw marks so a candidate who sat a harder shift is not disadvantaged.

The practical consequence is that the score you calculate from a memory-based answer key will rarely match your published score, and comparing your raw performance against a friend who sat a different shift tells you very little. Candidates spend a great deal of energy on this comparison every cycle and it produces no useful information.

What is worth checking when scorecards are released is whether your recorded responses match what you remember marking. That is a discrepancy worth raising through the proper channel. A difference between your estimate and your normalised score is not.

## Mistakes that cost candidates this exam

Waiting for the prelims result before starting mains preparation. The gap is roughly six weeks and the result consumes part of it, so candidates who wait are effectively preparing for the deciding stage in a month.

Skipping the descriptive paper. It is the cheapest differentiation available in the mains because the formats are predictable and most candidates arrive unprepared.

Treating banking awareness as a final-fortnight subject. The scope is six months of banking and financial news, which cannot be compressed, and it is the section where preparation converts most reliably into marks.

Guessing to fill blanks in the prelims. With 0.25 negative marking, an unattempted question is strictly better than a low-confidence guess, and sectional timing means a rushed final thirty seconds is where those guesses cluster.

## NBEMS Recruitment 2026 to 53 Group A, B and C posts at New Delhi HQ

National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS), the autonomous body that conducts NEET PG, FMGE, and DNB exams, has opened direct recruitment for **53 permanent posts** across Group A, B, and C. Applications close on **20 July 2026** at natboard.edu.in. The written exam (CBT) was scheduled for 5 and 6 September 2026.

Postings are at NBEMS headquarters in New Delhi, a stable central government job with 7th CPC pay, NPS pension, CGHS medical, and standard central-service benefits. Application fee is ₹1,500 plus 18 percent GST (total ₹1,770); SC/ST/PwBD candidates are exempted.

The bulk of the vacancies (39 out of 53) are for Junior Assistant, so if you have a 12th pass with computer skills, this is worth applying for.

---

## Important dates

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Notification released | 19 June 2026 |
| **Online application opens** | **29 June 2026** |
| **Last date to apply** | **20 July 2026** |
| Admit card release | Mid-August 2026 (approximately) |
| **Written exam (CBT)** | **5 and 6 September 2026** |
| Skill test | Announced after CBT result |

Don't wait for the last day. The NBEMS payment gateway has historically been slow between 6 and 11 PM in the final 48 hours.

---

## Post-wise vacancy breakdown

| Post | Group | Vacancies | Pay Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deputy Director (Medical) | A | 2 | Level 11 |
| Junior Programmer | B | 1 | Level 7 |
| Junior Accountant | C | 4 | Level 4 |
| Stenographer | C | 7 | Level 7 |
| **Junior Assistant** | **C** | **39** | **Level 2** |
| **Total** | | **53** |: |

74 percent of the vacancies are Junior Assistant. If you're a 12th pass with typing skills, that's your target post.

---

## Who can apply: post-wise eligibility

### Deputy Director (Medical): 2 posts, Group A

- **Qualification**: Postgraduate Medical qualification per the Indian Medical Council Act 1956 (MD/MS/DNB or equivalent), with current medical council registration
- **Age**: Below 35 years as on closing date

### Junior Programmer: 1 post, Group B

- **Qualification**: B.Tech / BE in Computer Science or IT; or BCA; or a Degree in Computer Science / IT
- **Age**: Below 27 years

### Junior Accountant: 4 posts, Group C

- **Qualification**: Bachelor degree with Mathematics, Statistics, or Commerce as one of the subjects
- **Age**: Below 27 years

### Stenographer: 7 posts, Group C

- **Qualification**: Class 12 pass; Stenography skill at 80 wpm dictation and 30 wpm transcription on computer
- **Age**: 18 to 27 years

### Junior Assistant: 39 posts, Group C

- **Qualification**: Class 12 pass with computer proficiency (typing speed plus basic office applications)
- **Age**: Below 27 years

### Age relaxation for reserved categories

- SC / ST: +5 years
- OBC (Non-Creamy Layer): +3 years
- PwBD: +10 years additional

---

## What is the NBEMS salary?

All posts are 7th CPC. Approximate monthly figures at Delhi HRA rates:

| Post | Basic Pay | Estimated Gross/Month |
|---|---|---|
| Deputy Director (Medical) | ₹67,700+ (Level 11) | ₹1,00,000+ (with NPA) |
| Junior Programmer | ₹44,900 (Level 7) | ₹65,000 to ₹75,000 |
| Stenographer | ₹44,900 (Level 7) | ₹65,000 to ₹75,000 |
| Junior Accountant | ₹25,500 (Level 4) | ₹38,000 to ₹45,000 |
| Junior Assistant | ₹19,900 (Level 2) | ₹28,000 to ₹35,000 |

On top of the gross, all posts get:

- **NPS pension** (10 percent employee + 14 percent employer contribution)
- **CGHS medical cover** for self and dependents at any CGHS hospital
- **Leave Travel Concession**: free travel to home town every two years
- **Gratuity** on retirement
- Standard central government leave: casual, earned, medical, and maternity

Notice one thing about the Stenographer post, it's at Pay Level 7, same as Junior Programmer. That's an unusually high pay level for a stenographer role and reflects the specialised skill.

---

## What is the application fee?

- **General / OBC / EWS**: ₹1,500 + 18 percent GST = **₹1,770 total**
- **SC / ST / PwBD**: **Exempted**: no fee

Payment is online only via debit card, credit card, net banking, or UPI. There is no refund once you pay, even if you don't appear for the CBT.

---

## How to apply: step by step

1. Go to **natboard.edu.in** and open the **Recruitment** section
2. Click on the notice titled **Direct Recruitment for Group A, B and C posts in NBEMS 2026**
3. Register with a valid email ID and mobile number, both should stay active until the admit card release
4. Fill in personal, educational, and single-post preference details. You can apply for only one post
5. Upload scanned photo, signature, and category certificate (if applicable) in the specified size and format
6. Pay the fee online. Exempted candidates skip to the next step
7. Submit and download your acknowledgement page. Print a copy and keep it safe

No offline applications will be accepted. Corrections are usually not allowed once submitted, so verify every field before hitting submit.

---

## Selection process

Four stages. All are qualifying, but only the CBT and Skill Test count toward merit.

### Stage 1: Computer Based Test (200 marks)

Objective MCQ exam on 5 and 6 September 2026. Five sections:

| Section | Weightage |
|---|---|
| General Awareness | ~40 marks |
| English Language | ~40 marks |
| Numerical Ability | ~40 marks |
| Reasoning | ~40 marks |
| Post-specific Technical Knowledge | ~40 marks |

The technical section is where you separate yourself. General Awareness, English, and Reasoning tests are standard fare. The technical section for Junior Assistant tests computer proficiency; for Stenographer, it tests shorthand knowledge; for Junior Programmer, it tests coding and DBMS basics.

Negative marking will be specified in the admit card. Assume 1/4 mark deducted per wrong answer unless the admit card says otherwise.

### Stage 2: Skill / Knowledge Test (100 marks)

Post-specific applied test:

- **Stenographer**: Shorthand dictation at 80 wpm, transcription at 30 wpm on computer
- **Junior Programmer**: Coding test plus computer proficiency
- **Junior Assistant**: Typing test in Hindi or English, plus MS Office practical
- **Junior Accountant**: Accounting practical
- **Deputy Director (Medical)**: Descriptive medical knowledge paper or interview panel review

### Stage 3: Document Verification

Combined merit from CBT plus Skill Test decides who is called for DV at NBEMS HQ, New Delhi. Bring originals: 10th and 12th marksheets, degree, PG certificate (if applicable), category certificate, medical council registration (for Deputy Director), and one valid photo ID.

### Stage 4: Medical examination

Standard central government medical fitness check. Once cleared, appointment letters are issued for posting at NBEMS HQ, New Delhi.

---

## Should you apply?

Depends on your target post.

**Junior Assistant: apply if:**
- You are 12th pass and comfortable with typing (Hindi or English)
- You want a stable central government job in Delhi
- ₹28,000 to ₹35,000 gross with pension and CGHS is acceptable as a starting salary
- 39 vacancies is a decent number and gives a real chance

**Stenographer: apply if:**
- You already have shorthand skill at 80 wpm dictation and 30 wpm transcription
- Pay Level 7 (~₹65,000+ gross) is attractive for the effort involved

**Junior Programmer or Junior Accountant: apply if:**
- You match the specific qualification (Computer Science degree or Commerce/Math bachelor)
- You want a settled central government job over private sector churn

**Deputy Director (Medical): apply if:**
- You are a postgraduate medical qualifier with current registration
- You want an administrative role over active clinical practice

The ₹1,770 fee is not trivial for a 12th pass candidate, but the post is genuinely well-paid for its qualification level. If you clear the CBT, the skill test is straightforward for candidates who have prepared.

---

## Frequently asked questions

**When does NBEMS Recruitment 2026 close?**
20 July 2026. Applications submitted after midnight on this date will not be accepted.

**What is the salary of a Junior Assistant at NBEMS?**
₹19,900 basic (Level 2, 7th CPC). Estimated gross including DA and Delhi HRA is ₹28,000 to ₹35,000 per month, plus NPS pension and CGHS medical.

**What is the exam date for NBEMS Recruitment 2026?**
The Computer Based Test was scheduled for 5 and 6 September 2026. Admit cards release approximately 10 to 15 days before the exam.

**What is the application fee for NBEMS 2026?**
₹1,500 plus 18 percent GST, total ₹1,770. SC, ST, and PwBD candidates are exempted.

**Can I apply for more than one post at NBEMS?**
No. You can apply for only one post per candidate. Choose based on your qualification and age carefully.

**Is there negative marking in the NBEMS CBT?**
The exact marking scheme will be confirmed on the admit card. Assume 1/4 mark deducted per wrong answer as a working assumption.

**Where will I be posted if selected?**
All selected candidates are posted at NBEMS headquarters in New Delhi.

**Is NBEMS a central government job?**
NBEMS is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India. Employees get central government service benefits: NPS pension, CGHS medical, LTC, and gratuity.

---

## Quick links

- **Apply online**: [natboard.edu.in/recruitment](https://natboard.edu.in/recruitment)
- **NBEMS home**: [natboard.edu.in](https://natboard.edu.in)
- **Ministry of Health**: [mohfw.gov.in](https://www.mohfw.gov.in)

## NBEMS Recruitment 2026 to 53 Group A, B and C posts at New Delhi HQ

National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS), the autonomous body that conducts NEET PG, FMGE, and DNB exams, has opened direct recruitment for **53 permanent posts** across Group A, B, and C. Applications close on **20 July 2026** at natboard.edu.in. The written exam (CBT) is scheduled for **5 and 6 September 2026**.

Postings are at NBEMS headquarters in New Delhi, a stable central government job with 7th CPC pay, NPS pension, CGHS medical, and standard central-service benefits. Application fee is ₹1,500 plus 18 percent GST (total ₹1,770); SC/ST/PwBD candidates are exempted.

The bulk of the vacancies (39 out of 53) are for Junior Assistant, so if you have a 12th pass with computer skills, this is worth applying for.

---

## Important dates

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| Notification released | 19 June 2026 |
| **Online application opens** | **29 June 2026** |
| **Last date to apply** | **20 July 2026** |
| Admit card release | Mid-August 2026 (approximately) |
| **Written exam (CBT)** | **5 and 6 September 2026** |
| Skill test | Announced after CBT result |

Don't wait for the last day. The NBEMS payment gateway has historically been slow between 6 and 11 PM in the final 48 hours.

---

## Post-wise vacancy breakdown

| Post | Group | Vacancies | Pay Level |
|---|---|---|---|
| Deputy Director (Medical) | A | 2 | Level 11 |
| Junior Programmer | B | 1 | Level 7 |
| Junior Accountant | C | 4 | Level 4 |
| Stenographer | C | 7 | Level 7 |
| **Junior Assistant** | **C** | **39** | **Level 2** |
| **Total** | | **53** |: |

74 percent of the vacancies are Junior Assistant. If you're a 12th pass with typing skills, that's your target post.

---

## Who can apply: post-wise eligibility

### Deputy Director (Medical): 2 posts, Group A

- **Qualification**: Postgraduate Medical qualification per the Indian Medical Council Act 1956 (MD/MS/DNB or equivalent), with current medical council registration
- **Age**: Below 35 years as on closing date

### Junior Programmer: 1 post, Group B

- **Qualification**: B.Tech / BE in Computer Science or IT; or BCA; or a Degree in Computer Science / IT
- **Age**: Below 27 years

### Junior Accountant: 4 posts, Group C

- **Qualification**: Bachelor degree with Mathematics, Statistics, or Commerce as one of the subjects
- **Age**: Below 27 years

### Stenographer: 7 posts, Group C

- **Qualification**: Class 12 pass; Stenography skill at 80 wpm dictation and 30 wpm transcription on computer
- **Age**: 18 to 27 years

### Junior Assistant: 39 posts, Group C

- **Qualification**: Class 12 pass with computer proficiency (typing speed plus basic office applications)
- **Age**: Below 27 years

### Age relaxation for reserved categories

- SC / ST: +5 years
- OBC (Non-Creamy Layer): +3 years
- PwBD: +10 years additional

---

## What is the NBEMS salary?

All posts are 7th CPC. Approximate monthly figures at Delhi HRA rates:

| Post | Basic Pay | Estimated Gross/Month |
|---|---|---|
| Deputy Director (Medical) | ₹67,700+ (Level 11) | ₹1,00,000+ (with NPA) |
| Junior Programmer | ₹44,900 (Level 7) | ₹65,000 to ₹75,000 |
| Stenographer | ₹44,900 (Level 7) | ₹65,000 to ₹75,000 |
| Junior Accountant | ₹25,500 (Level 4) | ₹38,000 to ₹45,000 |
| Junior Assistant | ₹19,900 (Level 2) | ₹28,000 to ₹35,000 |

On top of the gross, all posts get:

- **NPS pension** (10 percent employee + 14 percent employer contribution)
- **CGHS medical cover** for self and dependents at any CGHS hospital
- **Leave Travel Concession**: free travel to home town every two years
- **Gratuity** on retirement
- Standard central government leave: casual, earned, medical, and maternity

Notice one thing about the Stenographer post, it's at Pay Level 7, same as Junior Programmer. That's an unusually high pay level for a stenographer role and reflects the specialised skill.

---

## What is the application fee?

- **General / OBC / EWS**: ₹1,500 + 18 percent GST = **₹1,770 total**
- **SC / ST / PwBD**: **Exempted**: no fee

Payment is online only via debit card, credit card, net banking, or UPI. There is no refund once you pay, even if you don't appear for the CBT.

---

## How to apply: step by step

1. Go to **natboard.edu.in** and open the **Recruitment** section
2. Click on the notice titled **Direct Recruitment for Group A, B and C posts in NBEMS 2026**
3. Register with a valid email ID and mobile number, both should stay active until the admit card release
4. Fill in personal, educational, and single-post preference details. You can apply for only one post
5. Upload scanned photo, signature, and category certificate (if applicable) in the specified size and format
6. Pay the fee online. Exempted candidates skip to the next step
7. Submit and download your acknowledgement page. Print a copy and keep it safe

No offline applications will be accepted. Corrections are usually not allowed once submitted, so verify every field before hitting submit.

---

## Selection process

Four stages. All are qualifying, but only the CBT and Skill Test count toward merit.

### Stage 1: Computer Based Test (200 marks)

Objective MCQ exam on 5 and 6 September 2026. Five sections:

| Section | Weightage |
|---|---|
| General Awareness | ~40 marks |
| English Language | ~40 marks |
| Numerical Ability | ~40 marks |
| Reasoning | ~40 marks |
| Post-specific Technical Knowledge | ~40 marks |

The technical section is where you separate yourself. General Awareness, English, and Reasoning tests are standard fare. The technical section for Junior Assistant tests computer proficiency; for Stenographer, it tests shorthand knowledge; for Junior Programmer, it tests coding and DBMS basics.

Negative marking will be specified in the admit card. Assume 1/4 mark deducted per wrong answer unless the admit card says otherwise.

### Stage 2: Skill / Knowledge Test (100 marks)

Post-specific applied test:

- **Stenographer**: Shorthand dictation at 80 wpm, transcription at 30 wpm on computer
- **Junior Programmer**: Coding test plus computer proficiency
- **Junior Assistant**: Typing test in Hindi or English, plus MS Office practical
- **Junior Accountant**: Accounting practical
- **Deputy Director (Medical)**: Descriptive medical knowledge paper or interview panel review

### Stage 3: Document Verification

Combined merit from CBT plus Skill Test decides who is called for DV at NBEMS HQ, New Delhi. Bring originals: 10th and 12th marksheets, degree, PG certificate (if applicable), category certificate, medical council registration (for Deputy Director), and one valid photo ID.

### Stage 4: Medical examination

Standard central government medical fitness check. Once cleared, appointment letters are issued for posting at NBEMS HQ, New Delhi.

---

## Should you apply?

Depends on your target post.

**Junior Assistant: apply if:**
- You are 12th pass and comfortable with typing (Hindi or English)
- You want a stable central government job in Delhi
- ₹28,000 to ₹35,000 gross with pension and CGHS is acceptable as a starting salary
- 39 vacancies is a decent number and gives a real chance

**Stenographer: apply if:**
- You already have shorthand skill at 80 wpm dictation and 30 wpm transcription
- Pay Level 7 (~₹65,000+ gross) is attractive for the effort involved

**Junior Programmer or Junior Accountant: apply if:**
- You match the specific qualification (Computer Science degree or Commerce/Math bachelor)
- You want a settled central government job over private sector churn

**Deputy Director (Medical): apply if:**
- You are a postgraduate medical qualifier with current registration
- You want an administrative role over active clinical practice

The ₹1,770 fee is not trivial for a 12th pass candidate, but the post is genuinely well-paid for its qualification level. If you clear the CBT, the skill test is straightforward for candidates who have prepared.

---

## Frequently asked questions

**When does NBEMS Recruitment 2026 close?**
20 July 2026. Applications submitted after midnight on this date will not be accepted.

**What is the salary of a Junior Assistant at NBEMS?**
₹19,900 basic (Level 2, 7th CPC). Estimated gross including DA and Delhi HRA is ₹28,000 to ₹35,000 per month, plus NPS pension and CGHS medical.

**What is the exam date for NBEMS Recruitment 2026?**
The Computer Based Test is scheduled for 5 and 6 September 2026. Admit cards release approximately 10 to 15 days before the exam.

**What is the application fee for NBEMS 2026?**
₹1,500 plus 18 percent GST, total ₹1,770. SC, ST, and PwBD candidates are exempted.

**Can I apply for more than one post at NBEMS?**
No. You can apply for only one post per candidate. Choose based on your qualification and age carefully.

**Is there negative marking in the NBEMS CBT?**
The exact marking scheme will be confirmed on the admit card. Assume 1/4 mark deducted per wrong answer as a working assumption.

**Where will I be posted if selected?**
All selected candidates are posted at NBEMS headquarters in New Delhi.

**Is NBEMS a central government job?**
NBEMS is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India. Employees get central government service benefits: NPS pension, CGHS medical, LTC, and gratuity.

---

## Quick links

- **Apply online**: [natboard.edu.in/recruitment](https://natboard.edu.in/recruitment)
- **NBEMS home**: [natboard.edu.in](https://natboard.edu.in)
- **Ministry of Health**: [mohfw.gov.in](https://www.mohfw.gov.in)
